When $v\in\ell^1\setminus c_{00}$, the continuous band and its disjoint complement have the same lattice-isometric structure, with the latter contained in the cube-restriction kernel.

Functional Analysis.title: The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
Functional Analysis.summary:
We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture.
  The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity.
  We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar.
  In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is an expository version with navigational aids, not intended for publication

Functional Analysis.title: The Bishop--Phelps--Bollobás Property for Extremally Disconnected Ranges
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathbb F$ be either $\mathbb R$ or $\mathbb C$, and let $L$ be a nonempty extremally disconnected compact Hausdorff space. We show that $(X,C(L,\mathbb F))$ has the Bishop--Phelps--Bollobás property with $η(\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^2/2$ for every Banach space $X$ over $\mathbb F$. For each fixed $L$ and either scalar field, this bound is optimal uniformly over $X$.
Functional Analysis.comment: 2nd version; the separability assumption on the domain is removed. The title is changed accordingly

Functional Analysis.title: Kac lemma on noncommutative probability spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove non-commutative Kac's formula for actions of countable groups. We replace the return time functions by suitable projections in von Neumann algebras. Moreover, we prove a generalised Kac's formula in the non-commutative setting which extends the allocation construction of Meyerovitch and Weiss and is motivated by the random Kac inequality of Aaronson.
Functional Analysis.comment: 19 pages; preliminary version. Comments are welcome

Functional Analysis.title: The linear scale in metric cotype for Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature
Functional Analysis.summary: We answer a question of Eskenazis, Mendel, and Naor by proving that the optimal universal scaling parameter in metric cotype $2$ for complete Alexandrov spaces of nonnegative curvature has order $n$. The upper bound follows from a dyadic application of the Lang--Schroeder inequality, and the lower bound follows from snowflake universality of $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb{R}^3)$.

Functional Analysis.title: Crossed-Heinz Inequalities
Functional Analysis.summary: For positive matrices $A,B$ and $p,q>0$, the second author (2009) asked whether the inequality \[ \|A^pB^q+B^pA^q\|\leq \|A^{p+q}+B^{p+q}\| \] holds for every unitarily invariant norm. Despite a series of papers addressing this question, as well as recent intensive computational and AI-assisted investigations by Matthew Colbrook (2026, \cite{Col}), the problem remains open. It is a striking example of how an elementary scalar statement can become extremely difficult to handle in the noncommutative setting. Some partial positive results are known. In this note, we provide one more: the crossed-Heinz inequality holds for two-by-two matrices. This result also leads to a new and elegant characterization of the singular values of two-by-two matrices. In arbitrary dimension, we turn to the special case $p=q=1$, obtaining a series of eigenvalue estimates for the anticommutator $AB+BA$.
Functional Analysis.comment: This paper has been accepted for publication in the Bulletin of the Australian Mathematical Society

Functional Analysis.title: Three Lipschitz functions on infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with no common point of Fréchet differentiability
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that on every infinite-dimensional real Hilbert space \(H\), there exist three real-valued Lipschitz functions with no common point of Fréchet differentiability. This gives a negative answer to a longstanding question of Lindenstrauss, Preiss, and Tišer. The proof is constructive and relies on elementary calculus and finite-dimensional linear algebra. Since every Lipschitz map from a Hilbert space into $\mathbb R^2$ has a point of Fréchet differentiability, the target dimension three is optimal.

Functional Analysis.title: Invariant subspaces for integration and differentiation on convex domains
Functional Analysis.summary: For a conformal map $g$ of the unit disc $U$ onto any bounded convex domain $Ω$ we determine the invariant subspaces for the integration operator $T_gf = \int_0^zfg'$ on the Hardy space $H^p$, by means of a Fock space model. Under some additional regularity assumptions on $\partialΩ$ we also treat integration from a boundary point of $U$, and we determine the residual subspaces (those invariant subspaces on which the operator has empty spectrum) for the left inverse $D_gf = f'/g'$ of $T_g$ on the smooth disc algebra $A^\infty$. The latter result is new even for $Ω= U$.

Functional Analysis.title: Bilinear embedding for divergence-form operators with first-order terms and negative potentials
Functional Analysis.summary: This article establishes a bilinear embedding for second-order divergence-form operators with complex coefficients, characterized by the simultaneous presence of first-order terms and negative potentials. This work provides a further development of the theory initiated by Carbonaro and Dragičević for the homogeneous case, and recently extended by the second author in two papers where first-order terms and negative potentials were treated separately. We work in the general setting of arbitrary open subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ under Dirichlet, Neumann, or mixed boundary conditions. Our main contribution is the introduction of a unified notion of generalized $p$-ellipticity that extends all its predecessors and serves as the natural condition for the bilinear inequality. Methodologically, we overcome the rigidity of the Bellman-heat method on arbitrary open subsets by introducing a novel sequence-based approach that unifies and simplifies the previous techniques. As fundamental applications, we prove the boundedness of the $H^\infty$-calculus on $L^p$ and establish $L^p$-maximal regularity. Moreover, we show that this generalized $p$-ellipticity provides a sufficient condition for the $L^p$-contractivity and $L^p$-analyticity of the generated semigroup. Finally, we apply our theory to magnetic Schrödinger operators, characterizing the range of exponents $p$ for which the associated coefficient tuple satisfies the generalized $p$-ellipticity condition introduced here.
Functional Analysis.comment: In v2 we have slightly modified the presentation of our results and added the example of magnetic Schrödinger operators; 65 pages

Functional Analysis.title: The Gleason--Kahane--Zelazko theorem: a gentle introduction
Functional Analysis.summary: After some personal recollections of Jean-Pierre Kahane, this paper gives a gentle introduction to the Gleason-Kahane-Zelazko theorem. The theorem states that a normalised complex-linear functional on a unital complex Banach algebra is multiplicative whenever it does not vanish on invertible elements. Neither continuity of the functional nor commutativity of the algebra is assumed. We give a detailed account of three proofs: the original argument of Gleason and, independently, Kahane and Zelazko; the polynomial proof of Roitman and Sternfeld; and a proof by the author. We explain the complex analysis behind each: a special case of Hadamard's factorisation theorem, a polynomial argument using the fundamental theorem of algebra, and the Polya-Saxer theorem on zero-free entire functions and their derivatives. The elementary entire-function lemma needed for the first proof is proved in full; the Polya-Saxer theorem is used without proof. We give full details of the algebraic argument common to the three proofs, which deduces multiplicativity from the preservation of squares, including the non-commutative case. We then discuss applications and counterexamples, and present an extension to Ransford's generalised spectra using the Roitman--Sternfeld argument. We conclude with a brief guide to the more recent literature.
Functional Analysis.comment: 31 pages. Paper submitted to a volume in memory of Jean-Pierre Kahane

Functional Analysis.title: Invariance Preserving Conjugation and Linear Operators on the Hardy Space
Functional Analysis.summary: We study linear and anti-linear operators on the Hardy space $H^2$ in connection with the Beurling lattice. First, in contrast to Sarason's result \cite{S1}, we show that no non-zero anti-linear operator leaves every shift-invariant subspace invariant. Then we completely characterize the class of conjugations, isometries, and invertible linear operators preserving the shift-invariant subspace structure in terms of weighted composition operators induced by disk automorphisms--combined with the canonical conjugation, isometric multiplication, and invertible Toeplitz operators, respectively. We also establish the existence and non-existence of conjugations that map shift-invariant subspaces to coinvariant subspaces. Finally, we construct a counterexample that rules out an analogous factorization for bounded linear operators preserving shift-invariance of closed images.

Functional Analysis.title: Fast approximation and learning of binary classification tasks in o-minimal structures using ReLU neural networks
Functional Analysis.summary: We study binary classification tasks whose decision sets are given by definable sets in o-minimal expansions of the real field. Motivated by the cell decomposition theory of definable sets, we introduce traceable sets that isolate the analytical properties of definable sets used for fast approximation by ReLU neural networks. Under uniform bounds on the number of cells and a suitable extension assumption for the boundary functions, we prove that classifiers can be approximated in $L^p$ up to accuracy $\varepsilon>0$ by ReLU neural networks of size $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-p(n-1)/m})$, with depth independent of $\varepsilon$ and polynomially bounded weights. This establishes quantitative approximation rates for suitable definable collections in o-minimal structures using ReLU neural networks. Furthermore, the stated approximation rates are also derived for definable maps under similar geometric assumptions on their smoothness domains. We then obtain statistical learning rates for empirical risk minimization with hinge loss over the approximating ReLU neural network classes. For $N$ uniformly distributed samples, the predicted classifiers achieve expected misclassification error of order $N^{-m/(m+n-1)}$ up to an arbitrarily small polynomial loss.

Functional Analysis.title: Improvement of a Hardy-Littlewood inequality and applications to the boundedness of analytic paraproducts on mixed norm spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
Let $\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ denote the space of analytic functions in the unit disc $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$. For $0<p<\infty$ and $f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$, let $M_p^p(r,f)=\int_0^{2π}|f(re^{iθ})|^p \frac{dθ}{2π}$ and $M_\infty(r,f) = \sup_{|z|=r}|f(z)|$.
  For $0<p<q\leq \infty$, Hardy and Littlewood proved the prevalent inequality $$M_q(r,f)\le C(p,q)\frac{M_p(ρ,f)}{(ρ-r)^{\frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q}}}$$ for $0\leq r<ρ\leq 1$ and $f\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$.
  In this paper, we obtain an improvement of this well-known inequality which is employed to characterize the symbols $g\in\mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D})$ such that the analytic paraproducts $T_gf(z)=\int_0^z f(ζ)g'(ζ)\,dζ$, $S_gf(z)=\int_0^z f'(ζ)g(ζ)\,dζ$ and $M_gf(z)=f(z)g(z)$, are bounded between two different mixed-norm spaces $A^{p,q}_ω=\{ g\in \mathcal{H}(\mathbb{D}): \int_0^1 M_p^q(r,g) ω(r)\,dr<\infty\}$ induced by a radial doubling weight $ω$. En route to the proof of these characterizations, we consider an open Carleson measure problem posed by Luecking and we solve it in a meaningful particular case.

Functional Analysis.title: Analogs of crystalline measures in tube sets
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $μ$ be a pure point complex measure on a tube set $R^d+i F$, where $F$ is a compact convex subset in $R^d$, such that this tube set is the minimal closed convex tube set containing support of $μ$. Furthermore, assume that the Fourier transform $\hatμ$ (in the sense of distributions) is a measure. We determine conditions on the measure $μ$ under which the variation of the measure $\hatμ$ grows at least as $\exp\{2πH_F(t)\}$, as well as conditions under which this variation grows at most as $\exp\{2πH_F(t)\}$; here $H_F(t)$ is the support function of $F$.

Functional Analysis.title: Banach-Valued Carré du Champ Operators and Functional Gaussian Approximation
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop a projective-tensor-valued carré du champ for Malliavin-differentiable Banach-valued random elements and establish an associated integration-by-parts formula. The resulting dimension-free comparison principle bounds Gaussian approximation against twice Fréchet-differentiable test functions by the expected projective norm of a random covariance discrepancy. For processes on Skorokhod space equipped with the uniform norm, a smoothing argument converts this comparison into a quantitative bound in the bounded-Lipschitz metric, subject to explicit regularization errors. On Banach-valued Wiener chaos we express the carré du champ through contractions and obtain quantitative estimates in terms of contracted kernels. As a concrete application, we establish a quantitative functional Breuer--Major bound for the canonical polygonally interpolated partial-sum process, together with a corollary for the original Skorokhod step process. The estimate applies to the entire path in the uniform topology under explicit covariance conditions. We also record the trace-class specialization of the contraction bounds in Hilbert spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: The Strong Naor--Schechtman Convolution Inequality on the Product of Cyclic Groups
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we resolve the convolution inequality problem posed by Naor and Schechtman in \cite[Question 6.1]{N-S2016} (see also \cite{Na2016}). More precisely, we establish the following strong convolution inequality on products of finite cyclic groups: For each $1\leq p<\infty$ there exists $c_{p}>0$ such that for every $n$, $m\in \mathbb{N}$ the following holds \[ \begin{split} &\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x+\varepsilon)-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}}f(x-\varepsilon)\right|^{p}\\ \leq& c^{p}_{p}\sum_{\varepsilon\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}\sum_{x\in \Z}\left|\varepsilon_{j}\left[E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x+e_{j})-E_{\{1,\cdots,n\}\setminus\{j\}}f(x-e_{j})\right]\right|^{p}, \end{split} \] $E_{A}f(x)=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\sum_{δ\in \{-1,1\}^{n}}f\left(x+\sum_{j\in A}δ_{j}e_{j}\right)$ for every $A\subseteq \{1,\cdots,n\}$. The growth order we obtain here $c_{p}=O(p)$ as $p\to \infty$. For the endpoint $p=\infty$, we show by a counterexample that the strong convolution inequality fails for the $L_{\infty}$, and we prove that the appropriate endpoint for $p=\infty$ is the martingale $BMO$ space.

Functional Analysis.title: Weighted STSAFT-Modulation Spaces and Approximation by Phase-Adapted Neural Networks
Functional Analysis.summary: We develop a transform-adapted approximation framework for shallow neural networks based on the short-time special affine Fourier transform (STSAFT). Replacing the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) in the definition of classical modulation spaces, we work with weighted STSAFT-modulation spaces, building on the existing SAFT-associated modulation-space framework, and use their chirp correspondence with classical weighted modulation spaces through the chirp factorization of the SAFT kernel. We construct an associated neural dictionary and establish an $N$-term Sobolev approximation bound of order $N^{-1/2}$ on bounded one-dimensional domains. A global approximation theorem is also obtained when the spatial translation parameter ranges over the whole real line; a compact-support argument explains why an unrestricted global conclusion cannot in general be inferred from a bounded translation range. For a fixed-scale chirp family $f_κ(x)=e^{iπκx^2}u(x)$, we combine the global estimate with a phase analysis to obtain the stronger phase-dependent upper-bound factor $\langleλ\rangle^n\langleκ-λ\rangle^{n+3/2-1/r}.$ For each fixed nonzero Schwartz envelope, matching the dictionary phase reduces the growth of this specified upper bound from order $|κ|^{n+3/2-1/r}$ to order $|κ|^n$, while preserving the $N^{-1/2}$ rate. The associated mismatch scale is stated as a comparison of upper bounds, not as a threshold for the optimal approximation error. Four numerical experiments examine model comparison, error decay with dictionary size, phase mismatch, and the obstruction caused by restricted translations. We discuss the effective number of fitted output coefficients, including the rank loss of the sine branch at zero phase, and distinguish the numerical diagnostics from the theoretical best-approximation estimates.

Functional Analysis.title: Convolution on quantum tori I: Sharp Young inequalities and endpoint Sobolev embeddings
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce a convolution of noncommutative tori. The construction is the preadjoint of a trace-preserving cocycle-addition homomorphism. Its zero-parameter case is the function--operator semi-convolution. We prove both mixed $L_{1}$--$L_\infty$ inequalities and various Young inequalities with the optimal constant one, including their limiting cases. The endpoint bounds also yield submajorization and convolution estimates in fully symmetric spaces. As applications, we establish, for every integer $k\geq1$ and $1\leq p\leq\infty$, $W_{p}^{k}(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})\hookrightarrow B_{\infty,\infty}^{k-\frac{d}{p}}(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})$, and prove the critical embedding $W_{1}^{d}(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})\hookrightarrow L_\infty(\mathbb{T}_θ^{d})$. These results settle the two questions posed in Remark~6.8 of Xiong, Xu and Yin \cite{XiongXuYin}.

Functional Analysis.title: The Triangular Abrikosov Constant and the Thomas--Fermi $Γ$-Limit of Rotating Bose--Einstein Condensates
Functional Analysis.summary:
We resolve the Abrikosov coefficient conjecture for rapidly rotating two-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensates within the variational framework of $Γ$-convergence. For a harmonic trap, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the rescaled Gross--Pitaevskii energy functionals in the fast-rotation regime, through weak $L^2$ convergence of the rescaled densities, and identify the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with $b_\triangle$, the Abrikosov ratio associated with the triangular vortex lattice. The limiting Thomas--Fermi functional determines the first correction to the minimum energy and the macroscopic density of almost minimizers. For the auxiliary rescaled model and its lowest-Landau-level restriction, we also compute a strictly positive limiting $L^2$ distance between minimizing densities and the Thomas--Fermi profile.
  The identification of the effective interaction coefficient $β_*$ with the triangular Abrikosov ratio $b_\triangle$ relies on the sharp Gaussian-minorant theorem established in a recent OpenAI preprint~\cite[Theorem~1.2]{Atomic}. A Fourier representation of the quartic energy and a weighted Poisson identity yield a lower bound for arbitrary magnetic-periodic lowest-Landau-level states. The sign conditions on the minorant and its Fourier transform give the bound, while the lattice contact conditions identify its coefficient with $b_\triangle$. Cutoff and magnetic projection transfer this estimate to local holomorphic states without boundary conditions or periodicity assumptions. Consequently, the free-cell coefficients converge to $b_\triangle$ with error $O(L^{-1/5})$ on squares of side length $L$.

Functional Analysis.title: Noncommutative Rational Positivstellensätze with Operator Coefficients
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish a convex Positivstellensatz for noncommutative rational functions with bounded operator coefficients. A hermitian operator-valued rational function that is positive semidefinite on a matrix convex set described by a linear pencil admits a positivity certificate consisting of rational hermitian squares and a completely positive term involving the defining linear pencil. The certificate comes with an explicit complexity bound independent of the dimension of the coefficient Hilbert space. As a consequence, we solve the operator-valued noncommutative rational analog of Hilbert's 17th problem: every positive semidefinite operator-valued noncommutative rational function is a sum of hermitian squares, and even a single hermitian square when the coefficient Hilbert space is infinite-dimensional. In contrast, the corresponding commutative statement fails for infinite-dimensional operator coefficients.

Functional Analysis.title: Composition operators on weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Given a function $\varphi:\D\to \D$ holomorphic in a neighborhood of the closed unit disk $\overline{\D}$, we study the matrix \[ A_\varphi = \big(\widehat{\varphi^n}(k)\big)_{n,k\geq 0}. \] We obtain a complete characterization of those $\varphi$ for which $A_\varphi$ acts boundedly from $\ell^p$ to $\ell^q$, $p,q\in [1,\infty]$. These results can be reformulated in terms of composition operators, providing a complete description of the symbols $\varphi$ holomorphic in a neighbourhood of $\overline{\D}$ that induce a bounded composition operator $C_\varphi:f\mapsto f\circ \varphi$ between two possibly different Beurling--Sobolev spaces. In particular, we prove that $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\ell_a^p$ for some $p\neq 2$ if and only if it is bounded on every $\ell_a^p$, $p\in [1,\infty]$, if and only if $\varphi$ satisfies an analytic condition at the points of $\overline{\D}$ where it touches the unit circle. Extensions to weighted Beurling--Sobolev spaces are also provided.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Open Inextensible Filaments in Planar Stokes Flow: Well-Posedness, Endpoint Asymptotics, and Straightening
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study an inextensible open filament with free ends in a planar Stokes fluid. The system reduces to a third-order nonlocal curvature equation coupled to an elliptic equation for the tension. We prove local well-posedness for nearly critical initial data in supported Sobolev spaces $\widetilde H^s$, $-1/2<s\le0$, satisfying the arc-chord condition. For positive times, we prove improved Sobolev regularity and derive a $d^{3/2}$-type expansion at each free end using Wiener--Hopf factorization, where $d$ denotes the distance to that endpoint. We further prove global existence and exponential convergence to a straight filament for sufficiently small initial data and for finite-energy initial data satisfying $E(0)<π^2/4$. The finite-energy result follows from an energy identity and a geometric estimate relating the bending energy to the arc-chord constant. More generally, any finite-time breakdown must be accompanied by loss of the arc-chord condition, while every global solution either converges exponentially to a straight filament or has arc-chord constants tending to zero along a sequence of times tending to infinity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp nonuniqueness for the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the Vlasov--Navier--Stokes system on $\mathbb T^d\times\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$. For smooth data and every $p<2$, $q<\infty$, we construct infinitely many weak solutions with velocity in $L^p_tL^\infty\cap L^1_tW^{1,q}$ and bounded, renormalized distribution function; infinitely many of them violate the energy inequality. For smooth velocity data, weak solutions with velocity in $L^2_tL^\infty$ are unique, so the result is sharp at the endpoint of the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin scale. The fluid carries the nonuniqueness, through the convex integration scheme of Cheskidov and Luo, and the kinetic equation is solved exactly. The main new difficulty is the memory of the particles: the kinetic state at time $t$ depends on the whole past of the velocity, so a modification on a short interval changes the system at all later times. We overcome it by a causal gluing, carried out from left to right in time, which re-solves the system on every interval of regularity. This yields wild solutions that are strong outside a closed set of times of arbitrarily small Hausdorff dimension. A causal mollification extends the construction to rough data, including every finite-energy velocity datum in dimensions two and three; in two dimensions the energy class is thus exactly the borderline of uniqueness. Finally, in three dimensions we construct Leray solutions satisfying the strong energy inequality and show that they are strong outside a closed set of times of vanishing $\mathcal H^{1/2}$ measure.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Multiplicity of Positive Solutions for Singular Anisotropic Elliptic Equations with Variable Exponents
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study anisotropic elliptic Dirichlet problems with variable exponents, singular nonlinearities, and subcritical superlinear reactions. Our contribution is a direct variational construction that combines Nehari geometry and fibering maps without requiring global differentiability of the singular energy, and the result establishes the existence of two positive weak solutions for sufficiently small \(λ\), distinguished by their energy signs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We analyze resonance for partially dissipative systems, $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, where $A$ generates a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. {Resonance is} the phenomenon whereby a bounded, time-periodic $f$ yields an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, several other resonance notions, introduced here, may occur.
  Classically, {$T$-periodic solvability} is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and demonstrate how the growth rate of~$||(A-iωI)^{-1}||_H$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$. For super-polynomial growth, that gap can be infinite. We demonstrate this phenomenon and its equivalence to the existence of smooth resonant forces.
  The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Maxwell's equations with thin wires in critical scaling
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We derive effective equations for a situation in which electromagnetic waves hit an array of very thin wires. We study two cases, perfectly conducting wires and highly conducting wires, and investigate in both the critical scaling of the parameters. The electric field $E^η$ and the magnetic field $H^η$ satisfy the time-harmonic Maxwell equations, and the small parameter $η>0$ is the spacing of the wires. A non-critical scaling of the wires implies either that the wires have no effect or that the tangential component of the limiting electric field in the direction of the wires vanishes along the effective interface. In the critical scaling, we observe an interesting effect: The wires act as oscillators and there is a relation between the electric field in longitudinal direction and the jump of the magnetic field in transversal direction involving second derivatives of a flux quantity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Thresholds of the Polya Szego inequality for the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish three surprising features of the Polya Szego principle for the full signed energy of the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian. First, the energy doesn't not decrease under rearrangement for all admissible functions. Second, the sharp threshold for Polarization and Schwarz rearrangements are different. Third, for Steiner rearrangement, the threshold in 1 dimension and N dimensions is not the same. Additionally the dimension doesn't appear in the formula.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Full range of infinite point blow-up exponents for the critical generalized KdV equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For the quintic, mass critical generalized Korteweg-de Vries equation, for any $ν\in (\frac{1}{2}, 1)$, we prove the existence of solutions in the energy space that blow up in finite time $T>0$ with the blow-up rate $\|\partial_x u(t)\|_{L^2} \sim (T-t)^{-ν}$ (infinite point blow-up). These solutions are constructed arbitrarily close to the family of solitons and correspond to the concentration of a soliton traveling at $+\infty$ in space as $t\uparrow T$. This complements the previous results obtained in the work of Martel, Merle, Raphaël in 2015 on infinite point exotic blow-up, which were valid under the technical restriction $ν>\frac {11}{13}$. The value $ν=\frac 12$ corresponds to a critical case to be treated elsewhere. At the technical level, we implement a modification of the virial-energy functional, to allow all $ν> \frac 12$ and simplify the proof of energy estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Slowly travelling infinite point blow-up for the critical generalized KdV equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the finite time blow up phenomenon for the quintic, mass critical gKdV equation. We prove the existence of a class of solutions $U$ with infinite point, finite time blow up behavior, at the particular blow up rate $$\|\partial_x U(t)\|_{L^2} \sim (T-t)^{-ν}\quad \text{as} \quad t \uparrow T,$$ where $ν= \frac 12$, $T$ is the blow up time and where the travel speed of the blow up bubble is logarithmic. Therefore, we call this behaviour slowly travelling infinite point blow up. The special blow up rate $ν=\frac 12$ is a threshold which separates finite and infinite point bubbling. In a previous work arXiv:2511.13538, the author constructed other infinite point blow up solutions for the continuum of rates $ν\in(\frac 12,1)$, using polynomial tails in the space variable and extending the results in arXiv:1209.2510, restricted to $ν> \frac{11}{13}$. However, that work suggested a change of the tail for the threshold case. In the present paper, we consider an exponentially decaying tail on the right in space. As in arXiv:2511.13538, the initial data can be taken arbitrarily close to the ground state in $H^1$. From a technical perspective, in addition to the change of tail, we have to adapt the energy-virial functional to the presence of the exponential tail, by modifying a scaling term used to control the right-hand side of the blow up solution.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Guerra Interpolation and Optimal Transport: Kantorovich Bounds, Brenier Maps and the Replicon
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Since Guerra's work, mean-field spin glasses have been studied through Hamilton--Jacobi equations. Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation.
  After a linear change of variables the finite-$N$ pressure becomes an action $u$ with $\partial_t u = -A/2$ and $\partial_x u = -B$, where $B^2 \le A$, so $u$ is a classical subsolution of $\partial_t u+\frac12(\partial_x u)^2 \le 0$. Integrating along a straight segment gives Guerra's sum rule, and dropping its remainder makes $u(0,\cdot)$ and $u(t,\cdot)$ an admissible pair for the dual Kantorovich problem with quadratic cost. For the Curie--Weiss model and $t > 0$, $T_t(y) = y-t\tanh y$ is an optimal transport map from every source with finite first moment if and only if $t \le 1$, and the Kantorovich potentials are the limiting pressures. For the replica-symmetric Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, the cavity map is injective on the physical half-line and the curvature of its Brenier potential is the longitudinal eigenvalue, which exceeds the replicon eigenvalue $Λ_{\mathrm{AT}}$: transport of Dirac masses does not detect the de Almeida--Thouless line. The replicon appears along the $\mathcal{W}_2$ geodesic that splits a Dirac mass into two atoms, as the second variation of a second-order surrogate of the two-atom Parisi functional. From a Dirac initial datum, Guerra's $K$-step bound takes Hopf--Lax form, and the Parisi formula becomes a Hopf--Lax formula over atomic measures. With a $\mathcal{W}_1$-Lipschitz bound for its initial datum, proved by comparing Cole--Hopf layers, we let $K\to\infty$ and recover at Dirac data the Hopf--Lax form of the Parisi formula due to Mourrat and to Mourrat and Panchenko, with a rate for equal-mass approximations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The BCC Lattice Maximizes the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue among 3D Lattice Voronoi Cells
Analysis of PDEs.summary: It is shown that, among three-dimensional lattices of fixed covolume, the body-centered cubic lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of its Voronoi cell uniquely, up to orthogonal transformations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Normalized ground state solutions to the nonlinear Born--Infeld problem
Quantitative high-contrast homogenisation of composite media with highly anisotropic fibres
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This work concerns a non-uniformly elliptic second-order differential operator with periodic coefficients that describes a composite medium formed by a periodic array of highly anisotropic cylindrical fibres set in an isotropic matrix. The ratio of transverse to axial conductivity in the fibres is linked to the period of the coefficients through a `critical' high-contrast scaling, and the axial conductivity is allowed to vary along the fibres. As the period $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, ellipticity degenerates in the directions transverse to the fibres. We are concerned with the resolvent of this operator in the small-$\varepsilon$ limit. For fibres with constant axial conductivity, the two-scale limit of such problems was identified by Cherednichenko, Smyshlyaev and Zhikov (Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh: Section A Mathematics 136(1), 87--114 (2006)), and a full two-scale asymptotic expansion, with remainder estimates for smooth right-hand sides, was constructed by Cherednichenko (Asymptotic Analysis 49(1--2), 39--59 (2006)). In the non-constant axial conductivity setting, considered here, we approximate the resolvent in terms of the two-scale limit operator and prove that the error is order $\varepsilon$ in the operator norm, uniformly over right-hand sides in the unit ball of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$; we also obtain order-$\varepsilon$ estimates for the reciprocals of the spectral band functions. This work builds on results announced, without proof, for fibres with circular cross-section in Cooper and Kamotski (Direct and Inverse Problems with Applications: Extended Abstracts of the 2024 GAP Center Summer School, pp.~69--75, Birkhäuser (2026)).

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity of critical immersions for scale-invariant curvature energies in even dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For immersions of a closed $2h$-dimensional manifold $Σ$ into $\mathbb R^m$, we consider curvature energies that are invariant under ambient isometries and dilations, with the principal term $\int_Σ \big|\nabla^{(h-1)} \vec{\mathrm{I\!I}}\big|_g^2\,d\text{vol}_g$ and lower-order submanifold invariants. Following the four-dimensional approach developed in joint work with Bernard, Martino, and Rivière, we prove that every weak critical immersion in the natural Sobolev class $W^{h+1,2}$, whose induced metric and its inverse have $L^\infty$ coefficients, is real-analytic in harmonic coordinates. The proof combines geometric conservation laws, structural identities, and elliptic estimates with critical Sobolev coefficients to obtain Morrey decay and bootstrap to full regularity.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: v2: revised title and abstract; shortened exposition; corrected reference; added role of AI. v3: reorganized the introduction

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,\varphi(\ell/h)\,\barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)=f, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(t):=\frac{t\varphi'(t)}{\varphi(t)}\ge k+1+δ, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the dynamics of N classical particles interacting with a complex environment
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The interactions of a particle with its environment eventually lead to the damping of its motion. This phenomenom is well understood when considering a single particle exchanging energy with the environment. The situation is definitely more complex when many particles are considered: the energy dissipation mechanisms are not clear whenever particles create a common well in which they keep interacting.  In this framework, we identify the equilibrium solutions, that consist in clusters of particles at rest, and we establish their spectral stability. We show that the mean position/velocity pair is damped exponentially fast at the linearized level.  Coming back to the non linear problem, we can show, at least in some simplified cases, that the dissipation mechanisms also involve far slower rates, that explain the difficulty in observing the relaxation behavior on the individual trajectories.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<θ<π/2$, we consider \[
  σ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)
  =
  f(ξ)h^{p-1}\frac{ρ^{k+1}}{\varphi(ρ)},
  \qquad
  ρ=(h^2+|\nabla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $\nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nondegeneracy of the bubble for a fourth-order Liouville boundary problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish the nondegeneracy of the bubble for \[ Δ^2u=0\quad \text{in }\mathbb R^4_+,\qquad \partial_tu=0,\quad \partial_tΔu=e^{24π^2u} \quad \text{on }\partial\mathbb R^4_+. \] Using Fourier analysis, stereographic projection and a removable-singularity argument, we classify the weighted $L^2$ boundary kernel without assuming boundedness of the boundary solution. This determines the bounded half-space kernel. Both kernels are generated by dilation and tangential translations. We further obtain sharp estimates for the projected spherical inverse.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Inverse energy transfer for 2D Navier--Stokes near a self-similar vortex collapse
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove inverse energy transfer for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse, confirming the 1979 prediction of Novikov and Sedov. Nonlinear interactions transfer kinetic energy from high to low frequencies over a common time interval that shrinks to the collapse time as the viscosity tends to zero. We prove that the net nonlinear transfer over this interval converges to the same positive constant across an expanding range of frequency cutoffs, with quantitative error bounds uniform in the cutoff.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2\varphi(\ell/h)}{f}\, \barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)-h, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(s)=\frac{s\varphi'(s)}{\varphi(s)} \ge k+1+δ, \qquad s a_\varphi'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_μ}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cotθ, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<θ\leπ/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_μ\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<θ<π$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Simultaneous recovery of elastic and viscous coefficients in a Kelvin-Voigt equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the simultaneous recovery of a spatially dependent elastic coefficient and a time- and space-dependent viscosity coefficient in a scalar Kelvin-Voigt equation. We prove that the displacement-to-traction map over any fixed time interval uniquely determines both coefficients, provided that the Riemannian metric induced by the viscosity is simple at each time. In the velocity formulation, the elastic term gives rise to a Volterra memory term involving second-order spatial derivatives, with a corresponding memory contribution to the boundary traction. We first determine all normal derivatives of both coefficients at the boundary using highly oscillatory boundary data. We then construct exact parabolic exponential solutions in the presence of memory and determine the viscosity by boundary rigidity. With the viscosity determined, an approximate identity argument reduces recovery of the elastic coefficient to injectivity of the scalar geodesic ray transform. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate a regularized finite-dimensional reconstruction of both coefficients from finitely many moments of the displacement-to-traction map.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Optimal polynomial decay and nonlinear stabilization for an indirectly damped wave-MGT system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a conservative wave equation coupled to a dissipative Moore--Gibson--Thompson equation by a zero-order interaction that is symmetric in augmented variables. A general modal proposition relates the exact resolvent and semigroup asymptotic constants through an asymptotically unitary diagonalization. Its application to this system yields the optimal fourth-order resolvent estimate and the exact linear decay constants. These estimates lead to nonlinear stabilization from small regular initial data. On smooth bounded domains, a weighted composition estimate that accommodates a singular third derivative of the source at zero gives the optimal state rate $t^{-3/4}$ and energy rate $t^{-3/2}$ for power and logarithmic sources. In dimension three, the result includes $f(u)=|u|^q u$ with $3/2<q<2$ and $f(u)=|u|^{γ-2}u\log|u|$ with $7/2<γ<4$, within the source ranges of the companion general-source theory. Dimension-dependent extensions hold through dimension seven in the same data space, and in arbitrary dimension with higher regularity and a higher order of vanishing at zero. A lower-regularity graph-norm theorem and a conditional transfer theorem for general sources are also proved. Each nonlinear small-data decay exponent is optimal among uniform estimates with the stated dependence on the initial-data norm.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We determine the Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth. For the full water wave system, we derive an explicit instability index and rigorously classify its sign throughout the depth-vorticity plane. With gravitational acceleration and carrier wavenumber normalized to one, we identify a unique minimum depth $h_{\text{crit}}\approx1.36271$, below which Benjamin-Feir instability is absent for every vorticity. Above this depth, two vorticity thresholds delimit the unstable regime, outside of which the spectrum near the origin remains purely imaginary for all small Floquet exponents. In particular, at each fixed finite depth, constant vorticity of sufficiently large magnitude suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability. Moreover, any constant vorticity $γ\ge 2/\sqrt{3}$ suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability at every finite depth. The proof combines Hamiltonian spectral perturbation theory, symbolic computations, and formal verification in Rocq. Away from the transition set, our results rigorously confirm the stability criterion predicted by the nonlinear Schrödinger approximation of Thomas, Kharif, and Manna.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This paper builds on our previous work arXiv:2610.39000 and reuses several technical results established there. Companion Mathematica notebooks and Rocq proof scripts are available upon request

Analysis of PDEs.title: Well-posedness for Wright--Fisher SPDEs with measurable drift
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove weak existence and uniqueness in law of $[0,1]$-valued solutions for a class of scalar stochastic heat equations with measurable drifts $b : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$, driven by Wright--Fisher noise. The only assumptions we require on the drift are Borel-measurability, and the one-way inequalities $-Cu\leq b(u)\leq C(1-u)$ for some $C<\infty$, compatible with the necessary condition $b(1)\leq 0\leq b(0)$. These are vastly more general conditions than were previously available. Our proof relies on a stochastic duality between the solution of the stochastic heat equation, and a voting scheme running along the graph of a branching-coalescing particle system, generalising the class of drifts for which a dual process is available. Our results and their proof put the regularisation-by-noise result of Barnes, Mytnik and Sun, and its explanation, on a much more general footing.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 27 pages, v2 plugs a gap in the proof in v1

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
For the unforced Euler equations, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity within the class of axisymmetric flows without swirl, whose solution blows up in finite time. The initial vorticity belongs simultaneously to every Hölder space $C^α$, $α<1/3$. This is sharp given that global regularity is known when $α=1/3$ in the case of axisymmetric flows without swirl.
  Previous constructions by Shkoller \cite{Shk26}, Chen \cite{Chen26I,Chen26II}, and Shao--Wei--Zhang--Zhang \cite{SWZZ26} establish blow-up for each prescribed exponent $α$ in the same sharp range. Our construction achieves simultaneous membership in all these spaces. In addition, our construction is short.
  Our proof uses multiscale initial data, in the spirit of Kim--Jeong~\cite{KJ22}, Córdoba--Martínez-Zoroa--Zheng~\cite{CMZZ25}, and Bang--Cheskidov~\cite{BC26}. The blow-up mechanism is a forward cascade through successively smaller scales. A main difficulty in approaching the critical exponent $1/3$ is caused by large self-deformation. Our main idea to overcome this difficulty is to obtain a lower bound for strain at the stationary non-smooth point by using angular redistribution.
  A related outstanding open problem is to establish an unforced Euler blow-up from smooth data in the case of axisymmetric flows with swirl. A recent multiscale construction by OpenAI for the unforced Euler equations is, however, non-axisymmetric. Although we work in the no-swirl class, the axisymmetric multiscale mechanism developed here may offer a possible route toward the still-open problem of axisymmetric smooth blow-up.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stochastic inverse source problem in inhomogeneous media: far-field statistics
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is concerned with an inverse random source problem for the stochastic Helmholtz equation in a known three-dimensional inhomogeneous medium. The source is driven by spatial white noise. We seek to recover its mean and strength from the mean and cross-frequency covariance of the far-field pattern. For a smooth nontrapping wave speed, we use the spectral measure of the acoustic operator to relate the far-field data to the source statistics. Under a priori regularity bounds, this relation gives conditional stability for the source mean and the source strength. We derive explicit reconstruction formulas for both quantities and bound the errors due to frequency truncation and data perturbations. We also obtain mean-square error bounds for reconstructions from finitely many independent experiments. Numerical experiments illustrate the reconstruction accuracy and the effects of bandwidth and sample size.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stochastic Nonlocal Conservation Laws with Lévy Noise: Stability, BV Estimates, and Vanishing Viscosity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study one-dimensional stochastic nonlocal conservation laws with a convolution-type interaction field, driven by multiplicative Brownian noise and compensated Poisson random measures. The nonlocal operator modifies the classical entropy structure, while the jump noise produces nonlinear correction terms in the entropy inequality. We introduce a notion of stochastic entropy solution and establish an $L^1$-stability estimate using spatial doubling of variables and the Itô--Lévy formula. This yields uniqueness in the vanishing-viscosity class and, under additional bounds, a localized Cauchy estimate of order $\sqrt{\varepsilon+\varepsilon'}$. Existence is obtained by vanishing viscosity: we construct the viscous solutions through a Faedo--Galerkin scheme and derive viscosity-uniform $L^1$ and localized $BV$ estimates, which allow us to pass to the limit and obtain a spatially $BV$ stochastic entropy solution.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local well-posedness for the Novikov-Veselov equation at subcritical regularity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish local well-posedness of the Novikov--Veselov equation (NV), at every fixed value of the energy parameter, for initial data in $H^s(\mathbb{R}^2)$ in the entire subcritical Sobolev range $s>-1$. The argument is perturbative and does not invoke the integrable structure, instead adapting the strategy in our previous work on KdV (2026). An infinite normal-form expansion indexed by binary trees is combined with a gauge transform that bypasses the obstructions in the associate bilinear estimate, and the resulting gauged equation -- carrying nonlinear contributions of every order -- is closed by a contraction in a Fourier restriction space. The analytic engine is a family of frequency-restricted multilinear bounds, supported by a detailed description of the two-dimensional resonance geometry attached to (NV).

Analysis of PDEs.title: Least energy solutions for a quasilinear Neumann problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the existence of nonconstant weak solutions and the qualitative behavior of the least energy level for a class of quasilinear elliptic problems with Neumann boundary conditions of the form \[ -\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}(a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}u) +\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_s a_{ij}(x,u)D_{x_i}uD_{x_j}u =g(u)-λu \quad \text{in }Ω. \] Since the associated energy functional is neither of class $C^1$ nor locally Lipschitz, the classical Nehari manifold method cannot be applied directly. We therefore rely on variational techniques combined with nonsmooth critical point theory.
  For $λ>0$, we prove the existence of least energy solutions and show that, under suitable assumptions, they are nonconstant for large $λ$ and constant for sufficiently small $λ$. Moreover, the least energy level tends to $+\infty$ as $λ\to+\infty$.
  In the indefinite regime, a key ingredient is a spectral decomposition of $H^1(Ω)$ associated with the linear operator \[ \mathcal L_0u :=-\sum_{i,j=1}^N D_{x_j}\bigl(a_{ij}(x,0)D_{x_i}u\bigr). \]

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and regularity for a non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation with a confining potential
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the non-autonomous Born-Infeld equation $\operatorname{div}(Du/\sqrt{1-|Du|^2})-V(x)u+|u|^{p-2}u=0$ in $\mathbb R^N$, where $N\ge3$ and $2<p<2^*=2N/(N-2)$. For a $C^1$ potential satisfying $\inf V>0$, $V(x)\to\infty$ as $|x|\to\infty$, and $|x\cdot\nabla V(x)|\le C_DV(x)$ with $0\le C_D<p-2$, we prove the existence of a positive classical solution and infinitely many distinct nontrivial classical solutions. The argument combines the nonsmooth monotonicity trick with compactness induced by the confining potential. A Pohozaev-type identity yields uniform bounds for parameter-dependent critical points. A local minimization characterization identifies these critical points with weak solutions and establishes strict spacelikeness. Local Schauder estimates then give $C^{2,α}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ regularity. All the solutions belong to the natural energy space $H_V^1(\mathbb R^N)$ and satisfy $|Du|<1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Essential spectrum of singularly perturbed Dirac operators on bounded domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper self-adjoint Dirac operators on bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ with elliptic boundary conditions perturbed by singular $δ$-shell potentials supported on compact curves or surfaces are considered. While the unperturbed operator has purely discrete spectrum, it is shown that certain critical values of the interaction strengths lead to the appearance of essential spectrum. More precisely, each connected component of the interaction support, where the coupling constants have such critical values, produces in dimension two a point and in dimension three even a closed interval in the essential spectrum, where the size of the latter depends on the geometry and the coupling constants.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Surface-to-Volume Homogenization of NonLinear Steklov Eigencouples with NonHomogeneous Orlicz Growth in Perforated Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study normalized principal Steklov eigencouples on periodically perforated domains when both the bulk energy and the boundary normalization have general, possibly nonhomogeneous, Orlicz growth. The surface term on the hole boundaries carries the critical surface-to-volume scaling. For each fixed mass level, the constrained minima converge along the whole family, while selected minimizers, fluxes and Lagrange multipliers converge along subsequences to the corresponding objects of a homogenized problem. In the limit, the bulk operator is given by a convex cell problem, and the boundary term becomes a volume term weighted by the total surface density of the reference hole. The key tool is a strong approximation of the microscopic traces by cell averages, measured in the scaled surface modular.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish local existence and uniqueness of solutions for the ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system posed on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$ and initial conditions given by a nonzero constant magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$ and arbitrary divergence-free velocity $v_0\in H^s$, in the range $(n+1)/2<s\le n/2+1$. The proof uses a Lagrangian wave--Hodge reformulation and exploits an Alfvén null--structure hidden in the pressure forcing. This work builds on Zhang \cite{Zhang2026} and provides a bridge from the Lagrangian theory to the Eulerian Cauchy problem. In particular, the constructed solutions are induced by a bi-Lipschitz and volume-preserving map.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: AI and LLM use statement added

Analysis of PDEs.title: Michael-Simon inequality for anisotropic energies close to the area via multilinear Kakeya-type bounds
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
Given an anisotropic integrand $F:\text{Gr}_k(\mathbb{R}^n)\to(0,\infty)$, we can generalize the classical isotropic area by looking at the functional $$\mathcal{F}(Σ^k):=\int_ΣF(T_xΣ)\,d\mathcal{H}^k.$$ While a monotonicity formula is not available for critical points, when $k=2$ and $n=3$ we show that the Michael-Simon inequality holds if $F$ is close to $1$ (in $C^1$), meaning that $\mathcal{F}$ is close to the usual area.
  Our argument is partly based on some key ideas of Almgren, who proved this result in an unpublished manuscript, but we largely simplify his original proof by showing a new functional inequality for vector fields on the plane, which can be seen as a quantitative version of Alberti's rank-one theorem, and we also remove a convexity assumption on $F$.
  As another byproduct, we also show Michael-Simon for another class of integrands which includes the $\ell^p$ norms for $p\in(1,\infty)$. For a general $F$ satisfying the atomic condition, we also show that the validity of Michael-Simon is equivalent to compactness of rectifiable varifolds.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This is the version published on Ars Inveniendi Analytica: https://ars-ojs-utexas.tdl.org/ars/article/view/53

Analysis of PDEs.title: Traveling waves of NLS system arising in optical material without Galilean symmetry
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) system with cubic interactions arising in nonlinear optics, focusing on how the absence of Galilean symmetry affects solution dynamics. In the mass-critical case, we establish a new global existence result that contrasts with classical results. By exploiting the properties of traveling solitary waves, we obtain a condition on the initial data that relaxes the standard sharp assumptions. We also characterize the high-frequency limit of these traveling solitary waves as the frequency $ω$ tends to infinity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions to semilinear elliptic problems on the exterior of a unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the problem \begin{equation}\notag
  \begin{cases} - Δu &= λK(x) f(u) \hspace{.1cm} \mbox { in } B_1 ^c, \\ u(x)&=0 \hspace{1.5cm} \mbox { on } \partial B_1, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $λ$ is a positive parameter, $B_1^c:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:|x|>1\}$ is the exterior of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$, $K:B_1^c\rightarrow (0,\infty)$ is a $C^1$ radial function and $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a $C^1$ concave function which is sublinear at infinity such that $f(0)<0$. We establish the existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions for large values of parameter $λ$. Moreover, we prove certain qualitative properties of nonnegative radial solutions for a class of problems in dimension 2. In contrast to the case $n\geq3$, where positive solutions decay to zero at infinity, we prove that non negative solutions are positive, radially increasing with the limit existing at infinity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The periodic Wulff problem in two dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We characterize the minimizers of the anisotropic perimeter in the two-dimensional flat torus under an area constraint. We show that, as the prescribed area increases, global minimizers undergo two phase transitions, changing from a droplet (a rescaled Wulff shape) to a flat band wrapping around the torus in a preferred direction determined by the anisotropy (lamellar phase), and finally to a bubble (the complement of a reflected and rescaled Wulff shape). The transition thresholds are given explicitly in terms of the area and the lattice width of the Wulff shape. For certain non-symmetric surface tensions, the lamellar phase is absent altogether. Finally, we characterize the surface tensions for which further minimizers appear: this may happen only in the lamellar regime, and exactly when the Wulff shape has a corner whose normal cone contains, in its interior, a direction realizing the lattice width; in this case there are infinitely many minimizers.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Contractions of realizations and differential invariants of the algebra sl(2,C)
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we formalize a method for constructing limit transitions between local realizations of Lie algebras based on contractions of the corresponding algebras. In the complex holomorphic category, contractions of faithful realizations of the special linear algebra sl(2, C) to the complex three-dimensional Poincaré algebra and the Weyl-Heisenberg algebra are explicitly constructed. For the contraction of a generating realization of the algebra sl(2,C) to the algebra g_{3.4}^{-1}, differential invariants are constructed and a limit system of Newtonian type is found.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the sharp multi-bubble stability for fractional Hardy--Sobolev equations: a quantitative approach in low dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish sharp quantitative multi-bubble stability for nonnegative critical points of the fractional Hardy--Sobolev inequality in the low-dimensional regime $2s<N<6s-2t$. For functions whose energy is close to that of a finite superposition of bubbles, we prove that the Euler--Lagrange deficit controls linearly the distance, in the homogeneous fractional Sobolev norm, to the multi-bubble set, and we recover the precise bubble configuration. This yields quantitative rigidity under arbitrary finite weak interactions. The proof combines a localization scheme adapted to the Hardy weight, Kato--Ponce type weighted commutator estimates, a bubble-wise spectral gap inequality, and a sharp bubble-bubble interaction analysis. We also show that the linear rate is optimal by constructing a matching counterexample.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 45 pages. Added Appendix C on Bahri-Coron type projection and fixed minor errors. Comments welcome!

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Dirichlet Problem for Quaternionic $k$-Hessian Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Dirichlet problem for quaternionic $k$-Hessian equations on smooth bounded domains. For a smooth positive density $f(q,z)$ satisfying $f_z\ge0$, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth admissible solution whenever a smooth admissible subsolution with the prescribed boundary values exists. The proof extends the quaternionic Monge--Ampère subsolution method to $2\le k<n$ through boundary second derivative estimates. We also construct subsolutions on strictly quaternionic $(k-1)$-convex domains and characterize smooth solvability for constant boundary values.

Analysis of PDEs.title: One-bubble stability, reduced coefficients, and threshold compactness for the Escobar functional
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth compact manifold with nonempty boundary and coercive conformal energy. For $n\ge5$, in a conformal representative with $H_g=0$, we prove quantitative stability near a concentrating boundary bubble whose center stays away from the umbilic locus. The norm of the constrained gradient controls the distance to the standard bubble family with sharp exponent $1/2$, and the distance to the Lyapunov--Schmidt corrected family linearly. In the same one-bubble neighborhood, at energies at least the sharp hemisphere value $S_\ast$, the distance to the standard family is also controlled linearly. These estimates follow from the exact reduced quadratic coefficient and the scale-derivative expansion of the reduced functional. The same scale equation shows that sequences of critical points at $S_\ast$ can concentrate only at umbilic points. For $n\ge3$, a profile decomposition without a sign assumption gives Palais--Smale compactness between $S_\ast$ and the first mixed level $(S_\ast^{n-1}+Y^{n-1})^{1/(n-1)}$, where $Y=C^*_{\text{Esc}}(M,g)$, and this endpoint is sharp. Between $S_\ast$ and the two-bubble level, we characterize noncompact levels by the lower critical values. For $n\ge7$, we obtain the fourth-order reduced expansion at umbilic centers. Under local total umbilicity, we evaluate the correction exactly, determine the conformal weight of the reduced coefficient, and obtain the optimal algebraic comparison with the squared ambient Weyl norm.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 57 pages. Split from arXiv:2601.22665v2 (Part 2/3). Final part forthcoming. Comments welcome!

Analysis of PDEs.title: An abstract averaging method for quasilinear equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop an abstract averaging method for equations $Mx=\varepsilon N(x,\varepsilon)$ in Banach spaces. The method applies when the equation can be separated into an averaged compatibility condition and a nonlinear complementary problem, and it allows the principal operator $M$ to be genuinely nonlinear. We prove that every nondegenerate zero of the corresponding averaged equation generates, for all sufficiently small nonzero values of $\varepsilon$, a nearby solution. Under a suitable small Lipschitz condition this solution is locally unique, while in the differentiable case it belongs to a unique local $C^1$ branch. The framework contains the abstract linear Fredholm averaging theory as a special case, but also covers quasilinear problems for which the principal operator has no invertible linearization at the reference state. We also determine the leading asymptotic profile of the solutions. Applications are given to a vector $p$-Laplacian Duffing system and to a nonsmooth problem in a Hilbert space.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The $α$-Limit Problem: Convergence of a Linear Degenerate Interface Transmission Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the singular limit of a family of linear degenerate interface transmission problems arising from a regularization procedure in the newly proposed Two-Parameter Diffuse Domain Method (DDM2p). For $α>0$, the regularized problem admits a strictly convex variational formulation on $H^{1}(Ω)$. In the limit $α\to0$, the problem degenerates to a weakly coupled interface system with a nonstandard energy structure. To characterize the limit, we introduce a closed Hilbert subspace $\mathcal{H}\subset H^{1}(Ω)$, defined through an auxiliary Helmholtz problem on an annular subdomain $Ω_2\subset Ω$, and identify the limiting energy functional $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ on $\mathcal{H}$. We prove that the regularized energies $\mathcal{E}_α$ restricted to $\mathcal{H}$ $Γ$-converge to $\mathcal{E}_{0}$ in the strong $L^{2}(Ω)$ topology, using the standard framework. Consequently, minimizers of $\mathcal{E}_α$ converge to the unique minimizer of $\mathcal{E}_{0}$, which is shown to be equivalent to the solution of the limiting interface problem. We further prove a strong convergence $u_α\to u_{0}$ in $H^{1}(Ω)$ and establish a convergence rate of $O(α)$. Numerical experiments in one spatial dimension exhibit first-order convergence, suggesting that the proved $O(α)$ upper bound is sharp.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Co-rotating and traveling asymmetric vortex sheets for the planar Euler equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The aim of this paper is to construct co-rotating and traveling vortex sheet pairs with asymmetric configurations for the two-dimensional incompressible Euler equation. The vorticity of these solutions is concentrated on two small closed curves of different sizes, which carry vortex sheets of different circulations and either rotate uniformly about their centroid or translate with constant speed. The proof relies on the Birkhoff--Rott formulation of the problem and on the implicit function theorem at the point vortex pairs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Strong solutions to the Cahn--Hilliard--Darcy--Forchheimer system for incompressible two-phase flows with a soluble surfactant
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a diffuse-interface model for incompressible viscous two-phase flows with a soluble surfactant in a bounded porous medium in two or three dimensions. The resulting system consists of a Darcy--Forchheimer equation for the seepage velocity $\bm{u}$ coupled with two Cahn--Hilliard equations, one for the difference in volume fractions of the two fluids denoted by $φ$, and the other for the local concentration of the surfactant $ψ$. In the general scenario of non-constant coefficients and mobilities, we establish the existence of a local (resp. global) strong solution in three (resp. two) dimensions to the corresponding initial-boundary value problem with the no-flux boundary conditions for the phase-field variables and chemical potentials and a no-penetration condition for the velocity. In the case of constant coefficients in the Darcy--Forchheimer equation and constant mobilities in the Cahn--Hilliard equations, with a suitably large Forchheimer exponent, we establish the existence of a global strong solution in three dimensions. Furthermore, using the Łojasiewicz--Simon approach, we prove the global existence of a unique strong solution when the initial data are sufficiently close to a local energy minimizer of the free energy.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Convergence for the porous medium equation with combustion in higher dimensions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: \paper{Lou--Zhou}{JEMS}{2026} proved convergence and sharp threshold results for the one-dimensional porous medium equation with combustion reaction. In this paper, we extend these results to radially symmetric solutions with compactly supported initial data in higher dimensions. Under suitable assumptions on the reaction term, we first prove that every solution converges to a stationary solution. Based on this result, we obtain a spreading--transition--vanishing trichotomy with a sharp threshold. When $N=2$, transition solutions converge to the ignition temperature $θ$ locally uniformly in $\mathbb R^2$ as $t\to\infty$. When $N\ge3$, they converge to positive ground state solutions uniformly in $\mathbb R^N$ as $t\to\infty$. The main difficulty is to exclude $θ$ from the $ω$-limit set when $N\ge3$. We prove this by normalizing the difference $u-θ$, estimating the resulting limit with the heat kernel, and applying the radial zero number argument. In contrast, when $N=1$ or $N=2$, the $ω$-limit set of a transition solution is $\{θ\}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Geometric Partial Differential Equations of Hydrodynamic Type for Maps into F$_\text{man}$-Lie Groups
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop a geometric framework for partial differential equations of hydrodynamic type on maps from a two-dimensional manifold into an F$_\text{man}$-Lie group. Using the left-invariant structure and the Maurer-Cartan form, we reduce these equations to non-linear evolution systems on the underlying F$_\text{man}$-algebra, governed by its Lie bracket and commutative associative product. We investigate the role of Poisson subalgebras, establishing that flatness of the canonical connection forces two-step nilpotency and yields a linearized evolution equation upon quotienting by the center. Furthermore, we introduce the notion of a Poisson splitting and derive the corresponding tangential and transversal evolution equations. Under suitable reductivity assumptions, we show that their non-linear coupling is governed by the curvature of the canonical principal connection on the homogeneous space $G/H$. These results reveal the interplay between the algebraic structure of F$_\text{man}$-Lie groups and the geometric dynamics of hydrodynamic-type equations.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 22 pages, comments and questions are very welcome

Analysis of PDEs.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz capacity in one dimension
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity is proved on the line for every $p<1$ and all compact sets, including disconnected sets. For $-1<p<1$, equality holds exactly for a singleton summand or else two intervals, provided at least one capacity is positive. The proof couples equilibrium measures in increasing order.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 9 pages, 1 figure; ancillary file: mathematical audit (4 pages)

Analysis of PDEs.title: Dynamics of a single 3D vortex ring
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the axisymmetric Navier--Stokes flow without swirl originating from a circular vortex ring. For each fixed $s\in(0,1)$ and sufficiently large circulation Reynolds number $Γ/ν$, we prove that, on the time scale $t\lesssim T_{\rm adv}(Γ/ν)^{s}$, the vorticity $ω_θ$ is approximated by a traveling wave solution featuring a Gaussian-type core with scale $O(\sqrt{νt})$, whose off-axis distance remains constant and which continuously translates along the axial direction. In particular, the leading-order axial translation velocity is given by the Kelvin-Saffman formula. The proof relies on the approximation and Arnold energy framework of Gallay and Šverák \cite{GS2024}. We modify the weight used in \cite{GS2024} and estimate the relative-vorticity error to obtain favorable boundary dissipation at the symmetry axis and close the energy estimate.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary.
