Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $σ>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^σΔu_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{σ-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Liouville theorems for nonlinear polyharmonic equations with indefinite nonlinearities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a Liouville theorem for nonnegative bounded solutions of the indefinite polyharmonic equation $(-Δ)^m u=x_1u^p$ in $\mathbb R^n$, for all integers $m\ge2$, $n\ge1$, and all $p>1$. The main difficulty lies in extending the moving-plane method to a higher-order equation with a sign-changing coefficient. We first combine sublinear growth estimates with reflection arguments to establish the super-polyharmonic property in the right half-space, without prescribing boundary conditions on the separating hyperplane. We then use a doubling and rescaling argument to obtain relative first- and second-derivative estimates on strips, replacing the scalar Harnack estimates used in the second-order case. These estimates allow us to establish monotonicity in the $x_1$-direction within the right half-space $\{x_1>0\}$, and a cutoff argument then yields the desired nonexistence result.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Solutions concentrating on spheres for Hamiltonian elliptic systems with supercritical growth
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study positive solutions of the singularly perturbed Hamiltonian elliptic system \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -\varepsilon^2Δu+u=|v|^{q-2}v &\text{in }A,\\ -\varepsilon^2Δv+v=|u|^{p-2}u &\text{in }A,\\ u,v>0\text{ in }A,\qquad u=v=0 &\text{on }\partial A, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $A=\{x\in\mathbb R^{2m}:a<|x|<b\}$, $0<a<b$, $m\geq2$, and $2<p,q<2(m+1)/(m-1)$. We prove the existence of a family of solutions whose two components concentrate around the same $(m-1)$-dimensional sphere on the inner boundary as $\varepsilon\to0$. The two spheres of maxima are at distance $o(\varepsilon)$ from each other, and both components decay exponentially away from these spheres. The admissible range of $(p,q)$ includes critical and supercritical exponent pairs in dimension $2m$. The proof uses a reduction to a weighted system in dimension $m+1$. We establish foliated Schwarz symmetry of its ground states with a common axis via reduction by inversion and polarization. A uniform estimate on generalized Nehari fibers gives the upper energy bound. A half-space nonexistence result and the corresponding lower bound then determine the concentration location and the limiting profiles.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Finite-time blowup in a one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics model
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove finite-time blowup of both the velocity and magnetic field in a one-dimensional magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) model starting from smooth odd initial data. The construction combines the dynamical rescaling approach with weighted stability estimates. Both the velocity and magnetic field remain in $L^2$ before the blowup time.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A sharper observability for diffusion equations in $\mathbb R^N$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish that for any small constant $\varepsilon>0$, there exists a nontrivial equidistributed set (with an unbounded complement) such that the observability cost in the short time $(0,T)$ of diffusion equations over $\mathbb{R}^{N}$ can be improved to a sharper exponential form of $Ce^{\varepsilon/T}$, where $C>0$ is a constant independent of $T$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2108.04540

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for the Two-Dimensional Compressible Flow with General Bulk Viscosity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with general density-dependent bulk viscosity is established for large initial data allowing vacuum. Both the periodic problem and the Cauchy problem with far-field vacuum are considered under a common logarithmic derivative bound and growth condition on the viscosity primitive. A time-independent density upper bound and uniform low-order estimates are obtained in both domains. The admissible coefficients include every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with logarithmic gains. Exponential relaxation to the positive equilibrium is proved in the periodic setting. In the whole space, uniform relaxation toward vacuum and algebraic decay of the pressure, velocity gradient, material acceleration, and relative kinetic energy are established.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stability threshold of Couette flow for two-dimensional MHD equations on the infinite channel
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the stability threshold of the two-dimensional incompressible MHD equations near Couette flow and a constant horizontal magnetic field \((β,0)\) on \(\mathbb T\times\mathbb R\). For \(N>10\), \(0<ν,μ\le1\) and \(|β|\ge(ν+μ)/(3\sqrt{νμ})\), we prove global stability for initial perturbations of size \(δ_N\min\{ν,μ\}^{1/3}\) in \(H^N\), where \(δ_N>0\) is independent of \(ν,μ,β\). We also obtain enhanced dissipation of the nonzero horizontal modes on the time scale \(\min\{ν,μ\}^{-1/3}\), together with inviscid damping of the vertical components. The proof combines time-dependent Fourier multipliers with an energy correction constructed using the Alfvén oscillations. By combining the nonlinear terms arising from this correction, we obtain the cancellation needed to close the energy estimates at the $1/3$ scale.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness for an inverse problem of determining orders and coefficients for multi-term time-fractional diffusion equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper investigates a uniqueness problem for determining all fractional orders and their corresponding coefficients in multi-term time-fractional diffusion equations with Caputo derivatives in an abstract Hilbert space. The main result establishes that these parameters can be uniquely identified from a single scalar observation of the solution, of the form (u(t), phi), by comparing the solutions of two evolution equations governed by possibly different positive self-adjoint operators A and B. In contrast to existing results that rely on local space-time measurements and, in particular, may require the initial data to satisfy sign conditions and strong spatial regularity assumptions, our approach uses only the minimal assumption that a belongs to H, without imposing any sign or additional smoothness conditions on the initial value. The proof combines spectral representations of the solutions with a recursive asymptotic comparison method based on fundamental identities for the multinomial Mittag-Leffler function. This approach enables the successive identification of all fractional orders and their associated coefficients, even when the two equations involve different operators. Furthermore, the uniqueness argument extends to multi-term time-fractional wave equations with orders in the interval (1,2).

Analysis of PDEs.title: Effects of elasticity on the stability of viscoelastic boundary layers
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The elastic effect on the stability of boundary layers is studied for incompressible elastic fluids in the half-plane. It is known from [33] that if the deformation tensor matrix is nonsingular near the boundary, elasticity can prevent the formation of a boundary layer. In this paper, we prove stability properties when the deformation tensor degenerates. Our results are twofold: (1) when the first row of the deformation tensor has a non-degenerate projection onto a fixed direction, the initial-boundary value problem for the two-dimensional viscoelastic Prandtl boundary layer equations in the half-plane admits local well-posedness in Sobolev spaces, without any monotonicity condition on the velocity profile; (2) when the first row of the deformation tensor vanishes simultaneously at one point, the linearized Prandtl boundary layer system is ill-posed. The first result reveals the stabilizing effect of elasticity against the classical Prandtl instability. The second result shows that elastic effects cannot suppress the Prandtl-type instability associated with a non-degenerate critical point of the velocity profile.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative homogenization of $k$-Hessian equations in periodic media
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $1\leq k\leq n$, and let $u^\varepsilon$ and $u$ be the $k$-admissible solutions of $σ_k(D^2u^\varepsilon)=f(x,x/\varepsilon)$ and $σ_k(D^2u)=\overline f(x)$ on a bounded convex domain $Ω$, with the same Dirichlet data. Here, $f$ is uniformly positive and periodic in its second variable, and $\overline f(x)=\int_{\mathbb T^n}f(x,y)dy$. For $m=0,1$ and $0<α\leq1$, we prove $\|u^\varepsilon-u\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\leq C\varepsilon^{m+α}$ for all $0<\varepsilon\leq1$, provided that $u\in C^{m+2,α}(\overlineΩ)$ and $f\in C_x^{m,α}(\overlineΩ;C_y^{2,γ}(\mathbb T^n))$ for some $0<γ<1$. Periodic cell estimates give smooth dependence of the correctors on the background Hessian and the normalized density. The divergence-free property of the Newton tensor cancels the first macroscopic correction and yields the higher rate. Both exponents are optimal in general, already for $n=k=1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-Ljusternik--Schnirelman eigenvalues of the pure $p$-Laplacian exist
Analysis of PDEs.summary: An old and well-known open problem in the critical point theory asks whether, for some $p \neq 2$ and some bounded domain $Ω$, there exists a critical value of the $p$-Dirichlet energy $\|\nabla u\|_{p;Ω}^p$ over an $L^p(Ω)$-sphere in $W_0^{1,p}(Ω)$ lying outside of a Ljusternik--Schnirelman type sequence of critical values, the latter will be called LS eigenvalues of the $p$-Laplacian. In this work, we provide a positive answer by showing the existence of a non-LS eigenvalue when $p>2$ is sufficiently close to $2$ and $Ω$ is just a planar rectangle close to the square. The arguments pursue the observation that a simple eigenvalue of the Laplacian can be a common point for several branches of eigenvalues of the $p$-Laplacian as $p$ varies. Since LS eigenvalues are continuous with respect to $p$ and exhaust the whole spectrum when $p=2$, we deduce that at least one of the branches must contain non-LS eigenvalues.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 17 pages, 1 figure. Exposition revised, main theorem strengthened, its proof simplified, several remarks added, and bibliography updated. Accepted to Algebra i Analiz (St. Petersburg Mathematical Journal)

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative surface approximations for Maxwell scattering in nonlocal plasmonics
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish quantitative surface approximations for Maxwell scattering by a fixed collection of smooth, separated metallic particles described by the hard-wall generalized nonlocal optical response (GNOR) model. As the ratio $η$ of the reference screening length to the particle size tends to zero, regularized first-order and second-order transmission conditions approximate the electric far-field operator with errors $O(η^2)$ and $O(η^3)$, respectively. The estimates retain retardation and are uniform on compact subplasma frequency intervals with fixed positive damping and for a bounded dimensionless diffusion-to-pressure ratio. The proof combines exact elimination of the longitudinal field, a uniform weak bound for its boundary density, and smoothing by exterior observations. The same error orders hold for fields observed at a fixed positive distance from the particles. We also justify thin-coating representations on bounded tangential wave-number ranges for a planar interface and on fixed finite spherical angular subspaces. For each fixed quasistatic spherical multipole with a simple local pole, the first- and second-order models approximate the pole and its residue with errors $O(η^2)$ and $O(η^3)$, respectively.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large-time behavior of solutions to the 1D nematic liquid crystal with $γ>1$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the large-time behavior of solutions to the system modeling the compressible flow of nematic liquid crystals with a polytropic equation of state $P(ρ)=ρ^γ$ $(γ>1)$ in Lagrangian coordinates. In contrast to the isothermal case $γ=1$ treated in [4,5], we establish a new representation formula for the specific volume (Lemma 2.2) and, using Jensen's inequality, derive time-uniform estimates that yield global upper and lower bounds for the specific volume. A key ingredient is the reconstruction of the $D$--$Z$ structure for $γ>1$, which gives an exponential decay of $Z(t)$ and thus overcomes the difficulty caused by the power-type pressure.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Capacitary Hardy inequalities, Dirichlet boundary conditions, and the limit as $p\downarrow1$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We use nonlinear Dirichlet resolvents to prove Hardy inequalities with capacity-based and resolvent-based weights for $1<p<\infty$ on arbitrary open sets. On bounded Sobolev extension domains, integrability against either weight characterizes Sobolev functions satisfying homogeneous Dirichlet conditions on arbitrary closed subsets of the boundary. On bounded Lipschitz domains, the resolvent-based weight $\bm{W}_{D,p}$ converges locally in $L^1$ to the negative of Barozzi's interior variational mean curvature as $p\downarrow1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A singular minimizer of a uniformly convex Hessian-dependent functional
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct a smooth, uniformly convex Hessian-dependent energy functional, which admits a singular $C^{1,1}$ minimizer on $\mathbb{R}^5$ that is a two-homogeneous normalization of Cartan's five-dimensional cubic. Our construction relies on constructing a quadratic null Lagrangian for the Hessian that is suitably non-degenerate on the image of the Hessian for the candidate minimizer. This complements a partial regularity result previously obtained by the authors in this setting, and demonstrates that one cannot hope for a fourth-order version of classical second-order elliptic regularity theory à la De Giorgi-Nash-Moser.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On König's non-existence conjecture for the one-dimensional fractional Bianchi-Egnell inequality
Analysis of PDEs.summary: König conjectured that the sharp stability constant in the Bianchi-Egnell inequality for the one-dimensional fractional Sobolev inequality equals the local stability constant and that the associated quotient has no minimizer outside the set of optimizers of the fractional Sobolev inequality. We prove both assertions for $s<1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, with an explicitly computable threshold. The proof is based on a reinterpretation of the Frank-Lieb rigidity mechanism. Due to the lack of smooth variational structure of the Bianchi-Egnell quotient, we work with a refined limiting inequality of Beckner-Onofri-type on the circle with vanishing first-order moments, which we derive from Toeplitz determinants.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Flexibility of the isometric immersion system in arbitrary dimension and codimension and the energy scaling of prestrained thin films
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that, for a given $C^{r,β}$-regular Riemann metric posed on a $d$-dimensional domain, every short immersion into the Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^{d+k}$, can be uniformly approximated by exact isometric immersions of regularity $C^{1,α}$ for any $α<α_0=\min\{\frac{r+β}{2}, \frac{1}{1+d(d+1)/k}\}$. Our theorem recovers several previously known results as special cases. The novelty thereof lies in providing a unified flexibility statement for arbitrary dimensions $d$ and codimensions $k$, while also treating the so far uncharted range $k\in (1, \frac{d(d+1)}{2}-d+1)\setminus \{d\}$, where no corresponding general result was previously available. Our threshold flexibility exponent $α_0$ agrees with that previously obtained for the closely related Monge-Ampère system. As an application, we prove a new estimate in the quantitative immersability of thin prestrained films, setting the scaling exponent of the infimum of non-Euclidean energies in presence of an arbitrary prestrain metric, and in the limit of the film's vanishing thickness, at $\frac{4α_0}{α_0+1}$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 32 pages. The paper is now self-contained, whereas previously it relied on an external result concerning bounds for the normal frame which was partially erroneous, as it claimed that the constant in Corollary 2.7 was independent of the immersion. New version: we now added Example 2.8 providing an explicit construction showing that this constant cannot, in general, be independent of the immersion

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive solutions for a class of fractional Schrödinger equations in $\mathbb R$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study positive solutions $u\in H^s(\mathbb R)$ of the fractional Schrödinger equation $(-Δ)^su+λu=f(u)$ in $\mathbb R$, where $0<s<1$, $λ>0$, and $f$ is a general nonlinearity such that $f(t)/t$ is increasing. We prove that, under a single concavity condition on an auxiliary function, positive solutions are unique up to translations. The result applies to all positive solutions rather than only to ground states, and it allows $f'$ to be unbounded below at zero. It covers pure powers, sums of powers, logarithmic and saturable nonlinearities, for suitable ranges of the parameters. We further prove that every positive solution is nondegenerate, with the kernel of the linearized operator spanned by $u'$, and that it has Morse index one. If moreover $f(\sqrt h)/\sqrt h$ is concave, then for $1/2\le s<1$ a positive solution with prescribed $L^2$ norm is unique together with its Lagrange multiplier. The proofs are purely variational, using neither a continuation argument in $s$ nor the nondegeneracy of the linearized operator. Our method rests on the convexity of the action along an interpolation between symmetric decreasing functions that preserves a suitable integral quantity, and this convexity allows us to identify every positive solution as a constrained minimizer. For $1/2\le s<1$ we use the height interpolation of Delgadino, Yan and Yao, while for $0<s<1/2$ we introduce a new two-level interpolation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Optimal Interface Method: A Modelling Paradigm for Two-Body Contact Problems via Optimal Control and $Γ$-convergence
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This paper is concerned with the derivation of a model governing the equilibrium configuration of two linearly elastic bodies that may come into contact with each other. The contact zone, or coincidence set, is an \emph{a priori} unknown of the model, and the equilibrium configuration is governed by variational inequalities.
  We introduce a new modelling paradigm in which the contact interface between the two linearly elastic bodies under consideration is now regarded as the \emph{primary variable} of an optimal control problem whose states are the unique solutions of two \emph{independent} unilateral contact problems for which this very contact interface represents the obstacle itself. As a result, the free boundary emerges as the solution of a low-dimensional optimisation problem rather than as the active set of coupled variational inequalities.
  We establish the existence and uniqueness of optimal controls minimising the reduced cost functional arising from the modelling paradigm introduced beforehand, and we show that the family of marginal energy functionals associated with such model $Γ$-converges to the energy functional associated with the original variational inequalities as the positive \emph{cost parameter} $β$ in the reduced cost functional tends to zero. This $Γ$-convergence argument also yields a characterisation of the coincidence set of the limit problem in terms of the optimal interfaces.
  We further show that, after a suitable regularisation, the reduced cost functional is Gâteaux differentiable, and that its Gâteaux derivative can be explicitly computed \emph{without solving any adjoint system}.
  Finally, we corroborate the $Γ$-convergence result obtained beforehand with numerical experiments on a simplified and exactly solvable configuration.

Analysis of PDEs.title: From decay to regularity: the dispersion generalized Benjamin-Ono equation
Stokes flow in a wedge with a moving contact point: well-posedness with a fixed contact angle and Navier slip
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study 2D Stokes flow in a wedge-like region bounded by a solid substrate with Navier slip and by a free surface driven by surface tension. The two meet at a moving contact point with a fixed contact angle. This is the model of a moving contact line at scales below the slip length, in its simplest setting. The slip length is the only length scale, and nothing is prescribed at the contact point beyond the angle: no relaxation law for the angle, and no contact-point dissipation. Slip removes the paradox found by Huh and Scriven, the infinite dissipation at a contact line that moves without slip, but in this model a weaker singularity remains. We give, to our knowledge, the first rigorous characterisation of this singularity for solutions of the free-boundary problem near the stationary state. For small contact angles and small initial data satisfying two compatibility conditions, we prove local existence, uniqueness and Lipschitz dependence on the data. The compatibility conditions are the price of the fixed angle for solutions regular in time up to the initial time. Rather than hiding the singularity, the solution class carries it explicitly in corner expansions. The velocity is continuous up to the contact point. The pressure has a logarithmic singularity, the slip-regularised version of that of Huh and Scriven. Its coefficient is proportional to the contact-point velocity. The slope of the free boundary has a corresponding logarithmic correction, the slip-scale counterpart of the Cox-Voinov relation. The linearised problem combines terms of different scaling, which prevents a direct treatment by the Mellin transform. We solve it by a Lax-Milgram argument, and an auxiliary test function problem shows that the variational solution satisfies the equations. Explicit Mellin representations then yield the corner expansions, and the nonlinear problem is solved by a contraction argument.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A variational Free Boundary Ricci flow on Surfaces with Boundary
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a Ricci flow on a compact surface with boundary arising as the L2-gradient flow of the Liouville functional with its natural Neumann boundary condition. Geometrically, this boundary condition preserves the geodesic-curvature density H dσ. In the regime in which the total scalar curvature satisfies 0 < C_0 < 4π, a scale invariant normalised Liouville functional is monotone, and bounded below. In our first result, we use its dissipation to show that every compact blow-up limit is homothetically shrinking with constant positive scalar curvature. We then treat a rotationally symmetric disc with H_0 > 0 and C_0 > 0, in which case every noncompact limit is ruled out via singularity analysis and a noncollapsing theorem. Consequently, the normalised flow fully converges smoothly to the unique spherical cap determined by the initial area and the preserved boundary data, yielding our second result. Additionally, we also study the regime in which C0 is nonpositive. In this case standard PDE arguments prove full smooth convergence of the normalised flow towards a metric with constant nonpositive scalar curvature.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Finite-Time Blow-up for the Radial Mass-Critical Fractional Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that radial negative-energy strong solutions to the focusing mass-critical fractional nonlinear Schrödinger equation \[ i\partial_tu=(-Δ)^su-|u|^{4s/N}u, \quad N\ge2,\quad \frac12<s<1, \] blow up in finite time. This resolves the finite-time blow-up versus infinite-time grow-up alternative left open by Boulenger, Himmelsbach and Lenzmann in the mass-critical regime. The argument uses an exponentially localized virial field together with a dyadic resolvent estimate that transfers the resulting weighted Balakrishnan energy to localized fractional Sobolev norms. When $s\ge N/(2N-1)$, we extend the conclusion to radial $H^s$ solutions by establishing the integrated virial identity at energy regularity. As a consequence, mass-critical ground-state standing waves are strongly unstable by finite-time blow-up.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Multiplicity of Solutions for a Class of Logistic Problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The present paper investigates the existence and multiplicity of positive solutions to a class of degenerate logistic problems by combining the Nehari manifold {method} with nonlinear generalized Rayleigh quotients. The quotient associated with the Nehari constraint determines the threshold $λ_*$ at which the fibering structure and the Nehari manifold geometry emerge, while a second quotient identifies the zero-energy threshold $λ^*$ associated with the minimizing solution. Together with the threshold $\barλ$ for the existence of nontrivial solutions, these results yield the strict ordering \( 0<λ_*<\barλ<λ^*<λ_1(Ω)<λ_1(Ω_0), \) showing that the Nehari geometry becomes available before nontrivial solutions {exist} and that the zero-energy transition occurs only afterwards. In the variational range, we obtain a positive minimizing solution on $\mathcal N_λ^+$ and a second positive solution via the Mountain Pass Theorem. Complementary sub-supersolution and truncation arguments extend the multiplicity result to the remaining parameter range. We also establish the sign change of the minimizing energy, the blow-up and normalized asymptotic profile of the minimizing solutions as $λ\uparrowλ_1(Ω_0)$, and the convergence of the mountain-pass level $c_λ^m$ to zero as $λ\uparrowλ_1(Ω)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Orbital Stability and Instability of Slow and Fast Solitary Waves of gILW
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the solitary waves of the generalized Intermediate Long Wave equation (gILW), for a power-type nonlinearity of order $p\geq1$. Using concentration-compactness and symmetric rearrangement, we prove existence of suitable (even, strictly positive and radially decreasing) solitary waves of gILW for every $p\geq1$, and show that, as the depth parameter tends to infinity, they converge in the energy space and in $L^q$, $q\in[2,\infty]$, to the solitary waves of the generalized Benjamin-Ono equation (gBO), while, as the depth parameter tends to zero, after a suitable rescaling, they converge in $L^q$, $q\in[2,\infty]$, to the solitary waves of the generalized Korteweg-de Vries equation (gKdV). Our main results concern the orbital stability of slow and fast solitary waves of gILW, that is, of those for which the product $δc$ of the depth parameter and the velocity is small or large, respectively. For slow waves we obtain stability for $p=1,2,3$ and instability for $p\geq5$ (the same threshold as for gKdV), while for fast waves we obtain stability for $p=1$ and instability for $p\geq3$ (the same threshold as for gBO). In particular, for $p=3$ the stability of the solitary waves changes from one regime to the other. These results extend to $p>1$ the classical result of Albert, Bona and Henry for the Intermediate Long Wave equation ($p=1$). The proof proceeds by perturbation theory, transferring spectral information from gKdV and gBO to gILW through the convergence of the corresponding solitary-wave operators, and in particular avoids any use of an explicit formula for the solitary wave profile, none being available for $p>1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Lee-Huang-Yang Formula in the Hard-Core Simplified Approach to the Bose gas
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the hard-core variant of the Simplified Approach to the ground state of the dilute Bose gas. The hard-core potential has been the subject of renewed attention, and is physically relevant to realistic atomic Bose gases. The hard-core Simple Equation is an integro-differential equation, and we construct its solution via a monotone iteration scheme and prove existence and uniqueness (in a restricted sense) of the solution. The energy per particle $e$ and the density $ρ$ of the solution are shown to satisfy the Lee-Huang-Yang formula $e = 2πρ(1 + \frac{128}{15\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ))$ as $ρ\to 0$, and the condensate fraction $η$ predicted by the hard-core Simple Equation is shown to satisfy $η= 1 - \frac{8}{3\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ)$ as $ρ\to 0$, in agreement with Bogolyubov's theory. We thus extend results of Carlen, Jauslin, Lieb to the hard-core case.
  The hard-core equation is defined on its own terms, and the proofs proceed by approximating the hard-core potential with the soft-core potentials $m\,χ_{\{|x| \le 1\}}$ of increasing height $m$: at fixed energy, we establish the $L^1$ convergence of the corresponding solutions and the convergence of their densities at an $O(m^{-1/2})$ rate, and we show that the Lee-Huang-Yang expansions of the energy and of the condensate fraction for the soft-core equations hold with errors uniform in $m$, so that they survive the hard-core limit.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic analysis of Dirichlet problems in supercritically perforated domains via quantification by torsional rigidity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Dirichlet problem $-\mathrm{div}(A^{\varepsilon}\nabla u^{\varepsilon}) = f$ on varying open sets $D^{\varepsilon}$, with uniformly elliptic coefficients $A^{\varepsilon}$, in the regime where the solutions vanish in the limit for every source. For periodically perforated domains, this is the supercritical regime. We show that the torsional rigidity $T(D^{\varepsilon})$ is the natural normalization: up to a subsequence, $u^{\varepsilon}/T(D^{\varepsilon})$ converges weakly as measures to $kf$ for every continuous source $f$, where $k$ is a nonzero finite measure independent of $f$, which we call the effective measure. The key ingredient is an estimate comparing $u^{\varepsilon}$ with the product of $f$ and the torsion function, whose rate depends on the domains only through $T(D^{\varepsilon})$. We also show that this rate is optimal. No structural assumption on the perforation is needed, and the results hold for relaxed Dirichlet problems. Every nonzero finite measure arises as an effective measure, so the continuity of the source cannot be dropped in general. For rougher sources, we characterize the convergence by a condition on the domains alone, expressed through their torsion functions or, equivalently, their Poincaré constants. We also prove that the effective measure is local, satisfies optimal two-sided bounds and is monotone with respect to the coefficients, and we study the role of the antisymmetric parts of the coefficients.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Band edges of periodic Schrödinger operators are generically isolated and nondegenerate
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For periodic Schrödinger operators $H_V=-Δ+V$ with bounded real-valued potentials on $\mathbb R^d$ with $d\ge2$, we show that for generic potentials, each endpoint of every spectral gap is attained by a single Bloch band at only finitely many quasimomenta, and has a nondegenerate Hessian at every attaining point. This proves the Spectral Edge Conjecture for periodic Schrödinger operators.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: v2: 16 pages. Improved presentation and updated with a more detailed AI disclosure

Analysis of PDEs.title: A nonlocal transmission problem on a hybrid continuous-discrete domain
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a quadratic nonlocal variational problem on a hybrid domain formed by a compact interval and finitely many discrete points. The associated energy splits into continuous, discrete, and interface contributions. Our main estimate shows that the interface term yields a coercive coupling between the two phases and provides an equivalent hybrid norm. As a consequence, we prove existence and uniqueness of a minimizer for the corresponding variational problem and characterize it as the unique weak solution of the associated hybrid Euler--Lagrange system. The latter combines a nonlocal integral equation on the continuous component with a finite nonlocal algebraic system on the discrete nodes.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The present version has been substantially revised and extended, with additional theoretical developments, spectral investigations, and numerical experiments, and includes G. Rahman and K. Shaib Mohamed as co-authors

Analysis of PDEs.title: Long time decay for global solutions to the Navier-Stokes equations in Sobolev--Gevrey spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in the critical Sobolev--Gevrey space $\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}(\mathbb{R}^3)$, $a>0$. We first prove local well-posedness, together with a global existence criterion and a blow-up criterion for the maximal solution. Our main result is that every global solution $u\in C\big([0,+\infty),\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}(\mathbb{R}^3)\big)$ satisfies $\|u(t)\|_{\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}}\to0$ as $t\to+\infty$. The proof combines the classical decay of global solutions in $\dot{H}^{1/2}$ with an analyticity estimate for small data in $\dot{H}^{1/2}$ and Fourier-analytic product laws in Sobolev--Gevrey spaces. As consequences, we obtain the decay rate $\|u(t)\|_{\dot{H}^s}=o\big(t^{-\frac{s-1/2}{2}}\big)$ for every $s\ge\frac12$, and the stability of global solutions under small perturbations of the initial data in $\dot{H}^{1/2}_{a,1}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Finite time blow-up for the Willmore flow of symmetric figure-eight tori
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We show that the Willmore flow of symmetric figure-eight tori of revolution produces a finite time singularity, provided the initial energy is below $12π$. Our approach relies on the connection with elastic curves in the hyperbolic plane and a fine analysis of Palais--Smale sequences in the relevant energy regime.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantitative unique continuation for semiclassical Witten-Schrödinger type operator with low regular coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this note we study eigenfunctions localization of the semiclassical selfadjoint Schrödinger operator with low regular coefficients on domains of $\mathbb{R}^2$. We show a unique continuation result on the local decay of the eigenfunction: local supremum on open sets can't vanish faster than global supremum on these same sets times an exponential term that decrease in the semiclassical limit $h\to 0$ as $\exp(-c\log(1/h)/h)$ in the worst case. We deduce from this result a control on the eigenfunctions of the semiclassical Schrödinger operator on a $W^{2,\infty}$ compact Riemann surface with Lipschitz positive metric and with Robin boundary condition. This last part leads us to study the Schrödinger operator with a Witten Laplacian.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Linearization of nonlocal elasticity based on nonlocal gradients via Γ-convergence
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We provide a rigorous variational derivation of linear nonlocal elasticity from a general nonlinear elastic model based on nonlocal gradients. Under standard assumptions of nonlinear elasticity, we prove that the rescaled nonlinear energies Γ-converge, in the small-strain limit, to the corresponding quadratic linearized energy. The proof relies on a nonlocal geometric rigidity estimate and does not require any global upper growth condition on the stored-energy density.

Functional Analysis.title: Fourier Algebras of HLS Groupoids: Lifts, Amenability, and Spectrum
Functional Analysis.summary: We investigate the Fourier algebra of a certain class of groupoids, called the HLS groupoids, within Paterson's continuous framework for locally compact groupoids. We develop the basic harmonic analysis of HLS groupoids by obtaining concrete descriptions of their topology, representations, and Fourier algebra. We then study the restriction maps from the Fourier algebra $A(\mathcal{G})$ of an HLS groupoid $\mathcal{G}$ to the Fourier algebras of its isotropy subgroups, and construct explicit norm-preserving lifts for these restriction maps. As applications, we describe the norm of every element of $A(\mathcal{G})$ in terms of the norms of its restrictions to the isotropy subgroups. We prove an analogue of Leptin's theorem characterizing when $A(\mathcal{G})$ has a bounded approximate identity. We also show that the Gelfand spectrum of $A(\mathcal{G})$ is homeomorphic to $\mathcal{G}$. Finally, using abstract arguments that, unlike our methods for HLS groupoids, do not yield explicit constructions, we show that norm-preserving lifts exist and that the Gelfand spectrum of the Fourier algebra is homeomorphic to the groupoid for every étale groupoid. This generalizes Eymard's theorem and answers a question of Paterson for étale groupoids.

Functional Analysis.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schrödinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ norm and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.
Functional Analysis.comment: Version 3 fixes some English and notation issues, with the help from 'Gemini 4 Hydrogen Thinking". No changes for math contents

Functional Analysis.title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
Functional Analysis.summary: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
Functional Analysis.summary: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(π/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\fracπ{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $π/2$ and $π/4$, respectively.

Functional Analysis.title: Fourier--Stieltjes palettes on compact abelian groups
Functional Analysis.summary: Let G be an infinite compact abelian group and let K={0,a_1,a_2,...}, where a_1>a_2>...>0 and a_n\to 0. We construct a nonzero real, even, purely singular Rajchman measure whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in K. We then classify the compact abelian groups on which every positive null palette is exactly realizable in each of four classes: purely singular measures, atomless purely singular measures, strongly continuous purely singular measures, and Rajchman purely singular measures. Exact realization by a purely singular measure is always possible; atomless exact realization fails precisely for groups topologically isomorphic to \mathbb{T}\times F with F finite; and universal exact Rajchman realization is equivalent to \operatorname{Tor}(\widehat G) being infinite, or equivalently to G/G_0 being infinite. On \mathbb{T} we also give palette-dependent sufficient conditions for exact Rajchman realization. Finally, if U\subset\mathbb{C} is open and 0\in\overline U, we construct a continuous Rajchman measure with nonzero singular part whose Fourier--Stieltjes range is contained in U, assuming metrizability of G when 0\notin U. This gives a negative answer to an open-range absolute-continuity question of Ohrysko and Wojciechowski.

Functional Analysis.title: A description of the space with no separable quotient presented by OpenAI
Functional Analysis.summary: OpenAI recently presented a remarkable solution to the longstanding separable quotient problem in Banach space theory. The result establishes its independence from ZFC, relative to the consistency of ZFC with a measurable cardinal. Under the continuum hypothesis, the paper constructs a nonseparable Banach space $X$ with no separable infinite-dimensional quotient. The present paper offers an alternative exposition of the mechanism leading to $X$ and its properties. Our aim is to make the methods and results more accessible and to offer a clearer understanding of this exotic space.

Functional Analysis.title: Numerical range of finite perturbations of a 2-periodic weighted shift
Functional Analysis.summary: In this note, we consider a weighted shift operator of weight sequence which is a finite perturbation of a 2-periodic weighted shift. We characterise the equality of the closure of its numerical range and its essential numerical range. We end up with some applications and comments.

Functional Analysis.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$ be induced by a normal $τ$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},τ)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},τ;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},τ)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},τ)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.
Functional Analysis.comment: 32 pages, v2: Identified limit operator in Theorem 4.5 in the case of finite trace

Functional Analysis.title: Analytic Tools and Weighted Composition Operators on Paley--Wiener Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
We develop a scale-explicit analytic framework for operator-theoretic problems on the Paley--Wiener spaces $B_σ^p$, $σ>0$, throughout the full range $0<p\leq\infty$. Using localized Paley--Wiener packets, we obtain sharp-order point-evaluation estimates, quantitative separation of distinct point-evaluation functionals, sampling estimates, and Carleson measure characterizations.
  As a principal application, we develop a comprehensive theory of weighted composition operators $W_{ψ,\varphi}:B_σ^p\to B_τ^q$, $0<p,q\leq\infty$, $σ,τ>0$. Boundedness forces every nonconstant symbol to be affine with real slope. A sharp dichotomy appears: when $p\leq q$, the weight is governed by the residual bandwidth $τ-σ|a|$; when $q<p$, the weight must also supply the missing integrability, with exponent $pq/(p-q)$, and boundedness coincides with compactness. We also obtain compactness criteria and essential-norm estimates, characterize differences of weighted composition operators via a no-cancellation principle for distinct symbols, and determine the connected and path-connected components of the corresponding operator spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: The Local Embedding Problem for Hardy Spaces of Dirichlet Series
Functional Analysis.summary:
We solve the local embedding problem for Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series. For every $2<p<\infty$, the global $\mathscr{H}^p$-norm controls the $L^p$-norm of a Dirichlet polynomial on every unit interval of the line $\operatorname{Re}s=1/2$: $\sup_{θ\in\mathbb{R}}\int_θ^{θ+1}\left|P\left(\frac12+\mathrm{i}t\right)\right|^p\mathrm{d}t\le C_p\left\lVert P\right\rVert_{\mathscr{H}^p}^{p}$, where $C_p$ depends only on $p$, not on the interval or on the number and choice of primes occurring in $P$. The inequality was previously known at $p=2$ and, by taking powers, at every even exponent; it had been conjectured that these were the only positive cases above $2$. Together with the known counterexamples for $0<p<2$, our theorem shows that the embedding holds for finite $p$ exactly when $p\ge2$.
  The proof uses duality to control many critical-line evaluations together. A frequency decomposition isolates the contribution for which the relevant frequencies can nearly coincide. We estimate it by replacing the leading terms in the logarithms of the Euler factors with Gaussian variables, using the same variable for each prime at all evaluation points; the accumulated errors remain bounded. Comparison with a critical branching random walk and estimates for a finite-cyclic square function then give a bound independent of the number of prime variables. For $1\le p<\infty$, known equivalences also give the sharp range for the conformally invariant half-plane embedding, the reverse transfer of local Carleson-measure estimates, and boundedness of all characteristic-zero Gordon--Hedenmalm composition operators.
Functional Analysis.comment: This is an expository version and has been substantially revised with additional proof details and navigational aids. 110 pages

Functional Analysis.title: Generalized Limits of Finitely Additive Measures on Locally Compact Groups
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathscr{E}=\{E_α\}_{α\in I}$ be an increasing family of Borel subsets of a locally compact topological group $G$, indexed by a linearly ordered set $I$ with no greatest element. We call a nonnegative finitely additive $σ$-finite measure on the Borel $σ$-algebra of $G$ admissible if it takes finite values on the sets in $\mathscr{E}$ and these values are not bounded above. Every admissible measure $μ$ can be normalized to have total mass one by applying a generalized limit pointwise to the net of measures $\left\{B\mapsto\frac{μ(B\cap E_α)}{μ(E_α)}\right\}_{α\in I}$, defined for all sufficiently large $α$. We study invariant finitely additive measures obtained by normalizing admissible measures. We show that every invariant measure constructed in this way can be obtained by normalizing a measure of a special form. An example is given showing that not every measure of the type under consideration can be obtained by normalizing a countably additive measure. We obtain a generalization of the Yosida-Hewitt decomposition to finitely additive $σ$-finite measures.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp angle estimates for second order divergence operators
Functional Analysis.summary: This article is about the (minimal) sector containing the numerical range of the principal part of a linear second-order elliptic differential operator defined by a form on closed subspaces $V$ of the first-order Sobolev space $W^{1,2}(Ω)$ incorporating mixed boundary conditions. We relate the angle of sectoriality and the $\mathcal{H}^\infty$-angle of realizations of the elliptic operator to two reference angles: the optimal angle of the $L^2$-realization and the optimal angle of the coefficient function. We thereby consider the operator in several scales of Banach spaces: the Lebesgue space, the negative Sobolev space, and their interpolation scale. For the latter two types of spaces, we rely on recent results regarding the Kato square root property. We focus on minimal assumptions on geometry, and we consider both real and complex coefficients, in particular aiming at explicit estimates built on readily accessible problem data. New results include an explicit estimate for the angle of sectoriality for the elliptic operator on $L^p(Ω)$ with complex coefficients without any assumptions on geometry, which reduces to the known sharp angle for real coefficients, a new estimate on the angle of the sector containing the numerical range of a linear, continuous and coercive Hilbert space operator, and an estimate on the $\mathcal{H}^{\infty}$-angle for the elliptic operator on $L^p(Ω)$ with real coefficients.

Functional Analysis.title: Preserver Problems for Products of Operator Differences
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we investigate surjective maps $Φ:\mathscr B(H)\to\mathscr B(H)$ preserving various operator quantities associated with products of differences, namely, $$α\big((Φ(A)-Φ(B))Φ(C)\big) =α\big((A-B)C\big) \quad \text{for all}~ A,B,C\in\mathscr B(H),$$ where $α$ denotes one of the following: the numerical radius, maximal numerical range, minimum modulus, surjectivity modulus, reduced minimum modulus, or spectral radius. Under suitable assumptions, we establish structural characterizations of these maps and determine their possible forms.

Functional Analysis.title: Boundedness properties of bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we investigate mapping properties on Lebesgue spaces of bilinear Fourier integral operators (FIOs) with complex phases. Indeed, we provide for bilinear Fourier integral operators with complex phases boundedness theorems for the corresponding Seeger-Sogge-Stein orders, including the endpoint estimates. Our results extend the same boundedness property in the case of real-valued phases proved by Rodriguez-López, Rule, and Staubach, and provide the bilinear version for the linear one proved earlier by Ruzhansky for phases of positive type. Also, our Seeger-Sogge-Stein theorem for bilinear operators with complex phases cannot be directly deduced from its real counterpart. A new approach used in this article consists of providing directly the boundedness theorems on Lebesgue spaces without the use of the multilinear Fefferman-Stein interpolation theorem. For this, a maximal function theorem due to Bourgain is applied. As a byproduct, we also consider transference boundedness theorems of FIOs with complex phases from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to the torus $\mathbb{T}^n\equiv \mathbb{R}^n/\mathbb{Z}^n$ and then, we provide new criteria for the boundedness of Fourier integral operators on the torus with complex phases (Fourier series operators in the sense of Ruzhansky and Turunen).

Functional Analysis.title: Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality implies superreflexivity
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that if \(X\) is a Banach space for which Bourgain's vector-valued Stein inequality holds, then \(X\) is superreflexive. We also present an example of a superreflexive Banach space for which the vector-valued Stein property fails.

Functional Analysis.title: Entropy and frame measures for self-affine measures
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $M$ be a real expanding $d\times d$ matrix and let $\mathscr D=\{d_0,\ldots,d_{N-1}\}\subset\R^d$ consist of $N\ge2$ distinct vectors. We study the existence of frame measures for the self-affine probability measure $μ$ generated by the maps $S_i(x)=M^{-1}(x+d_i)$ with equal weights $1/N$. Extending the entropy obstruction for self-similar measures with a common scalar contraction, we prove that $μ$ admits no frame measure if the conditional entropy of the first symbol given the spatial point is positive. In particular, this holds whenever $N>|\det M|$, without assuming absolute continuity or imposing arithmetic conditions. When $M$ has integer entries, $\mathscr D\subset\Z^d$, and $N=|\det M|$, the measure $μ$ admits a frame measure if and only if $μ$ is normalized Lebesgue measure on its attractor.

Functional Analysis.title: Spectral and Isoperimetric Bounds on Flat Tori
Functional Analysis.summary:
We record several elementary relations between spectral and isoperimetric parameters of a flat torus $\mathbb{T}_Λ= \mathbb{R}^n/Λ$ and the covariance structure of a fundamental domain $K$ for the lattice $Λ\subset \mathbb{R}^n$. For every measurable fundamental domain $K$ and nonzero vector $ξ$ in the dual lattice $Λ^*$, we observe the sharp directional variance estimate \[ \left\langle \operatorname{Cov}_K ξ,ξ\right\rangle \geq \frac{1}{12}. \] This yields a lower bound on the torus spectral gap $λ_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ)$ (equivalently, the length of the shortest nonzero dual vector $λ_1(Λ^*)$) in terms of the maximal covariance of $K$: \[ λ_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ) = 4π^2 λ_1(Λ^*)^2 \geq \frac{π^2}{3\left\|\operatorname{Cov}_K\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}}. \] Analogous sharp results are obtained for the isoperimetric profile and the Cheeger constant $D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ)$ using an old argument of Hadwiger.
  In particular, when the Voronoi cell $K_Λ$ of a lattice with $\det Λ= 1$ is isotropic, the recent resolution of the Slicing Problem by Klartag and Lehec implies that \[ D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ),\quad λ_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_Λ),\quad λ_1(Λ^*) \geq c > 0, \] where $c > 0$ is a universal constant independent of dimension $n$; this may be thought of as a positive resolution of the Kannan--Lovász--Simonovits conjecture for all flat tori.
  While there are lattices $Λ$ and corresponding Voronoi cells $K = K_Λ$ for which no dimension-independent converse inequality to the spectral-gap bound above can hold, we show that under a certain sectional tiling hypothesis, this inequality is in fact an equivalence (up to numerical constants).
Functional Analysis.comment: 11 pages. Final version, to appear in GAFA Seminar Notes

Functional Analysis.title: Large deviations and the asymptotic geometry of Lorentz balls
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the uniform distribution on finite-dimensional Lorentz balls $B_{q,p}^n$ in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. We prove a Sanov-type large deviation principle for the empirical measures of the absolute coordinates of a random vector uniformly distributed on $n^{1/q}B_{q,p}^n$. The rate function is given by an entropy deficit under a weighted quantile constraint. We show that the entropy maximizer is unique and characterize its distribution function as the unique increasing solution of a nonlinear boundary-value problem. The limiting distribution has compact support, for which we obtain an explicit bound. These results establish the conjectured empirical limit of Kabluchko, Prochno and Sonnleitner [Journal of Functional Analysis, 288(1):110682, 2025] in the range $1<p<q<\infty$. As consequences, we determine the exponential volume asymptotics of Lorentz balls and obtain asymptotic independence of any fixed number of coordinates. We also prove a law of large numbers for Lorentz norms with finite parameters and use it, together with the volume asymptotics, to obtain a Schechtman--Schmuckenschläger type theorem for intersections of volume-normalized Lorentz balls. We further derive a variational formula for the logarithmic intersection asymptotics. The proof combines an exponential change of measure with quantile interpolation and a variational argument that does not assume regularity of the maximizing quantile in advance.

Functional Analysis.title: Linear Dynamics of Composition Operators on Zygmund Spaces of Rooted Trees
Functional Analysis.summary: We conjugate composition operators on the Zygmund and little Zygmund spaces of an infinite, locally finite rooted tree $T$ by the second-difference isometries. A path Green kernel gives row-finite matrices that characterize boundedness and yield exact operator norms. A rigidity result holds on the chain $\mathbb{N}_0$. Boundedness on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$ is equivalent to $\varphi(n)=qn+b$ for all sufficiently large $n$, with $q\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and $b\in\mathbb{Z}$. For these symbols, $\varphi(n)>n$ eventually characterizes Li-Yorke chaos of $C_\varphi$ on either Zygmund space, allowing noninjectivity and periodic vertices. If $C_\varphi$ is bounded on $\mathcal{Z}_0(T)$ and $\varphi^k(T)$ eventually avoids every finite set, then for each $λ\ne0$, $λC_\varphi$ is Li-Yorke chaotic on either space exactly when the norms of its powers are unbounded. For $\varphi_q(n)=q(n+1)-1$ with integer $q\ge2$, the corresponding conditions are $|λ|q^2>1$ on both Zygmund spaces and $|λ|q>1$ on the little Lipschitz space. For bounded $C_\varphi$ on $\mathcal{Z}_0(\mathbb{N}_0)$, topological mixing and Devaney chaos each hold exactly for injective symbols with no periodic vertices and eventual slope $q\ge2$. For such bounded operators with strictly increasing $\varphi$ and $\varphi(0)>0$, $q\ge2$ also characterizes hypercyclicity and frequent hypercyclicity.

Functional Analysis.title: Schauder bases and local unconditional structure in Hardy spaces of Dirichlet series
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that among the Hardy spaces $\mathcal{H}^p$ of Dirichlet series with $1\le p<\infty$, only $\mathcal{H}^2$ has local unconditional structure. Consequently, $\mathcal{H}^p$ admits an unconditional basis exactly when $p=2$. At the endpoint $p=1$, we also construct a Schauder basis of Dirichlet polynomials and give an explicit formula for each basis vector. Together, these results answer the basis questions posed by Aleman, Olsen and Saksman, as well as the question of Saksman and Seip concerning an unconditional basis for $\mathcal{H}^1$.

Functional Analysis.title: Multilinear embedding theorem for fractional sparse operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We show some simple sufficient conditions under which the multilinear embedding theorem holds for fractional sparse operators. By verifying these conditions, we establish the theorem for power weights. We also clarify the relation between vanishing local Morrey spaces and $L^p \to L^q$, $1<p,q<\infty$, infinitesimal relative boundedness theorem. More precisely, we establish that belonging to some vanishing local Morrey spaces of the weight $v$ with an appropriate power provides sufficient conditions under which $L^p \to L^q$, $1<p,q<\infty$, infinitesimal relative bounds holds for Schrödinger operators $(-Δ)^{α/2}+v$.

Functional Analysis.title: Structural and Dynamical Properties of Subfactor Commuting Squares
Functional Analysis.summary: This paper explores the algebraic invariants and ergodic behavior of the finite-index inclusions forming commuting squares of $\text{II}_1$ factors. We begin by establishing how regularity, intermediate-subfactor lattices, and Weyl groups transfer across the commuting square under relative commutant and irreducibility conditions. Furthermore, we provide a complete characterization, via a novel factorization theorem, of the unitary normalizers of the upper inclusion when the lower inclusion is regular. Applying these findings to crossed-product inclusions induced by discrete groups, we introduce a relative eigenbasis property that preserves regular inclusions. Finally, we contrast this by proving that a relative weak mixing condition on the group action forces the crossed-product inclusion to be singular.

Functional Analysis.title: Non-Ljusternik--Schnirelman eigenvalues of the pure $p$-Laplacian exist
Functional Analysis.summary: An old and well-known open problem in the critical point theory asks whether, for some $p \neq 2$ and some bounded domain $Ω$, there exists a critical value of the $p$-Dirichlet energy $\|\nabla u\|_{p;Ω}^p$ over an $L^p(Ω)$-sphere in $W_0^{1,p}(Ω)$ lying outside of a Ljusternik--Schnirelman type sequence of critical values, the latter will be called LS eigenvalues of the $p$-Laplacian. In this work, we provide a positive answer by showing the existence of a non-LS eigenvalue when $p>2$ is sufficiently close to $2$ and $Ω$ is just a planar rectangle close to the square. The arguments pursue the observation that a simple eigenvalue of the Laplacian can be a common point for several branches of eigenvalues of the $p$-Laplacian as $p$ varies. Since LS eigenvalues are continuous with respect to $p$ and exhaust the whole spectrum when $p=2$, we deduce that at least one of the branches must contain non-LS eigenvalues.
Functional Analysis.comment: 17 pages, 1 figure. Exposition revised, main theorem strengthened, its proof simplified, several remarks added, and bibliography updated. Accepted to Algebra i Analiz (St. Petersburg Mathematical Journal)

Functional Analysis.title: Topological Vector Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: Motivated by applications to duality theorems for $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology of rigid analytic spaces, we study the category of Topological Vector Spaces in the setting of condensed mathematics. We prove that it contains, as full subcategories, both the category of (topologically) bounded algebraic Vector Spaces and the category of perfect complexes on the Fargues-Fontaine curve. Vector Spaces coming from $p$-adic pro-étale cohomology of smooth partially proper rigid analytic varieties are examples of sheaves belonging to the former category.

Functional Analysis.title: Isospectral Density Design and Distinct Global Shape Transitions in Weighted Yukawa Droplets
Functional Analysis.summary: We study Euclidean perimeter plus Yukawa repulsion with a fixed radial source density and a fixed ordinary volume. For each sufficiently small positive screening parameter, we construct two smooth, positive, strictly increasing densities whose constrained shape Hessians at the unit ball agree for every coupling. Their source masses, Yukawa moments, and ball self-energies also agree. Just above their common first global transition threshold, all minimizers form one rotation orbit of tetrahedral shapes for one density and one orbit of sectoral threefold shapes for the other. Both transitions are continuous, and the minimizing shapes are strictly convex. We obtain the two densities by fixing the boundary data that determine the Hessian and changing the higher derivatives that determine the reduced quartic energy. We compute a positive quartic coefficient, restore the three scalar observables by interior corrections, and add a finite exterior density barrier to control all finite-perimeter competitors.

Functional Analysis.title: The numerical index with respect to a Lipschitz map
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce the Lipschitz numerical range, radius, and index with respect to a norm-one Lipschitz map, unifying the Lipschitz numerical index of a Banach space and the numerical index with respect to an operator. For real-valued maps, we obtain metric formulas on finite metric spaces and graphs. In particular, a connected simple unweighted graph with at least two vertices is bipartite if and only if its real Lipschitz-free space, or equivalently its dual, has classical numerical index one. We also characterize finite metric spaces by universal numerical-radius attainment. Among complete metric spaces, we characterize length spaces by non-denseness of maps attaining their $g$-Lipschitz numerical radius for every norm-one $g$. Moreover, we derive upper bounds for the $g$-Lipschitz numerical index with $\ell_p$ targets, $1<p<\infty$, and lower bounds for the Lipschitz numerical index of spaces with property $β$. Finally, for norm-one operators $G: X \to Y$ between real Banach spaces, we prove $$ n_{G^*}(Y^*,X^*) \leq n_{L,G}(X,Y) \leq n_G(X,Y), $$ with equality in the upper bound whenever $X$ is separable or $Y$ is $1$-complemented in its bidual. This extends recent equality results for the identity operator to arbitrary norm-one operators and a broader class of target spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Forelli--Rudin Type Operators in Infinite Dimensions, I
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce Forelli--Rudin-type integral operators on the open unit ball of \(\ell^2\). We completely characterize the boundedness of these operators between weighted \(L^p\) and \(L^q\) spaces for all \(p,q\in[1,\infty]\), as well as their membership in every Schatten class of operators between the corresponding weighted \(L^2\) spaces. We also establish trace formulas for these operators that cannot be obtained from their finite-dimensional counterparts by a formal passage to the limit as the dimension tends to infinity. Our results are not merely infinite-dimensional extensions of those obtained by Cheng, Fang, Wang, and the second author (2017), Zhao and Zhou (2022), and Ding (2022). Rather, they reveal new phenomena that are unique to infinite dimensions and arise from the fundamental geometric and measure-theoretic differences between finite- and infinite-dimensional spaces. A key ingredient in our proofs is the establishment of new Forelli--Rudin-type asymptotic estimates in infinite dimensions. These estimates also provide new insights into the development of function theory on the infinite-dimensional unit ball.

Functional Analysis.title: The norm formula in a Banach space and in its complete theory
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $h$ be the Hilbert norm on the real space $\ell_2(\mathbb{N})\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb{N})$, and put $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. For each of Bollobás's additive norms $h+\varepsilon q$, $\varepsilon>0$, and for the quadratic norm $\sqrt{h^2+q^2}$, the norm formula $\lVert x+y\rVert$ is unstable on the renormed space and has no independence property in its complete theory. We approximate $q(x+y)$ uniformly on bounded Hilbert balls by truncating small coordinates. For $n$ fixed test vectors and thresholds, the number of threshold patterns of $q(x+y)$ as $y$ varies is bounded by a polynomial in $n$ when the support sizes of the test vectors and of $y$ are bounded. These estimates give finite fat-shattering dimension for the translates of $q$ at every positive scale. The norm formula on a space can be stable, unstable without the independence property, or have the independence property. We give an example in each of these three cases where the formula has the independence property in the complete theory, and an example in each of the first two cases where it lacks that property in the complete theory. All five spaces satisfy a common midpoint estimate for uniform convexity, and each admits an isomorphism to Hilbert space of distortion at most $\sqrt3$.
Functional Analysis.comment: Revised abstract and introduction, with citations to Lupini

Functional Analysis.title: On König's non-existence conjecture for the one-dimensional fractional Bianchi-Egnell inequality
Functional Analysis.summary: König conjectured that the sharp stability constant in the Bianchi-Egnell inequality for the one-dimensional fractional Sobolev inequality equals the local stability constant and that the associated quotient has no minimizer outside the set of optimizers of the fractional Sobolev inequality. We prove both assertions for $s<1/2$ sufficiently close to $1/2$, with an explicitly computable threshold. The proof is based on a reinterpretation of the Frank-Lieb rigidity mechanism. Due to the lack of smooth variational structure of the Bianchi-Egnell quotient, we work with a refined limiting inequality of Beckner-Onofri-type on the circle with vanishing first-order moments, which we derive from Toeplitz determinants.

Functional Analysis.title: Operator-valued maximal $f$-divergences for completely positive maps
Functional Analysis.summary:
We introduce an operator-valued maximal $f$-divergence for completely positive (CP) maps between von Neumann algebras, associated with an operator convex function $f$ on $(0,+\infty)$. The construction takes values in the extended lower-semibounded self-adjoint part of the codomain von Neumann algebra. We prove independence of the common CP upper bound used in its computation, joint subadditivity, monotonicity under unital precomposition and normal postcomposition, a martingale convergence theorem for normal CP maps, and joint lower semicontinuity in the point-$σ$-weak topology.
  For normal positive functionals, our construction recovers Hiai's maximal $f$-divergence. As a consequence, we establish its joint weak lower semicontinuity for arbitrary von Neumann algebras, answering a question left open by Hiai.
  For $η(t)=t log t$, we obtain an operator-valued Belavkin--Staszewski (BS) relative entropy. Moreover, for normal channels with $σ$-finite codomain, we prove that the BS channel divergence of Hollands and Ranallo coincides with the extended norm of our operator-valued divergence.
  Finally, we give finite-dimensional examples and obtain an explicit formula for a finite-index conditional expectation. In the BS case, this formula reduces to the logarithm of the Jones--Kosaki index.

Functional Analysis.title: Spectral Landmarks: Alignment of Landmark Kernel Translates with the Leading Eigenfunctions of a Kernel Operator
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the problem of choosing $m$ landmark points so that the span of the kernel translates is as close as possible to the leading $s$-dimensional eigenspace of a positive-definite kernel. The natural measure is the Hilbert-Schmidt operator discrepancy between the reproducing-kernel-Hilbert-space (RKHS) projectors onto the two subspaces. We give a closed form spectral alignment function in terms of the truncated Mercer kernel and relate it to the classical integrated power function (Nyström trace error) through a two-sided sandwich bound. Minimizing the function by gradient descent on the landmark coordinates produces landmark sets that are evenly spaced. Theoretical results show that optimal configurations are those whose eigenfunction sampling matrix is a scaled isometry. On homogeneous spaces these are exactly the minimal equal-weight cubature rules for products of leading eigenfunctions, and for every $m\ge s$ they are the configurations whose sampled eigenfunctions form a unit-norm tight frame. Experiments on $\mathbb{S}^1$ and $\mathbb{S}^2$ agree with the theory. On the circle, with $s\le2m$ and a moderate bandwidth, every random start converges to equispaced landmarks, and on the sphere the optimizer recovers the regular tetrahedron, octahedron, and icosahedron from random starts. Finally, we analyze the numerical conditioning of the problem.

Functional Analysis.title: Zong's problem on $2d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball
Functional Analysis.summary:
We prove that the intersection of $2d$ half-spaces containing the Euclidean unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{d}$. Equality in the radius bound characterizes the cube up to orthogonal transformations. The proof gives a lower bound for the average squared norm of the vertices, weighted by the Gaussian measures of their normal cones. This estimate follows from an inequality for the Gaussian measures of a simplicial cone and its projected facets, which in turn reduces to a linear estimate for the Gaussian centroid of a simplicial cone.
  We also discuss a quadratic extension of the problem and give a bound for it using an independent spectral argument. This bound implies that the intersection of any $m > d$ half-spaces containing the unit ball contains a point of norm at least $\sqrt{m}\,\ln\frac{m}{m-d}$.

Functional Analysis.title: Banach-Mazur distance and related methods of comparing convex bodies
Functional Analysis.summary: The Banach-Mazur distance is one of the standard tools used in the study of mathematical objects such as convex bodies or normed spaces, and it becomes indispensable when investigating properties that are invariant under linear isomorphisms. It appears in convex geometry and convex analysis as a way to quantify the approximation of convex bodies. In functional analysis, it plays a basic role in the study of local properties of Banach spaces. The goal of this survey is to present a cohesive picture of these two perspectives. We supply an extensive collection of known results for reference and list open problems of varying difficulty, which could stimulate further research. We include in our discussion several distinct variations on the concept of the Banach-Mazur distance, some of them exploratory, that haven't received much attention to date in the literature. We follow the trend - which emerged in recent decades - of considering arbitrary convex bodies, and not just those that are centrally symmetric. Finally, we include a comprehensive list of references on the Banach-Mazur distance.

Functional Analysis.title: The dimension-free threshold for maximal sections of $\ell_p$
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove the existence of a sharp threshold $p_0 \approx 26.265\ldots$, such that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\geq p_0$, the volume maximizing section of the unit ball of $\ell_p^n$ is the section with Ball's hyperplane $(\frac{e_1+e_2}{\sqrt{2}})^\perp$, whereas for $p\in(2,p_0)$ the asymptotic maximizer as the ambient dimension $n\to\infty$ is the hyperplane orthogonal to the diagonal vector $\frac{e_1+\cdots+e_n}{\sqrt{n}}$.

Functional Analysis.title: Adapted transport inequalities in continuous time
Functional Analysis.summary: Given a strong solution $X$ to a stochastic differential equation (SDE), we establish sufficient conditions under which $\text{Law}(X)$ satisfies an adapted quadratic transport cost inequality (AQTCI) with respect to the semimartingale adapted Wasserstein distance. When the drift and diffusion coefficients are Markovian, we further show that the AQTCI tensorizes in a dimension-free manner. As a corollary, we show that various stochastic control problems, e.g. optimal stopping and mean-variance portfolio selection, are stable under bounded, measurable drift perturbations. Additionally, we derive concentration inequalities (with respect to certain dynamic risk measures) for stochastic integrals $\int H_s dX_s$ and deduce appropriate bounds on their tail behavior. Furthermore, using the functional Itô formula, we show that the AQTCI for $\text{Law}(X)$ allows one to deduce classical transport inequalities for $\text{Law}(F(X))$ even when $F$ is not Lipschitz on path space. Finally, we give sufficient conditions for $\text{Law}(X)$ to satisfy AQTCIs when $X$ is a solution to a scalar fractional SDE or stochastic Volterra equation.

Functional Analysis.title: Actions of quantum groups: the standard implementation and relatively invariant weights
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish a characterisation of the standard implementation for actions of locally compact quantum groups on von Neumann algebras, extending results of Daws-Skalski-Viselter and Haagerup. As a consequence, we prove that taking the standard implementation respects morphisms of quantum groups. We also prove that several natural conditions expressing relative $ρ$-invariance for n.s.f. weights are equivalent.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge for generative AI: numerical algorithms and approximation guarantees
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a soft-constrained formulation of the Schrödinger bridge problem, in which the terminal distribution constraint is relaxed into a penalty on the discrepancy between the terminal law of the controlled process and a target distribution. This leads to an unconstrained McKean--Vlasov stochastic control problem, where the interaction enters only through the terminal cost. We characterize the optimizer via a McKean--Vlasov forward-backward stochastic differential equation and establish well-posedness under very mild assumptions. We also analyze two approximation regimes relevant to data-driven computation: approximation of the target law by empirical samples, and finite-particle approximation of the McKean--Vlasov control problem. For both, we derive convergence results and error estimates. Finally, building on the well-posedness and approximation results, we investigate two neural numerical methods: one based on the forward-backward system and the other on direct control optimization. Both methods are tested on state-of-the-art generative tasks. Our results provide both an algorithmic foundation and its theoretical guarentee for soft-constrained Schrödinger bridge problems in sample-based generative modeling.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Characterizing nonlocal Sobolev spaces as generalized Bessel potential spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study nonlocal Sobolev spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, defined via a general class of nonlocal gradients $D^ρ$ associated with a kernel function $ρ$. As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. First, we describe $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in terms of Fourier multipliers involving the symbol of the nonlocal potential associated with $D^ρ$. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $ρ$-Laplacian $Δ^ρ$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-Δ^ρ)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_ρ* L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces. These results generalize the well-known fact that, in the special case of the Riesz kernel, the resulting fractional Sobolev spaces coincide with the classical Bessel potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded simply connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover an initial vacuum point will persist and force the exponential growth of density gradients.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic radial symmetry of $p$-Ginzburg-Landau minimizers on the disk
$p$-ellipticity for systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We extend the concept of $p$-ellipticity for (single) elliptic operators, that we introduced in arxiv:1611.00653, to the case of systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients. The $p$-ellipticity condition from this paper turns out to be equivalent, up to a factor depending on $p$, to a condition for systems introduced (and equally named) by Dindoš, Li and Pipher in arXiv:2007.13190. We prove several key properties of $p$-ellipticity akin to those that have been known to hold in the scalar case (arxiv:1611.00653).
