In some respects, however, the vector case fundamentally differs from the scalar one. As an application we establish the contractivity on $L^p$ of the operator semigroup generated by systems of elliptic equations with complex coefficients and subject to Dirichlet, Neumann or mixed boundary conditions.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 71 pages. This paper is currently submitted for publication. The version posted here is a revised version of the submitted one. We plan to post a substantial follow-up on this paper soon, containing several extensions and improvements

Analysis of PDEs.title: Long time derivation of the Boltzmann equation from dynamics of short-range potentials
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We derive the Boltzmann equation from the Newtonian dynamics of particles interacting through a short-range repulsive potential for arbitrarily long times, in the Boltzmann--Grad limit. This extends the recent hard-sphere result of Deng, Hani and Ma (arXiv:2408.07818) to short-range potentials. Compared with hard spheres, two new difficulties arise: (i) in the absence of a Burago--Ferleger--Kononenko-type bound (Ann. of Math. 147 (1998), 695--708, doi:10.2307/120962), a bounded number of particles may undergo an unbounded number of collisions within a short time; and (ii) since collisions last a positive time, three or more particles may interact simultaneously. To overcome (i), we treat such clusters of recollisions as single objects, called boxes, keeping track only of their entry and exit structure, so that internal collisions do not enter the combinatorial counting. The multi-particle collisions in (ii), together with the boxes, lead to more complicated molecules, which requires adapting the counting estimates and the cutting algorithm.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Half-delocalization for semiclassical measures of split higher-dimensional quantum cat maps
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study quantum cat maps on multidimensional tori and prove an optimal lower bound for the Kolmogorov-Sinai entropy of their semiclassical measures under the hypothesis that the dynamics splits over the rationals. This is the first instance of such a bound for a dynamical system with multiple positive Lyapunov exponents. The proof is based on a new notion of conditional quantum dynamical entropy and a careful study of the multiple Ehrenfest time adapted to the dynamics.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 61 pages. Comments are welcome. A log was missing in a hypothesis of theorem 5.1 and in the proof of corollary 5.1

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Maxwell Bethe-Sommerfeld problem I: Thin-layer induction and results for planar TE modes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We present a framework for constructing a single medium that supports infinitely many complete spectral gaps for periodic divergence-form operators, which arise from the transverse electric (TE) polarization of Maxwell's equations. The construction proceeds by inductively inserting a seed medium with a prescribed spectral gap into a thin layer of the unit cell. As a result, we obtain densely many counterexamples to the Bethe-Sommerfeld Conjecture (BSC) for divergence-form operators. Moreover, we prove that the thin-layer construction controls the gap topology: by carefully selecting the seed medium, one can realize a single operator with any prescribed configuration of gap Chern numbers. This is the first of two papers that contains all the fundamental ingredients for the thin-layer induction. In the second paper, we will apply this framework to disprove the BSC for the full three-dimensional Maxwell operator.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A formally verified convergence theorem for the tug-of-war scheme of the normalized $p$-Laplacian
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We present a complete formalization, using Lean 4, of the convergence of $p$-harmonious functions to the viscosity solution of the Dirichlet problem for the normalized $p$-Laplacian, $2 \le p < \infty$, as the step size goes to zero. By $p$-harmonious functions we mean solutions of the dynamic programming principle of tug-of-war with noise. Our proof follows the argument of Barles and Souganidis and is formalized in full, depending only on Mathlib and the standard axioms of Lean. In particular, we include the asymptotic expansion of the scheme, the viscosity properties of the half-relaxed limits, existence and uniqueness for the discrete problem, the comparison principle and uniqueness for the homogeneous equation, Aleksandrov's theorem, and Jensen's lemma.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 14 pages, 1 figure. Lean 4 source: https://github.com/BehroozMoosavi/tugofwar_formalization (tag v1.3). Blueprint and browsable formal statements: https://behroozmoosavi.github.io/tugofwar_formalization/

Analysis of PDEs.title: Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove global Strichartz estimates without loss outside two strictly convex obstacles, combining arguments from M.Ikawa (1982,1988) with more recent ones inspired by N.Burq, C.Guillarmou, and A. Hassell (2010) and O. Ivanovici (2010). This is to be contrasted with the loss in the smoothing estimate for the Schrödinger equation with Dirichlet boundary conditions in the presence of a trapped geodesic.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Strictly positive optimal Hardy weights on manifolds and graphs via Green potential
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Consider a subcritical functional $Q$ associated with a $p$-Schrödinger operator defined on a domain $Ω$ in a noncompact Riemannian manifold. Employing the supersolution construction, we obtain a family of strictly positive-critical Hardy weights for $Q$. The construction is based on the Green potential $G_f$, with a strictly positive charge $f$ such that $G_f$ vanishes at infinity. An interesting new feature of this family, depending on a parameter $0\leq \varepsilon\leq 1$, is the transition from positive-criticality to null-criticality at $\varepsilon=0$. Furthermore, we prove an analogous result on graphs.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 31 pages, argument for Theorem 6.10-(a) has been corrected

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quadrature-Induced Local Minima in Structure-Preserving Lotka-Volterra Control
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Harvest quadrature can change a discrete optimal control problem even when the state scheme stays fixed. We study this effect for a positivity-preserving Lotka--Volterra scheme. The difference appears in a model with harvesting alone: rewarding the scheme's removal flux gives a strictly convex reduced cost, whereas using prey density at the start of each step overestimates harvest and can create negative curvature and a strict local minimum that is not global. Rational root isolation certifies the two-step global minimizers. With diffusion in one space dimension, nonnegative bounded $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities, the costs, weighted gradients and Hessians differ by $O(τ)$ uniformly in the spatial mesh, where $τ$ is the time step. A uniform positive lower bound on the reduced Hessian gives the same order for the distance between nearby controls. A large enough effort penalty gives unique global discrete minimizers. We also prove positivity, exact population balance and a common variational limit, and derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions. Numerical tests trace changes in curvature and stationary controls across parameters and grids, with costs evaluated on a common reference using adaptive time stepping. The construction extends to weighted production--destruction systems, giving exact harvest accounting and smooth derivatives on fixed grids.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An abstract observability criterion via translation hulls, with applications to transport systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish an observability criterion for translation-covariant families of operators on $L^2(\mathbb R^d)$. Under continuity of the observed cell energies, a common summable localization bound, and reconstruction up to a locally collectively compact error, observability is equivalent to the absence of nonzero uniformly local invisible states on every configuration in the full translation hull. For one-dimensional transport systems satisfying the Kalman rank condition, this yields localized observability in the intrinsic Kalman--Jordan energy space for arbitrary real Jordan structure and nonzero speeds. For unions of observed intervals with a uniform positive lower length bound, the sharp condition is that the slowest characteristic travels farther than the gap supremum. Observability fails at equality even when this supremum is not attained. Duality gives exact controllability in the dual energy space. We also obtain sharp criteria for translating observation regions and scalar transport with an integrable convolution kernel. The reconstruction hypothesis is also necessary for observability. An anisotropic heat-flux example shows that it applies beyond coercive multiplication-plus-compact Gramian decompositions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Multiplicity of sign-changing solutions to higher-order $Q$-curvature equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we employ the dual cone method to establish the existence of infinitely many sign-changing solutions to the $Q$-curvature problem involving $GJMS$-operators of arbitrary order $m$ on closed Riemannian manifolds of dimension $n > 2m$, under the assumptions that the operators are coercive and positivity-preserving and that the manifold admits appropriate symmetries. To demonstrate the applicability of our framework, we provide explicit examples on both closed Einstein manifolds and closed special Einstein products. Notably, one of the major contributions of this work is deriving explicit conditions that guarantee the coercivity of $GJMS$-operators on closed special Einstein products.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stability of Plasma Echo Growth and the Sharp Sobolev Stability Threshold for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish stability of growing plasma echo cascades for the Vlasov--Poisson--Landau equation with Coulomb collisions near a global Maxwellian. The occurrence of plasma echoes, or even a growing cascade in a reduced model, does not by itself establish this stability. We prove that the amplification persists under changes in the linearized operator, including collisions and the exact evolving background coefficients, and under nonlinear perturbations. This yields optimality of the exponent $1/3$ obtained by Chaturvedi, Luk, and Nguyen in the Sobolev stability threshold. Specifically, we construct solutions with initial Sobolev perturbations of size $ν^{1/3}[\log(1/ν)]^p$ whose transport profiles exhibit norm inflation before the enhanced-dissipation time scale $ν^{-1/3}$. Since collisions preclude the backward Sobolev construction used in collisionless echo arguments, we prepare the initial data at physical time zero and control the entire forward evolution.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 162 pages. The roadmap of the proof can be found in Appendix C

Analysis of PDEs.title: Controllability of Acoustic Waves by Point Sources: Reachable States and Stable Reconstruction
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the terminal controllability of the three-dimensional acoustic wave equation driven by finitely many fixed point sources, with zero initial data and time-dependent amplitudes supported in a finite interval. Although finitely many fixed sources cannot control the whole energy space, we establish the following results:
  (i) For source amplitudes in the first-order Sobolev space in time, the terminal state has finite energy if and only if all amplitudes vanish at both endpoints of the control interval.
  (ii) We derive an exact frequency-domain identity for the terminal energy involving a Gram matrix whose diagonal entries are one and whose off-diagonal entries are given by the sinc function, depending on frequency and source separation.
  (iii) For every positive control time, the terminal control operator is bounded below and is an isomorphism onto its closed reachable range, which has infinite codimension even among states satisfying the finite-propagation support condition.
  (iv) We establish a necessary and sufficient radiation-field criterion for reachability, provide stable reconstruction of the unique controls, and characterize the best approximation of non-reachable targets.
  The optimal coercivity constant equals one before the shortest source travel time. At long times, it decays as the inverse square of the control time for two sources and as the inverse fourth power for three equally spaced collinear sources. We also obtain upper bounds for general configurations and illustrate the theoretical results through reproducible Galerkin computations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Liouville equation on Riemannian surfaces: the role of volume growth in classification and rigidity results
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Liouville equation $-Δ_g u = e^u$ on a complete, connected, non-compact, boundaryless Riemannian surface $(M, g)$ with non-negative Ricci curvature. Assuming only some asymptotic lower bound on the solution, we establish classification results for both the solutions and the ambient manifold, discussing also their optimality. Our results reveal a close connection between the volume growth of the manifold and the classification of both the solutions and the underlying manifold.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the planar four-junction solution to a vector-valued Allen-Cahn system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper concerns entire minimizing four-junction solutions to a two-dimensional Allen-Cahn system with a four-well potential. In a suitable regime of unequal surface tensions, the construction yields a family of solutions with varying opening angles of phase sectors. The proof employs two-direction slicing arguments for tight energy bounds and localization of the diffuse interface, together with a new iteration scheme that controls change of approximating sharp interfaces at successively smaller scales.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Dirichlet problems and Green functions for the octonionic Monge--Ampère equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the Dirichlet problem for the octonionic Monge-Ampere equation on smooth bounded domains in the octonionic plane $\mathbb{O}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^{16}$. For a smooth positive density that is nondecreasing in the unknown function, we prove existence and uniqueness of a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic solution whenever there is a smooth strictly plurisubharmonic subsolution with the prescribed boundary values. The result also holds on relatively compact domains with smooth boundary in flat translation quotients.
  On smooth bounded strictly octonionic pseudoconvex domains, we construct the unique Green function with zero boundary values and singularity $-|q-a|^{-6}+O(1)$ at an interior pole $a$. We prove $C^{1,1}$ regularity locally up to the boundary away from the pole, together with sharp bounds for the gradient and the full real Hessian. The proof combines boundary estimates based on translations and spin rotations with weighted estimates obtained by differentiating along rotations and dilations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4πm,4π(m+1))\times(4πk,4π(k+1))$, then \[
  \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k
  =(1-x)^{χ(M)-1}(1-y)^{χ(M)-1}(1-xy)^{χ(M)}, \] where $χ(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block.
  At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4π,0)$ and $(8π,4π)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Higher Integrability of Differential Form Globally Solving Certain Minimization Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $0\leq k\leq n-1,1<p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}\left(B;Λ^k\right)$, where $Λ^k$ is the vector space of all $k$-forms in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $B$ is an open ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this article, with one global higher integrability assumption on $du$, we study the global higher integrability of $dv$ where $v$ is the unique minimizer of the following functional: \begin{align*} \overline{w}\mapsto \int_{B} \left \lvert d\overline{w} \right \rvert^p \text{ where } \overline{w} \in u+W^{1,p}_{d^*,T}\left(B;Λ^{k}\right). \end{align*} As a machinery, with a similar higher integrability assumption on the $k+1$-differential form $\widetilde{F}$, we prove one local higher integrability of $d\widetilde{W}$ where $\widetilde{W}\in W^{1,p}\left(B_r\left(0\right);Λ^{k}\right)$ weakly solves: \begin{align*} d^*\left(\left \langle G \left(d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right), d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right \rangle^{\frac{p-2}{2}}G \left(d \widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right)\right)=0 \text{ in } B_r\left(0\right), \end{align*} for $G:B_r\left(0\right)\rightarrow GL\left({n\choose k+1};\mathbb{R}\right)$ symmetric, bounded, and uniformly elliptic measurable map, which is sufficiently close to the identity map $I:Λ^{k+1}\rightarrow Λ^{k+1}$. For each of the above mentioned cases, we prove one strong $\left(q,q\right)$ type estimate. As the primary tools, we use the Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality, Fefferman-Stein inequality, and one classical regularity result of K. Ulhenbeck.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 39 pages. This is a working draft. We will upload revised version soon. Comments are welcome!

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Critical Choquard Problem for a Quasilinear Schrödinger Operator with Singular Discontinuous Nonlinearity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this article, we study the quasilinear Schrödinger equation $-Δu - Δ\bigl(|u|^{2α}\bigr)\,|u|^{2α-2}u =λ\left(χ_{\{u<b\}} u^{-β}+\left(\int_Ω\frac{H(y,u)}{\left|x-y\right|^μ} dy\right)h(x,u)\right)$ in $Ω$, $u>0$ in $Ω$, $u=0$ on $\partialΩ$, where $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth bounded domain, $b>0$, $0<μ<2$, $α>\frac12$, $0<β<3$, and $h$ has critical exponential growth with primitive $H$. We show that there is $λ^*_b\in(0,\infty)$ such that the problem has a positive solution if and only if $λ\in(0,λ^*_b]$. For $λ<λ^*_b$, this solution is $g(v_λ)$, where the change of variables $g$ makes the problem semilinear and $v_λ$ is a local minimizer of the transformed energy in $H^1_0(Ω)$. If $h$ satisfies a lower bound at the critical scale $\exp\bigl(2α\,g^{-1}(u)^2\bigr)$, we obtain a second positive solution for every $λ\in(0,λ^*_b)$. The level estimate for this solution must be done at this scale, and not at the scale $e^{u^{4α}}$ used for semilinear problems. This bound excludes $h=f\,e^{u^{4α}}$ with $f$ of polynomial growth. For $α>1$, we obtain a second solution for $h=u^{4α-1}e^{u^{4α}}$, provided that the maximum of the first solution exceeds a constant depending only on $α$. For $α\leq1$, this question remains open.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Subwavelength resonances and localization in finite resonator chains with a size defect
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study subwavelength resonances of a finite chain of $N\ge2$ close-to-touching spherical resonators in three dimensions with a single radius defect of relative size $τ\in(0,1]$ and gap width $\varepsilon$. Taking the high-contrast limit before the narrow-gap limit, we prove that the positive generalized eigenvalues of the weighted chain coupling matrix with respect to the volume matrix determine the leading relative resonant frequencies. After eliminating the finite tails, we obtain an exact characteristic determinant and identify a unique critical ratio $τ_*\in(0,1)$ at which the largest eigenvalue crosses the upper edge of the homogeneous recurrence band $[0,4]$. For every $0<τ<τ_*$, exactly one eigenvalue lies above this band, and its eigenvector decays geometrically along the tails. As $τ\toτ_*^-$, its recurrence decay length diverges like $(τ_*-τ)^{-1/2}$. As $τ\to0$, exactly one eigenvalue diverges like $τ^{-2}$ and its eigenvector concentrates at the defect; if the defect is interior, one additional positive eigenvalue has order $τ$. For suitably normalized relative resonant modes, the sequential limit of the $\varepsilon$-scaled gradient supremum in each gap equals the absolute difference between adjacent reduced amplitudes. For the largest-eigenvalue mode, this yields defect-adjacent gradient concentration as the defect shrinks.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Strong transport noise prevents self-intersection in 2D fluid-structure interaction
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the interaction of a viscous incompressible fluid with a flexible elastic shell occupying the boundary of the fluid's domain in two space dimensions. The shell is modelled by a visco-elastic linearised beam equation. It is an open problem in fluid-structure interaction, if a self-intersection of the structure can be excluded in the long run. We show that by adding a physically well-motived and sufficiently strong transport noise in the structure equation, the self-intersection does not occur before any given end-time with any prescribed probability smaller than 1.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: We are using now a truly infinite dimensional noise which is not energy-conservative. This fixes a flaw from the previous version

Analysis of PDEs.title: Time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann system with a general external force in $\mathbb{R}^3$
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This paper is concerned with the time-periodic solutions of the Vlasov-Poisson-Boltzmann (VPB) system with a given time-periodic external force in the whole space $\mathbb{R}^3$, where the force is allowed to be non-potential. For the purpose, we first study the Cauchy problem around global Maxwellians, proving the global existence of small-amplitude solutions in a hybrid function space that combines the low-frequency Besov framework for the forced Boltzmann equation with a corresponding control of the self-consistent electric field. One key point occurs to the nonlinear Vlasov force $-
abla_{x}φ\cdot 
abla_{v}f +  rac{1}{2}v \cdot 
abla_{x}φf$ at low frequencies. Rather than treating it as a generic source term, we exploit the Poisson equation and macroscopic balance laws to recover the structural cancellation required for the VPB semi-group estimates, which combined with high-frequency energy estimates and weighted microscopic propagation, yields a closed global well-posedness theory. We further prove uniform stability of the difference of two small-amplitude solutions driven by the same force with respect to distinct initial data. As a consequence of those results, for the time-periodic problem where the external force is time-periodic, we are able to make use of Serrin's method to establish the existence of a unique time-periodic solution of the same period together with its large time asymptotic stability. Our result also gives the existence and stability of stationary solutions when the external force is time-independent.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 46 pages. Typos corrected. All comments are welcome

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary singularities for weak solutions of semilinear elliptic problems throughout the subcritical range
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^N$ ($N \ge 2$) be a bounded domain with smooth boundary $\partial Ω$. We construct positive very weak solutions for the problem $Δu + u^p = 0$ in $Ω$ for all $p \in [(N+1)/(N-1),(N+2)/(N-2))$ when $N \ge 3$ and for all $p \ge (N+1)/(N-1)$ when $N = 2$. These solutions vanish in a suitable trace sense on $\partial Ω$ but are singular at prescribed isolated points. This gives a completely affirmative answer to a conjecture of del Pino-Musso-Pacard.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Geomagnetic Q-Response Inversion as a Calderón-Type Inverse Boundary Value Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Whether electrical conductivity can be uniquely determined from magnetic measurements alone is a fundamental question in geomagnetic induction sounding. For a spherical conductor in the magnetoquasistatic model, we establish an equivalence between the complete Q-response and a restricted magnetic boundary operator, connecting geomagnetic induction to Calderon-type inverse boundary value theory. For axisymmetric conductivities, we derive exact representations of the zero-frequency zonal response derivatives as conductivity-weighted spatial moments. These formulas give an explicit interpretation of individual response derivatives, and completeness of the moment family yields conductivity uniqueness. For layered axisymmetric models with known shell interfaces and piecewise-constant radial dependence, we further establish uniqueness at a single nonzero frequency. Finite-dimensional subclasses also admit uniqueness and stability estimates from finitely many response coefficients at sufficiently low nonzero frequencies. These results identify complementary mechanisms for conductivity recovery from magnetic-only observations, while uniqueness for general three-dimensional scalar conductivities from ideal magnetic-only Q-response data remains unresolved.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness of invariant measures for mean-field stochastic damped wave and heat equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study invariant measures for a Wick-renormalized mean-field stochastic damped wave equation on the two-dimensional torus and for the corresponding stochastic heat equation. With Wick ordering relative to the massive Gaussian free field with covariance $(1-Δ)^{-1}$, we prove uniqueness among invariant laws whose renormalized second moment belongs to $H^{-σ}(\mathbb T^2)$, where $0<σ<\tfrac12$. Stationarity reduces the mean-field equation to a linear equation with a deterministic distribution-valued potential. We show that self-consistency forces this deterministic potential to vanish. The damped wave equation therefore has invariant law $\mathcal N(0,(1-Δ)^{-1})\otimes\mathcal N(0,\varepsilon^{-2}I)$, with covariance understood distributionally, while the heat equation has the Gaussian free field as its invariant law. This resolves self-consistency for spatially varying distribution-valued potentials and establishes uniqueness in the specified class. As the inertia parameter tends to zero, the position marginal remains equal to the invariant law of the corresponding stochastic heat equation, whereas the velocity marginal assigns vanishing probability to every bounded subset of $H^{-1-σ}(\mathbb T^2)$, establishing Smoluchowski-Kramers type behavior.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 20 pages, 1 figure. Based in part on the author's master's thesis at the University of Bonn

Functional Analysis.title: Weil's quadratic form via the screw function
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish a unified operator-theoretic framework for understanding the results on the Weil quadratic form obtained by Yoshida (1992), Bombieri (2001, 2003), Connes--Consani (2023), and Connes--Consani--Moscovici (2025+) from the perspective of the screw function introduced in Suzuki (2023). An advantage of the approach via the screw function is that it provides a method to study the Weil quadratic form, which is originally defined in terms of distributions, by means of continuous functions and brings the theory of de Branges spaces into the analysis of the Weil quadratic form via the Fourier transform. Based on this framework, we formulate a conjecture stating that a self-adjoint operator whose eigenvalues are the imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function can be obtained as the limit, as $a \to \infty$, of self-adjoint operators arising from nonlocal realizations of the first-order differential operator on the finite interval $[-a,a]$. All these results are obtained without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis. This conjecture may be compared with the limit formula for the Riemann zeta function expressed in terms of zeta-regularized products proposed by Connes, Consani, and Moscovici, and it sheds new light on the spectral-theoretic interpretation of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

Functional Analysis.title: Higher-Order Isometric Liftings of Convex and Concave Operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We study higher-order isometric liftings of bounded operators on Hilbert spaces under convexity and concavity assumptions. First, we prove that every $m$-convex operator $T$ satisfying $\sup_{n\geq 1}n^{-(m-1)}\|T^n\|^2<\infty$ admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting whose complementary diagonal entry is an expansive $(m-1)$-isometric weighted shift. Next, we show that every $m$-concave operator admits a minimal $m$-isometric lifting with an expansive $m$-isometric weighted-shift component, without imposing an additional growth assumption. We also establish an alternation between convexity and concavity under polynomial growth conditions and give examples illustrating limitations of converse implications.

Functional Analysis.title: Totally Positive Interpolation and Critical Sampling of Positive Operator Orbits
Functional Analysis.summary: How few observations are needed for the stable recovery of the initial state of a linear dynamical system? We study this question for systems governed by a positive operator, with fixed sensors and freely chosen sampling times and positive weights. Our main tool is an interpolation theorem for translates of a nonzero continuous integrable totally positive function. For every uniformly separated sequence of centers, we choose one node near each center so that the corresponding collocation operator is boundedly invertible. The displacement, node separation, and operator bounds depend only on the kernel and the lower separation of the centers; no upper bound is needed on their gaps. If a single integer orbit is a frame, we construct weighted Riesz bases whose sampling counts attain the spectral lower bound up to a bounded additive error. The same method yields bases from continuous functional calculus, including explicit resolvent bases. In the case of normal operators, we give a single-orbit frame for which every admissible weighted design has sampling count growing faster than the radial spectral count.

Functional Analysis.title: Property A and the identification of the maximal and reduced uniform Roe algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $X$ be a discrete metric space of bounded geometry. We prove that $X$ has property A if and only if the canonical map $$λ:C^*_{u,max}(X)\to C^*_u(X)$$ is an isomorphism.

Functional Analysis.title: Isometries for Hilbert's metric on vector lattices of continuous functions
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper Hilbert's projective metric on the interior of the positive cone of an Archimedean vector lattice with a strong order unit is studied. We show that every surjective isometry between two such projective cones is induced by a lattice isomorphism, possibly composed with the inversion map, and that the inversion occurs precisely when the vector lattice is a bounded inverse closed $f$-algebra. In particular, two such projective cones are isometric if and only if the underlying vector lattices are lattice isomorphic, and we determine the corresponding isometry groups. We apply these results to spaces of Hölder continuous functions, absolutely continuous functions, and continuous functions of bounded variation, for which we describe the surjective isometries explicitly. Finally, we show that the projective cones of these spaces of functions on an interval all have the same metric completion, but that no two of them are isometric.

Functional Analysis.title: Dynamical frames through Sz.$-$Nagy$-$Foias dilations
Functional Analysis.summary: We present a unified operator-theoretic treatment of dynamical frames based on defect operators, Stein equations, and the Sz.-Nagy-Foiaş dilation theory of contractions. An explicit realization of the minimal isometric dilation relates generating vectors to the wandering subspace and provides a geometric interpretation of standard frame constructions. For Parseval dynamical frames, polar decomposition yields a complete factorization of the generating families through the adjoint defect operator. General dynamical frames are described in terms of positive solutions of a Stein equation, leading to an equivalent formulation of the frame index. We also collect characteristic-function criteria for strong stability and joint strong stability. In the diagonal case, the characteristic function expresses the classical separation and Carleson conditions in operator-theoretic terms. The emphasis is on explicit constructions, direct proofs, and a common framework for known results.

Functional Analysis.title: Stochastic Multivariate Taylor Measure Functions
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce stochastic multivariate Taylor measure functions (SMTMFs), which extend the multivariate Taylor measure function framework through random Taylor coefficients and a possibly random Taylor parameter. We establish their measurability properties and derive sufficient conditions for the associated processes to be martingales, including criteria based on conditional covariance and continuous semimartingale decompositions. We construct standard Brownian motion as an almost surely uniformly convergent limit of finite SMTMFs using the Levy-Ciesielski representation. We also show that the completion of the finite stochastic MTMF space under the expected uniform norm contains Brownian motion, Brownian bridges, fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter H, and Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes with integrable initial conditions. Our main result characterizes this completion as the Bochner space, under an admissibility condition on jointly measurable stochastic Taylor coefficients. The proof uses dyadic piecewise linear interpolation to approximate integrable continuous stochastic processes in the expected uniform norm. Thus, the completed SMTMF space encompasses the full class of integrable continuous random functions on a compact time interval.
Functional Analysis.comment: 63 pages; Keywords: Bochner space; Brownian motion; fractional Brownian motion; Martingales; Semimartingales; Stochastic multivariate Taylor measure functions

Functional Analysis.title: Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
Every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of simply connected generalized gyrovector spaces (GGVs) with real value-line structure extends uniquely to a global bijective isometry. The extension is a left gyrotranslation composed with an isometry preserving the identity, gyroaddition, and scalar multiplication. Gyromidpoints and point reflections give continuation of local isometry germs. Without assuming simple connectedness, a global bijective isometric extension exists exactly when the germs of the map and its inverse are fixed by their respective monodromy actions. Continuity of each fixed-scalar multiplication map implies contractibility and hence simple connectedness.
  We construct standard-norm GGVs for $t>0$ on positive invertible cones of nonzero unital JB-algebras and, in dimension greater than one, on their projective cones. Power maps relate their gyrometrics to Thompson's and Hilbert's metrics, respectively, with equality at $t=1$. Thus for both metrics, bijective isometries between nonempty connected open subsets extend uniquely to global bijective isometries. We give proofs of the known Thompson and Hilbert isometry classifications, together with their power-coordinate forms for every $t>0$, using the GGV Mazur--Ulam theorem and recovering the Jordan structures from infinitesimal gyrations. Applications include a new proof of Mankiewicz's theorem on connected open subsets of real normed spaces and a local extension theorem for hyperbolic balls in real inner product spaces, including incomplete and infinite-dimensional spaces. We also give constructions for products and function spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Higher Integrability of Differential Form Globally Solving Certain Minimization Problem
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $0\leq k\leq n-1,1<p<\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}\left(B;Λ^k\right)$, where $Λ^k$ is the vector space of all $k$-forms in $\mathbb{R}^n$ and $B$ is an open ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$. In this article, with one global higher integrability assumption on $du$, we study the global higher integrability of $dv$ where $v$ is the unique minimizer of the following functional: \begin{align*} \overline{w}\mapsto \int_{B} \left \lvert d\overline{w} \right \rvert^p \text{ where } \overline{w} \in u+W^{1,p}_{d^*,T}\left(B;Λ^{k}\right). \end{align*} As a machinery, with a similar higher integrability assumption on the $k+1$-differential form $\widetilde{F}$, we prove one local higher integrability of $d\widetilde{W}$ where $\widetilde{W}\in W^{1,p}\left(B_r\left(0\right);Λ^{k}\right)$ weakly solves: \begin{align*} d^*\left(\left \langle G \left(d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right), d\widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right \rangle^{\frac{p-2}{2}}G \left(d \widetilde{W}+\widetilde{F}\right)\right)=0 \text{ in } B_r\left(0\right), \end{align*} for $G:B_r\left(0\right)\rightarrow GL\left({n\choose k+1};\mathbb{R}\right)$ symmetric, bounded, and uniformly elliptic measurable map, which is sufficiently close to the identity map $I:Λ^{k+1}\rightarrow Λ^{k+1}$. For each of the above mentioned cases, we prove one strong $\left(q,q\right)$ type estimate. As the primary tools, we use the Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality, Fefferman-Stein inequality, and one classical regularity result of K. Ulhenbeck.
Functional Analysis.comment: 39 pages. This is a working draft. We will upload revised version soon. Comments are welcome!

Functional Analysis.title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
Functional Analysis.summary: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property. We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

Functional Analysis.title: Schatten isometries of Grassmann spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
We characterize all (not necessarily surjective) Schatten $p$-isometries of the Grassmann space of rank $k$ projections on a complex Hilbert space for every $p\in(0,\infty]$. We prove that every such isometry is induced by a linear or conjugate-linear isometry of the underlying Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, with the additional possibility of composition with orthocomplementation when $\dim \mathcal H = 2k > 2$.
  Our result generalizes Wigner's theorem, which plays a central role in the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics. It also extends previous results on Schatten $p$-isometries of Grassmann spaces, including characterizations of surjective isometries by Gehér and Šemrl for $p=\infty$ and by Qian et al. for $0<p<\infty$ and that of not necessarily surjective isometries by Gehér for $p=2$.

Functional Analysis.title: Operator Fejér-Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial $F\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H)[x]$ positive semidefinite on $K$ admits a certificate in the operator quadratic module generated by $S$, with weighted degree at most $\operatorname{deg} F+c_S$. Here, $c_S$ depends only on $S$ and is independent of both $F$ and the coefficient Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, which may be infinite-dimensional. In contrast to the scalar case, natural matrix preorderings admit no uniform degree bound over compact semialgebraic subsets of the real line. We construct positive semidefinite quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees tend to infinity as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap remains bounded below. Conversely, uniform degree bounds hold for interval unions in a fixed compact interval when the component and gap lengths are bounded below by positive constants. Our proofs develop two techniques. The first is a quadratic reduction principle that reduces the problem of obtaining degree bounds for arbitrary-degree operator polynomials to the quadratic case, with a fixed additive increase in degree. The second uses a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil to transfer positivity on unions of intervals to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fejér-Riesz theorem provides certificates. We also obtain operator-valued Fejér-Riesz factorizations on unions of circular arcs, rational certificates with a fixed denominator on unbounded semialgebraic sets, and a characterization of the sets whose natural operator preorderings admit degree-preserving certificates.
Functional Analysis.comment: 38 pages; Three new corollaries have been added

Functional Analysis.title: A remark on the entropy numbers of mixed smoothness classes
Functional Analysis.summary: We find the right orders of both the entropy numbers and the Kolmogorov widths of classes of multivariate functions with bounded mixed derivative, when the class is defined by the restriction in the uniform norm and the error of approximation is measured in the uniform norm. The case of functions of two variables was settled about 30 years ago and the case of three or more variables stayed open.

Functional Analysis.title: A simple proof of the characterization of $\ell_\infty^n$ by norm-one projections and a stability estimate
Functional Analysis.summary: We give a short and elementary proof of a classical fact that an $n$-dimensional real or complex normed space with the absolute projection constant equal to one is linearly isometric to $\ell_\infty^n$. The proof uses only finite-dimensional convexity and linear algebra, with no infinite-dimensional ingredients. The same approach yields a quantitative stability estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{3}}$ when the absolute projection constant is at most $1+\varepsilon$. This improves Zippin's estimate of order $\varepsilon^{\frac{1}{8}}$ in each fixed dimension as $\varepsilon \to 0$. The real and complex cases are treated by the same arguments.

Functional Analysis.title: Scaling Fourier Inequalities for Locally Compact Quantum Groups
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we study Fourier and convolution inequalities on locally compact quantum groups in the presence of the scaling group. For $1\le p\le 2$, we investigate a family of scaling Fourier transforms and the associated norms $H_{p,θ}(\mathbb G)$, and we show that $H_{p,θ}(\mathbb G)<1$ for the real quantum $az+b$ group and $0<θ<1$, $1<p<2$. We also investigate scaling convolution for locally compact quantum groups and, by extending the ordinary convolution, obtain the corresponding scaling Young inequality in four different regions. In Young Region~II, under $1<p,s<2$ and $2\leq r<\infty$, we construct sequences proving norm one at every effective vertex and prove strict inequality at every other effective point.

Functional Analysis.title: Reflectionless measures with singular continuous components on Widom sets
Functional Analysis.summary: We implement a program of constructing a reflectionless measure on a Widom set with a nontrivial singular continuous component of Nazarov-Volberg and Yuditskii. The construction is an induction that based on two types of operations: splitting point mass and inserting bands. Each operation is realized by multiplying the Cauchy transform of the measure by some explicit multipliers. We provide necessary estimates on measures and the Green functions after each operation.
Functional Analysis.comment: One reference and Yuditskii's example were added to intro. The scales of Proposition 4.1 were adjusted. Accuracy of arguments were improved

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities for solvable and semisimple Lie groups
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we obtain the sharp constants for Hausdorff--Young inequalities on simply connected, completely solvable Lie groups, and connected real semisimple Lie groups with finite center.

Functional Analysis.title: Lau's Fixed Point Problem for Elementary Amenable Groups and Finite Left Amenable Semigroups
Functional Analysis.summary: Lau's fixed point conjecture is proved for elementary amenable groups. More generally, a weak$^*$-continuous nonexpansive representation of such a group on a nonempty weak$^*$-closed nonexpansive retract of a weak$^*$-compact convex subset $C$ of a dual Banach space has a nonempty common fixed point set that is a nonexpansive retract of $C$. For finite left amenable semigroups, continuity and weak$^*$-closedness of the retract are unnecessary. The argument also leads to a new class of amenable groups with the same retraction property, which contains all elementary amenable groups and may be strictly larger. This class may provide a useful framework for further research on Lau's conjecture. Bruck's theorem is also extended from abelian to elementary amenable group actions on nonexpansive retracts of weakly compact convex sets with the fixed point and conditional fixed point properties, without weak continuity, thus partially answering a longstanding question of Bruck. Several consequences of the theorem are recorded.

Functional Analysis.title: Spectral coincidence and generalized Hua inversion in rings and Banach algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: For additively coupled elements with invertible sum and selected commuting outer inverses, we study coincidence of the core idempotents and inversion of the Hua element. Intertwining forces coincidence for finite-Drazin data in unital rings and for generalized-Drazin data in complex unital Banach algebras. Under coincidence, the output splits into an invertible core and a complementary parallel sum, called the residue, yielding exact criteria for inverse existence and success of the prescribed candidate. Explicit ring examples show that strict generalized-Drazin input inverses need not force coincidence under intertwining, and that a common core with a Harte-quasinilpotent residue need not give a strict output inverse. For rings finite as modules over a commutative central subring with the same identity, we prove intertwining transfer and automatic bicommutation for commuting outer inverses with Harte-quasinilpotent remainders, without Noetherianity. This gives input-core coincidence under intertwining. If the central subring is Noetherian, every Harte-quasinilpotent element also has separated left and right powers. For common-core data in the finite-central class, the candidate is a strict output inverse exactly when the residual parallel sum is Harte-quasinilpotent. In the Banach setting, uniform input spectral gaps characterize continuity of the core and candidate along convergent input pairs, with intertwining and quasinilpotent input remainders at every term and at the limit. The output gap is equivalent when the residues of the sequence and limit are also quasinilpotent. Exact defect identities give local estimates on augmented inverse data. At an exactly intertwined base with invertible coefficient operators, we determine the feasible first-order defect space and its sharp norm constant, with a norm-specific matrix calibration.

Functional Analysis.title: Invariance of Arens module actions on the norm dual of a Riesz-normed f-algebra
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $A$ be an f-algebra and let $V$ be an order ideal of its order dual $A^{\sim}$ that separates the points of $A$. In a comment accompanying a theorem of Huijsmans and de Pagter (J. Funct. Anal. 59 (1984), 41--64), it is stated that the proof of that theorem can easily be adapted to show that the order continuous dual $V_n^{\sim}$ of $V$ is an f-algebra under the Arens multiplication. We show that this statement is false. The Arens multiplication on $V_n^{\sim}$ requires two invariance conditions on $V$, with respect to the module actions of $A$ and of $V_n^{\sim}$, which do not follow from the stated hypotheses and can fail already in the most natural case, where $A$ carries a Riesz norm and $V=A^$ is the norm dual of $A$. We prove that the first condition holds if and only if $A$ is bounded, and that the second holds whenever the Riesz norm is submultiplicative (which forces $A$ to be bounded); in that case $(A^)_n^{\sim}$ is indeed an f-algebra. We then construct a bounded f-algebra of finitely supported real sequences, equipped with a non-submultiplicative Riesz norm, for which the second condition fails, so that the Arens multiplication on $(A^*)_n^{\sim}$ is not even defined. The comment has also been used in the literature to derive a further result, which is false as well. This clarifies the exact scope of the comment.

Functional Analysis.title: Conic Frames, Cosine Measure, and Gaussian Frames
Functional Analysis.summary: Conic combinations play an important role across mathematics in areas such as optimization, non-negative matrix factorization, and sparse coding. Frames which span their underlying space using only conic combinations, known as positive spanning sets or conic frames, are of special interest in derivative free optimization. In particular, sets with large cosine measure, a measure of how spread out the vectors are, are favored. We focus on the asymptotics of the cosine measure of Gaussian frames and present tail bounds in a variety of regimes.

Functional Analysis.title: Primal/Dual Method for the Grothendieck Constant
Functional Analysis.summary: We determine the hundredths digit of the real Grothendieck constant by proving $1.773 \leq K_G \leq 1.7799$. Furthermore, numerical heuristics suggest the estimate $K_G \approx 1.779$. We start by simplifying the Gaussian duality theory of $K_G$, based on Hermite projection games and Krivine rounding schemes. The bounds are obtained by a heuristic primal/dual search for these objects, followed by rigorous {\em certification} of their values. The search and certification are performed using AI tools, and in particular the rigorous certificates are very large (analytical reductions to thousands of numerical inequalities).

Functional Analysis.title: Spaces with maximal monotone convex subdifferentials
Functional Analysis.summary: We characterize the real Hausdorff locally convex spaces on which every proper lower semicontinuous convex function has a maximal monotone convex subdifferential. Equivalent conditions are given in terms of the portability of closed convex sets and identities involving upper envelopes. Among normed spaces, this property is equivalent to completeness; among Fréchet spaces, it is equivalent to normability. We also prove that the property is preserved under products with finite-dimensional spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Numerical Range Geometry and Sharp Inequalities for Positive Block Matrices
Functional Analysis.summary: We give affirmative answers to two questions posed by Bourin and Lee concerning positive block matrices and numerical ranges. We prove that the elliptical width of a fixed off-diagonal block \(X\) is exactly the best correction term in their norm inequality. As a consequence, the corresponding inequality without a correction term holds for every positive completion of \(X\) if and only if \(X\) is essentially Hermitian, proving their Conjecture 3.3. We also show that the radius term in their eigenvalue inequality for normal off-diagonal blocks is best possible at every prescribed eigenvalue level.

Functional Analysis.title: Commutative exact superalgebras and super-modular tensor categories
Functional Analysis.summary:
We consider the theory of commutative exact algebras in braided finite tensor categories
  to superalgebras, motivated by extensions of vertex operator (super)algebras. For a braided category $\C$ let $\B=\C^{\gr}$ be the category of $\mathbb Z/2$-graded objects with the Koszul-signed braiding. Its even-morphism part is the underlying category of the supercategory of Creutzig-Kanade-McRae. A supercommutative superalgebra $A=A_0\oplus A_1$ in $\C$ is the same as a commutative algebra $\bA$ in $\B$, and super-local modules are the local $\bA$-modules. Hence, rigidity, pivotality and ribbon statements are instances of the ordinary theorems of Shimizu-Yadav, with the ribbon condition $θ_{A_0}=\id$, $θ_{A_1}=\varepsilon\,\id$, where $\varepsilon=\pm1$ is fixed by the statistics of the odd part. For $\C$ non-degenerate and $\bA$ haploid and exact we prove that the category of super-local modules is a braided finite tensor category whose Müger center is $\mathsf{sVect}$. It is the centralizer of a fermion in a non-degenerate category obtained by condensing in $\C\boxtimes(\text{toric code})$. If $\C$ is ribbon and $\bA$ is symmetric Frobenius it is ribbon. We give a self-contained treatment of graded simple current algebras and of the free fermion (Ising) example. We compare our formulation with Creutzig-Kanade-McRae and Creutzig-McRae-Shimizu-Yadav.

Functional Analysis.title: Lower bounds for the Kolmogorov widths of global attractors of dissipative systems
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce the notion of a strengthening set in a Hilbert space and prove an exponential lower bound for its Kolmogorov widths. For compact sets containing the origin, the strengthening property is equivalent to the existence of such a bound. As an application, we obtain an exact formula for the widths of the global attractor of a diagonal dissipative system.

Functional Analysis.title: A counterexample to the Jordan tuple conjecture of Ball and Helton
Functional Analysis.summary: This article constructs a pair of bounded commuting 3-symmetric operators with no Jordan-family extension. The operators are coordinate multipliers on a Sobolev space of functions with values in three dimensional complex Euclidean space with an equivalent Hilbert norm. Their quadratic symbol has no operator polynomial factorization, even with an auxiliary target Hilbert space. The construction transfers the nonfactorability of the matrix quadratic used by Russo to the symbol of a commuting 3-symmetric tuple. The factorization approach of McCullough--Russo and Russo then supplies the obstruction to a Jordan-family extension.

Functional Analysis.title: A generic $p$-Wasserstein space is isometrically rigid
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove for any parameter $p \geq 1$ that the $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ of a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X)$ is isometrically rigid, that is, its isometries are precisely the push-forwards of the isometries of $(X,d_X).$ We also study the question whether the isometry class of a $p$-Wasserstein space completely determines the isometry class of the underlying space. We prove for any $p\geq 1$ that for a generic compact metric space $(X,d_X),$ its $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(X,d_X)$ is isometric to another $p$-Wasserstein space $\mathcal{W}_p(Y,d_Y)$ if and only if $(Y,d_Y)$ is isometric to $(X,d_X).$ En route we prove that a stronger property, which we call the Dirac preservation property, is also generic.

Functional Analysis.title: A Kreiss theorem for fractional Cauchy problems with a finite slow component
Functional Analysis.summary: Fractional Cauchy problems with a Caputo derivative of order bounded by one are solved by Mittag-Leffler operator families that lack the semigroup property but remain bounded for classes of sectorial generators, even with spectrum in the right half-plane. To study their transient growth we introduce the fractional Kreiss constant via the Laplace transform of the propagator family. For a closed generator on a Banach space with a time-scale separation and a finite spectral component, that is, a finite-rank projector commuting with the generator whose complement carries a bounded family, we prove that the projected part of the propagator (typically slow spectral part carrying dynamics that is pertinent at mid and long time-scales) is comparable to a deflated Kreiss constant up to a factor linear in the rank, uniformly in fractional order and independently of the dimension. The analytic core of this result is a Bernstein-type inequality for a class of non-rational functions on vertical lines proved by bounding the turning of the derivative. This is a fundamentally different technique from the classical one used in Kreiss theorem for Markov semigroups based on counting intersections of algebraic curves. Importantly, we show that the rank dependence cannot be removed while keeping the Kreiss constant upper bound. Finally, we show that in Hilbert spaces, generators whose numerical range avoids the sector of instability obey the sharp bound of normal operators, which no spectral-set estimate improves. To conclude, we discuss how subdiffusion driven by a self-excited oscillator, the time-fractional Schrödinger equation, and time-changed Markov dynamics illustrate the theory.

Functional Analysis.title: On the ascent and the angle between the null space and the range of elementary operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the angle between the null space and the range of elementary operators of length one or two acting on $\mathcal{B}(\mathscr{X})$, the Banach algebra of all bounded linear operators on a complex Banach space $\mathscr{X}$. For the multiplication operator $μ_{A,B}(X) = AXB$, we characterize positivity of this angle in terms of the corresponding angles for $A$ and $B^*$. For elementary operators of length two $Δ_{\boldsymbol{A},\boldsymbol{B}} = μ_{A_1,B_1} - μ_{A_2,B_2}$, we establish conditions under which the angle is positive, and the ascent of $Δ_{\boldsymbol{A},\boldsymbol{B}}$ equals one. Finally, for a generalized derivation $δ_{A,B}$ and an injective holomorphic function $f$ on a neighborhood of $σ(A)\cupσ(B)$, we show that the angle between the null space and the range of $δ_{f(A),f(B)}$ is positive whenever the angle between the null space and the range of $δ_{A,B}$ is positive.

Functional Analysis.title: Multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for Banach space valued holomorphic functions
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we introduce and study a generalized notion of multidimensional mixed Bohr radii for holomorphic functions defined on the unit ball of the finite-dimensional Minkowski sequence space with values in complex Banach spaces. We first prove that the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius is positive for every non-null bounded linear operator whose norm is sufficiently small relative to the scaling parameter. We then determine the exact asymptotic behavior of the multidimensional mixed Bohr radius for infinite-dimensional Banach spaces of finite cotype and we obtain analogous bounds for spaces without finite cotype. Finally, for concave Banach lattices and summing operators, we prove lower bounds that involve a logarithmic factor. These results connect classical scalar Bohr phenomena with operator-valued and Banach space valued settings, and highlight how the geometry of the spaces and the mapping properties of the operator influence coefficient estimates and their dependence on dimension. Several examples illustrate the consistency of our results with the classical Bohr radius and the sharp Defant--Frerick asymptotics.

Functional Analysis.title: Interpolation, Factorization, and Approximation in the Numerical Radius Unit Ball
Functional Analysis.summary:
We initiate a systematic study of Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and function theory for matrix-valued holomorphic functions on the unit disk taking values in the numerical radius unit ball - a class we term as $ν$-Schur functions.
  In contrast to the operator-norm setting, where commutatnt lifting reduces interpolation to the positivity of a single Pick matrix, we show that a natural one-parameter familty of Pick-type matrices arising from Ando's characterization is necessary but not sufficient for solvability. We overcome this obstruction by establishing two necessary and sufficient solvability criteria. The first is constructive, resting on a factorization of $ν$-Schur function $F=PGQ$ into a classical Schur function $G$ and bounded holomorphic matrix functions $P, Q$ coupled by a boundary condition. This yields an accompanying Choi-Li-type dilation representation. The second is dual and geometric, characterizing solvability via a Nehari-type distance from a cononical model-space interpolant to a subspace determined by the interpolation data.
  Finally, we introduce $ν$-inner functions - $ν$-Schur functions whose non-tangential boundary values lie almost everywhere in the set of extremal numerical contractions - and prove that every non-extremal problem admits a $ν$-inner solution. As a consequence, we obtain a numerical-radius Caratheodory approximation theorem: $ν$-inner functions are dense in the $ν$-Schur class under the compact-open topology.

Functional Analysis.title: Matricial stability and central corrections for generalized Jordan derivations on amenable $C^*$-algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: We study norm stability of third-type generalized Jordan identities, allowing their auxiliary maps to be arbitrary. A canonical normalization eliminates these witnesses with a factor of four. For a unital $C^*$-algebra and a unital contractive Banach bimodule, the zero-defect maps are precisely sums of a derivation and multiplication by a central module element. We characterize scalar stability by the closed range of the normalized Jordan-defect operator. For operator bimodules, two explicit $2\times2$ tests recover an ordered Leibniz defect and a commutator defect. If the algebra has an approximate diagonal bounded by $M$ and the module is weak$^*$ closed, these tests yield approximation by an inner derivation plus a central multiplier with error at most $8M$ times the normalized matrix defect. The corresponding completely bounded estimate holds at all matrix levels. For full matrix algebras the constant is $8$, independently of their size, and weak$^*$ closedness is unnecessary. When the map vanishes at the identity, the constants improve to $2M$ and $2$, respectively.

Functional Analysis.title: Absolutely Summing Toeplitz operators on Fock spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
For $1\le p<\infty$, let $F^p_\varphi$ be the Fock spaces on ${\mathbb C}^n$ with the weight function $\varphi$ that \(\varphi \in {\mathcal{C}}^{2}\left( {\mathbb{C}}^{n}\right)\) is real-valued and satisfies
  $
  m{ω}_{0} \leq d{d}^{c}\varphi \leq M{ω}_{0}
  $
  for two positive constants \(m\) and \(M\), \({ω}_{0} = d{d}^{c}{\left| z\right| }^{2}\) is the Euclidean Kähler form on \({\mathbb{C}}^{n}\), \({d}^{c} = \frac{\sqrt{-1}}{4}\left( {\bar{\partial } - \partial }\right)\). In this paper, we completely characterize those positive Borel measure $μ$ on ${\mathbb C}^n$ so that the induced Toeplitz operators $T_μ$ is $r$-summing on $F_{\varphi}^{p}$ for $r \ge 1$.
Functional Analysis.comment: Updated to the accept version, corrected typos, results unchanged

Functional Analysis.title: The product of a weak Asplund space and a one-dimensional space is a weak Asplund space
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we prove that if $X$ is a weak Asplund space, then $X\times\mathbb R$ is also a weak Asplund space. This resolves an open problem posed by D. G. Larman and R. R. Phelps in 1979 (J. London Math. Soc. (2) 20 (1979), 115-127). The proof combines the Banach-Mazur game, properties of maximal monotone operators, and the G$\mathrm{\hat{a}}$teaux differentiability of Minkowski functionals. Specifically, we introduce an iterative perturbed Minkowski convex cone approximation game method, and establish a theoretical framework to verify the existence of dense differentiability sets for convex functions on product spaces. By relating the properties of convex functions on the base space and the product space via projection mappings, and constructing dense $G_δ$ subsets using sequences of dense open cones, we demonstrate that the product space satisfies the definition of a weak Asplund space.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Non-homogeneous parabolic conormal boundary problem with singular-degenerate coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study non-homogeneous conormal boundary value problems for a class of divergence-form parabolic equations whose volumetric heat-capacity coefficients belong to a Muckenhoupt class of weights. Consequently, the equations exhibit singular, degenerate, or simultaneously singular-degenerate behavior. Under smallness conditions on the partial mean oscillation of the diffusion coefficients and the weighted mean oscillation of the volumetric heat-capacity coefficient, we establish regularity estimates, existence, and uniqueness results in appropriate weighted Sobolev spaces. To obtain these results, we employ the level-set argument introduced by Caffarelli and Peral. We also establish weighted parabolic cylinders, weighted inequalities, and a weighted Aubin-Lions compactness theorem, which are essential tools in our analysis.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Almost minimizing Yang$-$Mills fields: log-epiperimetric inequality, non-concentration, and uniqueness of tangents
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a direct log-epiperimetric inequality for Yang$-$Mills fields in arbitrary dimension and we leverage it to prove uniqueness of tangent cones with isolated singularity for almost energy minimizing connections and $ω$-ASD connections (where $ω$ is not necessarily closed) satisfying some suitable regularity and non-concentration assumptions. En route to this we establish a Luckhaus type lemma for connections to exclude curvature concentration along blow-up sequences.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Large Gap between Galerkin Errors with and without Mesh-Uniform Regularity for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We compare two cubic Hermite Galerkin semidiscretizations of the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation. They use the same trial space. The first is the weighted scheme considered in our previous paper (arXiv:2610.39269), called the W-scheme. It has mesh-uniform regularity: the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit Crandall-Pazy regularity and Kato smoothing, with bounds uniform in the mesh size $h$. The second is the standard Galerkin method in $L^2$, called the S-scheme. It has no mesh-uniform regularity. For the W-scheme, the full error and the ordering error converge at an algebraic rate in $h$, uniformly on $[t_0,\infty)$ times small balls of $L^2$ for any fixed $t_0>0$. They are bounded by $Ch^p\varepsilon$ and $Ch^p\varepsilon^2$, respectively, where $\varepsilon$ is the size of the datum and $p>0$. We prove that neither bound holds for the S-scheme by using exact high-frequency spurious eigenpairs of the S-scheme. The existence of such eigenpairs for meshes with at least 512 elements and the failure of both bounds have proofs checked by Lean 4. The only premise is the mesh-uniform Crandall-Pazy estimate of the W-scheme (arXiv:2610.39269). Computations compare the two schemes on unit-norm data built from these eigenfunctions, on 512, 1024 and 2048 elements. The full error of the S-scheme stays at $4.6\times10^{-2}$. That of the W-scheme is at most $2.2\times10^{-9}$. The ordering error of the S-scheme stays at $9.6\times10^{-6}$. That of the W-scheme falls from $2.3\times10^{-9}$ to $1.4\times10^{-10}$. Their ratio grows from $4.2\times10^3$ to $6.6\times10^4$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 57 pages, 2 figures. v2 adds Lean 4 proofs of the main results. Ancillary files: Lean 4 sources, programs and outputs

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global strong solutions and large-time behavior for the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson system with general bulk viscosity and Navier slip boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The global existence of a unique strong solution to the two-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with Navier slip boundary conditions is established in a smooth bounded domain that may be multiply connected. Arbitrarily large initial data and vacuum are allowed, and the positive doping profile may have large spatial variations. The bulk viscosity satisfies a logarithmic derivative bound and a growth condition on its primitive, including every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with a logarithmic gain larger than one half. Time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponential convergence to the nonconstant hydrostatic state are obtained. For strictly positive initial density, uniform positivity and exponential convergence to the hydrostatic state in higher Sobolev norms are proved. An initial vacuum point persists and causes exponential growth of density gradients.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $p$-harmonic polynomials
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that every real polynomial $p$-harmonic function on $\Rn$ is affine when $n\ge3$ and $p\ge n-1/13$. The proof uses the Bernstein--Szegő inequality on great circles and a deficit estimate at the first Chebyshev node.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The Lean code and an explanation of the formalization process are available at https://github.com/na0b/pharmonicpoly-lean

Analysis of PDEs.title: Inverse Boundary Value Problems for a Coupled Semilinear Klein-Gordon System
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This article addresses the coefficient identification inverse problem for a coupled nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation with cubic nonlinearity. More precisely, we consider a coupled nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation in a bounded cylinder contained in $\mathbb{R}^{1+\ell}$, where $ \ell\geq 2$, and establish the unique recovery of the time-independent coefficients appearing in both the zeroth-order perturbation and nonlinearity term from both full and partial boundary measurements of the solution. The unique recovery of zeroth-order coefficients is obtained via first-order linearization; however, the nonlinearity coefficients are recovered using the higher-order linearization.
  Finally using the unique continuation principle, we establish the unique identification of the coefficients from the partial boundary measurements of the solution.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity of solutions to complex Monge-Ampère equations in big classes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the non-pluripolar complex Monge-Ampère equation in an arbitrary big class on a compact Kähler manifold. Under a weighted Laplacian lower bound on the log density, we obtain local $C^{2,α}$ regularity on the part of the ample locus where the data satisfy the stated hypotheses. A second criterion based on a quasi-plurisubharmonic decomposition gives similar regularity. In particular, a smooth positive density gives a smooth solution on the ample locus. None of these regularity results require nefness of the background class, resolving positively a question of Dinew, Guedj, and Zeriahi.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces
  with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles.
  The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a new relative BFK type gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to Lück and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles and discuss some extremal properties.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Well-posedness of compressible $2D$ nonlinear transport equations and quasiconformal maps
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove uniqueness of solutions to a class of nonlinear transport equations in the plane, for which the velocity field is obtained as the convolution of the classical Cauchy kernel with the unknown. Even though the initial datum is bounded and compactly supported, the velocity field may have unbounded divergence. The proof relies on the theory of quasiconformal mappings.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularity of velocity averages in kinetic equations with heterogeneity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This study investigates the regularity of kinetic equations with spatial heterogeneity. Recent progress has shown that velocity averages of weak solutions $h$ in $L^p$ ($p>1$) are strongly $L^1_{\text{loc}}$ compact under the natural non-degeneracy condition. We establish regularity estimates for equations with an $\boldsymbol{x}$-dependent drift vector $\mathfrak{f} = \mathfrak{f}(\boldsymbol{x}, \boldsymbolλ)$, which satisfies a quantitative version of the non-degeneracy condition. We prove that $(t,\boldsymbol{x}) \mapsto \int ρ(\boldsymbolλ) h(t,\boldsymbol{x},\boldsymbolλ)\, d\boldsymbolλ$, for any sufficiently regular $ρ(\cdot)$, belongs to the fractional Sobolev space $W_{\text{loc}}^{β,r}$, for some regularity $β\in (0,1)$ and integrability $r \geq 1$ exponents. While such estimates have long been known for $\boldsymbol{x}$-independent drift vectors $\mathfrak{f}=\mathfrak{f}(\boldsymbolλ)$, this is the first quantitative regularity estimate in a general heterogeneous setting. As an application, we obtain a regularity estimate for entropy solutions to heterogeneous conservation laws with nonlinear flux and $L^\infty$ initial data.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: We have modified the assumptions to accommodate nonsmooth drift throughout the paper. We have included two applications: (1) multidimensional scalar conservation laws with discontinuous flux and (2) a regularity result for the density variable in isentropic gas dynamics, given a regularity assumption on the velocity

Analysis of PDEs.title: Unique continuation for the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove a unique continuation property for eigenstates of the Pauli-Fierz Hamiltonian, viewed as functions of the electron configuration with values in the spin-photon space. The vector potential may lie in $L^6_\mathrm{loc}$, with its divergence, curl, and the scalar potential in $L^p_\mathrm{loc}$ for some $p>2$. As an application, we prove a Hohenberg-Kohn theorem at positive coupling strength: the spin-summed ground-state density and combined current density determine the external potentials up to a gauge transformation and an additive constant.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large diameter growth for vortex patches
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every $N>0$, the 2D incompressible Euler equation admits a smooth, simply connected vortex patch initially contained in the unit disk whose diameter exceeds $N$ at some finite time. We discover a point-vortex mechanism in which a bounded motion of three equal positive vortices drives a passive particle outward through successive transitions. A finite-time point-vortex approximation transfers the resulting separation to a single simply connected patch.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global dynamics of large smooth solutions to the two-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system with Navier-slip boundary conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions containing vacuum to the two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations with bulk viscosity depending on the density, in smooth bounded simply connected domains, subject to the Navier-slip boundary conditions. Without any restriction on the size of initial data, we obtain time-uniform density and velocity bounds and exponentialconvergence to equilibrium in Sobolev spaces for the density and velocity. Moreover an initial vacuum point will persist and force the exponential growth of density gradients.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stratonovich Waves Driven by Space-Time Gaussian Noise
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Motivated by Xia Chen's moment conjecture, we determine the exact second-moment asymptotics of the Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model in dimensions $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, driven by a centered Gaussian noise with temporal covariance $|s-t|^{-α_0}$ and an even, nonnegative, positive-definite tempered Radon spatial covariance $Γ$ homogeneous of order $-α$, where $0<α_0<1$, $0<α<d$ or $α=d=1$, and $α+α_0<2$. For initial displacement one and velocity zero, our main result is that $T^{-κ}\log\mathbb{E}u^2(T,x)$ converges, for every fixed $x$, to a constant $C_2(Γ,α_0)$, where $κ=(4-α-α_0)/(3-α)$. The constant is given by an intrinsic variational formula: a supremum over nonnegative smooth compactly supported space-time controls of twice the time integral of the square root of a Rayleigh value built from the covariance mean, minus half of the covariance variance. The variational class includes controls that do not separate in time and space, and the formula retains the original covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and Gaussian cost. The constant is positive and finite when $Γ\neq0$. An independent upper bound establishes finiteness at the scale $T^κ$. The identification of the constant combines Gaussian phase operators, convergence from the regularized noise, estimates uniform in the spatial localization radius, and finite optimization with nonnegative Gram entries. We also bound the constant through spatial energies and occupation measures, with explicit bounds for spatial white noise in one dimension. The work was developed with AI assistance; the proofs have not yet been checked line by line by a human reader, and a public verification ledger records the status of each result.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Version 1.0.0; 476 pages. Source, development history and verification ledger: https://github.com/chenle02/stratonovich-ham-second-moment (release v1.0.0). Lean companion: https://github.com/chenle02/stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean (release v0.10.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24295453). Developed with AI assistance; see AI-USE-STATEMENT.md in the repository

Analysis of PDEs.title: Fine properties of nonlinear potentials and a unified perspective on monotonicity formulas
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We rigorously show that a large family of monotone quantities along the weak inverse mean curvature flow is the limit case of the corresponding ones along the level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials. Such monotone quantities include Willmore and Minkowski-type functionals on Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature.
