In $3$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we also recover the monotonicity of the Hawking mass and its nonlinear potential theoretic counterparts. This unified view is built on a refined analysis of $p$-capacitary potentials. We prove that they strongly converge in $W^{1,q}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ as $p\to 1^+$ to the inverse mean curvature flow and their level sets are curvature varifolds. Finally, we also deduce a Gauss-Bonnet-type theorem for level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 52 pages. To appear: Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quantifying Concentration Phenomena of Mean-Field Transformers in the Low-Temperature Regime
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Transformers with self-attention modules as their core components have become an integral architecture in modern large language and foundation models. In this paper, we study the evolution of tokens in deep encoder-only transformers at inference time which is described in the large-token limit by a mean-field continuity equation. Leveraging ideas from the convergence analysis of interacting multi-particle systems, with particles corresponding to tokens, we prove that the token distribution rapidly concentrates onto the push-forward of the initial distribution under a projection map induced by the key, query, and value matrices, and remains metastable for moderate times. Specifically, we show that the Wasserstein distance of the two distributions scales like $\sqrt{{\log(β+1)}/β}\exp(Ct)+\exp(-ct)$ in terms of the temperature parameter $β^{-1}\to 0$ and inference time $t\geq 0$. For the proof, we establish Lyapunov-type estimates for the zero-temperature equation, identify its limit as $t\to\infty$, and employ a stability estimate in Wasserstein space together with a quantitative Laplace principle to couple the two equations. Our result implies that for time scales of order $\logβ$, which correspond to the early-phase behavior most relevant for practical finite-depth models, the token distribution concentrates at the identified limiting distribution. Numerical experiments confirm this and, beyond that, complement our theory by showing that for finite $β$ and large $t$ the dynamics enter a different terminal phase, dominated by the spectrum of the value matrix.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Conference: https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/loc/paris/poster/149032 Funded by the European Union's HORIZON-MSCA-2021-DN-01-01, through ModConFlex ("Modelling and control of flexible structures interacting with fluids"; No. 101073558; DOI: 10.3030/101073558). Code: https://github.com/albertalcalde/mean-field-transformer-concentration, code DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23726583

Analysis of PDEs.title: Shell crossing and the dynamical formation of thin shells in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we show that shell crossing in the collapse of self-gravitating relativistic dust in spherical symmetry can be understood as dynamical formation of a thin shell of dust. More precisely, we consider the spherically symmetric Einstein-dust system in double null coordinates (E-d), for which first singularities with area radius bounded away from zero are known as 'shell crossing' singularities. We show that there exists a weak solution of (E-d), in which a thin shell of dust forms, extending beyond any 'non-degenerate' first shell crossing singularity of a smooth 'collapsing' solution of (E-d). This local extension is unique in the class of piecewise smooth solutions of (E-d) satisfying a 'determinism condition'.
  We then consider the physical problem of smooth data for (E-d) on an initial hypersurface diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3$, containing a collapsing dust cloud. We show that, for generic such initial data, there exists a maximal globally hyperbolic piecewise smooth development satisfying a 'propagation condition' (stronger than the determinism condition). The development may contain an arbitrary (finite) number of thin shells which can moreover merge. All shell crossing singularities are 'resolved' and the area radius extends continuously to zero at any first singularity of the maximal development. We note that, for an open set of initial data in the smooth topology, as shown by Christodoulou, a Cauchy horizon emanates from a central 'shell-focussing' singularity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sobolev theory for the inverse problem of time-dependent density functional theory on the torus
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We show that, given a sufficiently regular time-dependent density, there exists a unique potential such that the Schrödinger equation with this external potential has the prescribed one-particle density. We treat densities that are twice differentiable in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space; the resulting potentials are continuous in time and of finite Sobolev regularity in space. Our method of proof is to rewrite the problem as a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a loss of derivatives, which we in turn handle with a completion-of-the-square argument. This is a refinement of our recent work [Lauritsen, Lewin, and Oldenburg, arXiv:2609.08984], which handled this loss of derivatives using the Cauchy-Kovalevskaya theorem and treated analytic-in-space densities and potentials.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global solvability, regularity and exponential convergence in a quasilinear chemotaxis-haptotaxis system with mostly repulsive signal production
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Motivated by biological and mathematical viewpoints, we systematically investigate the global dynamics of a quasilinear chemotaxis haptotaxis system with mostly repulsive signal production. We show unconditional 2D boundedness, blow up prevention for parabolic-elliptic-ODE case in nD, small data boundedness and exponential convergence under endpoint Lebesgue smallness, and 3D weak-solution eventual regularity. Our findings extend the corresponding repulsive chemotaxis only theory to the chemotaxis haptotaxis setting and demonstrate a positive effect of chemo-repulsion on global dynamics.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The weak-type (1,1) bound for the Hardy--Littlewood maximal function is $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove a weak-type $(1,1)$ estimate for the centered Hardy--Littlewood maximal function with respect to Euclidean balls with dimensional dependence $O(\sqrt{n} \log n)$. This improves the order of growth in the classical $O(n)$ estimate of Stein and Strömberg. The proof goes through a pointwise bound of the Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator by the heat maximal operator with $\sqrt{n}$ loss. The key technical aspect of our result is an improvement of the weak-type bound for the heat maximal operator from $O(\sqrt{n})$ to $O(\log n)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Moser--Trudinger inequalities and the complex Monge--Ampère mean field equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study sharp Moser--Trudinger inequalities for the complex Monge--Ampère energy. On the unit ball, we determine the optimal energy coefficient and additive constant in the logarithmic Moser--Trudinger inequality. We deduce subcritical Moser--Trudinger inequalities in exponential form with explicit bounds proportional to $\varepsilon^{-1}$, where $\varepsilon$ is the relative distance to the critical coefficient. The proof establishes radial symmetry and uniqueness for the associated mean field equation by showing that every smooth solution has constant boundary normal derivative. This gives existence and uniqueness precisely for total masses $0<Λ<[2π(n+1)]^n$, proving Berman--Berndtsson's conjecture. We also establish smoothness of bounded pluripotential and finite-energy solutions. Domain monotonicity transfers the exponential estimates and the optimal logarithmic energy coefficient to bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Boundary concentration and minimum-mass bifurcation for inverse-power absorption
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For \(Δu=λu^{-p}\), \(λ>0\), \(0<p<1\), we obtain a uniform half-plane profile law at moving points along smooth boundary arcs. It gives the exact local energy constant \(8p(1-p)/(1+p)^2\) for the secant potential at a common zero slope. On a one-corner domain, positive ordinary slopes at the minimum Martin mass \(m_*\) yield exactly two solutions at each nearby larger mass, with square-root displacement in the Martin norm. On these domains, for \(p\ne1/3\), there are at most two solutions at each nearby larger mass without a slope hypothesis, and just one if the endpoint energy kernel is trivial. We construct flat-tangent Lipschitz domains with an explicit slope loss and a logarithmic correction. The first construction gives a saturated endpoint with sharp Martin response of order \((m-m_*)^{1/(1+p)}\) and a compact energy operator. For \(p\ge1/2\) a second construction has positive local energy concentration and a strict global energy gap. As a result, we substantially advance the solvability and establish a sharp classification for the negative-power absorption equation in the Mazya 50 problem at the minimal mass endpoint, largely resolving the existence and regularity issues.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Characterization of parabolic rectifiability in terms of Jones' square function
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We show that a measure $μ$ in $\mathbb{R}^n \times \mathbb{R}$ equipped with the parabolic metric is rectifiable (in the parabolic sense) if and only if the Jones' square function is finite $μ$-almost everywhere. This square function is constructed using the parabolic version of the Jones' beta numbers, which control how close $μ$ is to being supported in time-independent planes (these planes are the paradigmatic example of parabolic rectifiable set). Our only background assumption is that $μ$ has positive and finite densities (qualitatively) almost everywhere.
  A key feature of our proof is the use of a parabolic version of the Reifenberg parametrization theorem, which in the Euclidean setting is due to David and Toro (MAMS, 2012), and has recently been extended to the parabolic setting by Hoffman, Mourgoglou and the fourth author. In the latter work, the authors construct a bi-Hölder map. Here, under an additional summability condition, we improve this construction to obtain a parabolic regular bi-Lipschitz map. This improvement in regularity plays a crucial role in our arguments.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Convergence of a Parametric Symmetric Galerkin Boundary Element Method for the Mullins-Sekerka Flow
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove convergence of the fully discrete parametric scheme for the two-phase Mullins-Sekerka flow of a closed curve in the plane. The scheme combines piecewise linear parametric curves, a curvature discretization of Barrett--Garcke--Nürnberg type and a symmetric Galerkin boundary element approximation of the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. For a smooth solution whose curves satisfy a capacity condition, a uniform parameter mesh of size $h$, a constant time step $τ$ and exact boundary element integrals, we show that the discrete curves stay regular and embedded, and that their distance to the exact curves in the topology $W^{1,\infty}$, after reparametrization by arclength, tends to zero in the first order of the time-step size $τ$ whenever the mesh size $h$ is bounded by $c_0τ^2$ for some $c_0$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global strong solutions and large-time behavior for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with general bulk viscosity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions to the two-dimensional repulsive Navier--Stokes--Poisson system with general density-dependent bulk viscosity is established for arbitrarily large initial data allowing vacuum. The periodic problem and the Cauchy problem with a positive constant background are treated under a common growth condition on the viscosity primitive. The coefficient class includes every superlinear power law and near-linear laws with logarithmic gains. A density upper bound and low-order estimates, uniform in time and independent of a positive density lower bound, are obtained without an initial acceleration compatibility condition. Exponential relaxation is proved on the torus, and qualitative convergence to equilibrium is established in the whole space under a finite electric energy condition and without spatial moment assumptions. If the initial density vanishes at a point, the vacuum persists and density gradients become unbounded as time tends to infinity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Scalar Entropy and Source Terms in Harmonic Ricci Flow on Surfaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The modified scalar curvature $S=R-α|\nablaφ|^2$ satisfies a reaction--diffusion equation with a nonnegative source $Q$ under harmonic Ricci flow on a surface. The relative entropy of $|S|$ need not decrease for either sign of $S$. At a nonzero constant initial value its second time derivative is the spatial variance integral of $Q$, divided by $|S|$. We construct closed examples of both signs with spatially varying tension norm. For $S<0$, normalizing by the mass of $-S$ gives an exact covariance threshold for decay and a sufficient bound in terms of the variances of $\frac{Q}{-S}$ and $-S$, the scalar mass and density bounds, and the first positive eigenvalue. On a torus this variance bound gives decay even when the covariance is strictly negative. For $S>0$ we retain the source and boundary flux in the Hamilton square formula. In the fixed harmonic free-boundary disk case the source vanishes, and equality for a nonconstant map forces $S$ to be constant. The appendices give the boundary terms for the coupled Perelman functionals.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Pohozaev identities and Liouville theorems for $L$-tension energies on manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study autonomous energies $B(φ,e,\|τ_L\|^2/2)$ for a general Lagrangian $L=L(y,r)$. The scaling derivative $\widehat L=2rL'$ determines the trace of the stress tensor and a vector-field identity on Riemannian domains. For homogeneous $L=a(y)(2r)^{p/2}/p$, the divergence term in this trace vanishes when $p=m$. A conformal vector field with a strictly signed conformal factor then gives $L$-harmonicity for positive mixed tension powers, under explicit integrability and flux conditions. This applies, in particular, to hyperbolic space. On complete gradient Ricci solitons with bounded Ricci curvature, a separate cutoff argument gives a global identity for general $L$. On the cigar and on Euclidean space, direct metric variations give second-order boundary criteria that also cover tension powers $1<q<2$. The applications include target weights and the fourth-power case. Examples distinguish the annular condition from global first-derivative integrability and show why scalar growth bounds or finite tension energy alone do not imply vanishing.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Time-decay rates toward viscous shock waves for the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study small H^2(R) perturbations of a fixed weak viscous 3-shock for the one-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes-Fourier system. For each fixed initial perturbation, the error from the shifted profile in the uniform norm and the shift velocity are o(t^{-1/4}). Nearby stationary profiles give spatial estimates in terms of the time derivative. Estimates along the characteristics bound the perturbation at time t by the dissipation on [t/2, t]. The exponent 1/4 is sharp for a uniform bound on the small H^2 ball.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform boundedness and exponential stabilization in a planar degenerate migration-consumption system with logistic source
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the no-flux problem for a planar taxis-type migration-consumption system with logistic source, where the motility function $φ$ satisfies $φ(0)=0$ and suitably generalizes the prototype $φ(s)=s^α$ with $α\ge1$. For every fixed $b>0$ and without smallness assumptions, we prove uniform $L^\infty(Ω)\times W^{1,\infty}(Ω)$-boundedness. For all $α\ge1$, we further show that $v\to0$ exponentially in $W^{1,\infty}(Ω)$ and $u\to \frac{a}{b}$ exponentially in $L^\infty(Ω)$, with an explicit admissible rate; this quantitative stabilization complements the global classical solvability and the $L^2$--bound established by Wang and Mu (2025). The proof relies on a weighted Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality and a reciprocal--power functional adapted to both the degeneracy and the dissipative structure of the signal equation. These results show that quadratic logistic damping drives the system toward a homogeneous state even though diffusion degenerates at $v=0$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 32 pages. Title and abstract revised; exposition improved. The exponential stabilization result is extended from $α>1$ to $α\ge1$, and convergence is strengthened to the $L^\infty$ norm, with explicit admissible decay rates

Analysis of PDEs.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions II
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This is the second of two papers on isolated boundary singularities of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We construct positive solutions that violate the critical upper bound, proving that the dimension ranges in Part I are sharp. For general smooth metrics, the conformal metric can be incomplete near the singularity in every dimension $n\ge18$, and complete in every dimension $n\ge19$. For Euclidean domains with smooth boundary, both types exist for $n\ge23$. We also construct both types for metrics with totally geodesic boundary in dimensions $n\ge35$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlinear Stability of Spiky Patterns for a Three-Dimensional Chemotaxis--Consumption Model with Signal-Dependent Motilities
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We prove the nonlinear asymptotic stability of one-dimensional spiky steady states for a three-dimensional chemotaxis--consumption system with signal-dependent motility $w^p$ ($p>0$, $α\ge2$) in the half-cylinder $Ω=\mathbb{R}_+\times\mathbb{T}^2$. The cell density satisfies a no-flux boundary condition at $x_1=0$, while the chemical concentration satisfies $w(0,x',t)=b>0$ and vanishes as $x_1\to+\infty$. For any prescribed steady-state cell mass $λ>0$, we show that any sufficiently small compatible initial perturbation with zero mass generates a unique global strong solution that converges to the spiky steady state in $L^\infty(Ω)$, with the chemical concentration converging uniformly relative to the steady profile, namely $\|w(\cdot,t)/W-1\|_{L^\infty(Ω)}\to0$ as $t\to\infty$.
  The stability analysis for an arbitrarily large steady mass $λ>0$ in three dimensions involves four main difficulties: the algebraic degeneracy of the diffusion coefficient $W^p(x_1)\sim (1+x_1)^{-2/(α-1)}$ as $x_1\to\infty$, the $O(λ)$ linear coupling between the density perturbation and the chemical logarithmic gradient on the transversal nonzero modes, the nonlinear boundary conditions at $x_1=0$ produced by the Hopf--Cole transformation, and the different spatial weights required across derivative orders. We resolve these difficulties by introducing the algebraic weights $(ω_1,ω_2,ω_3)=(W^{-p}U^{-1},U^{-1},W^pU^{-1})$, coupling a weighted Neumann inverse on the transversal nonzero modes with the scalar logarithmic potential $Ψ+q$ to cancel the $O(λ)$ linear coupling terms exactly, performing tangential and time-differentiated weighted energy estimates whose boundary traces vanish identically at $x_1=0$, and closing the time-derivative energy before recovering the full weighted Hessian dissipation from the parabolic system.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global rigidity and the Hessian energy identity for the one-phase Bernoulli problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that every entire classical stable solution of the one-phase Bernoulli problem in dimension five or six is one-dimensional. In dimensions three through six, we establish an exact interior identity for the scale-invariant Hessian energy of sequences with bounded Morse index. Hence, the global stability conjecture is solved.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Fine spectral analysis of concentrating solutions to Brezis--Nirenberg problem in dimension $4$
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This paper is devoted to the qualitative properties and Morse indices of concentrating solutions to the Brezis--Nirenberg problem \[
  -Δu=u^3+εu, \quad u>0, \quad\text{in }Ω,
  \qquad
  u=0 \quad \text{on }\partialΩ, \] where $Ω\subset\mathbb R^4$ is a smooth bounded domain, $ε>0$ is small parameter. For a family of $m$-bubble solutions with distinct interior concentration points and comparable concentration scales, we establish precise asymptotic expansions for the first $6m$ eigenvalues of the associated linearized eigenvalue problem and determine the corresponding eigenfunction profiles.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Interior curvature estimates for convex solutions of a prescribed curvature quotient equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this note, we prove a priori interior curvature bounds for convex solutions to an elliptic Weingarten curvature quotient equation. The proof avoids integral estimates, doubling inequalities and compactness arguments. It relies on a concavity inequality for the equation operator and a novel choice of the auxiliary function to carry out an elementary maximum-principle argument. As an application, we obtain interior curvature bounds for convex solutions of a prescribed special Lagrangian curvature equation in dimensions three and four.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: v4: a few more typos fixed; to appear

Analysis of PDEs.title: Shape design for degenerate elliptic Equation with degenerate boundary and its application to quantitativeweak unique continuation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
This paper investigates the unique continuation property (UCP) for a class of degenerate elliptic equations of the form $-\text{div}(A\nabla u) = λu$ in a bounded domain $Ω\s \mathbb{R}^N$ with Dirichlet boundary conditions. While unique continuation is well-established for uniformly elliptic operators via Carleman estimates or frequency-function methods, spatial degeneracy introduces substantial analytical obstacles in higher dimensions, particularly due to the lack of sufficient regularity for weak solutions and the breakdown of classical boundary integration-by-parts identities.
  To overcome these challenges, we develop an alternative framework based on the shape design (shape optimization) method under suitable structural assumptions. We highlight the fundamental distinction between qualitative and quantitative unique continuation in the degenerate setting. While qualitative UCP can sometimes be adapted from classical arguments, quantitative UCP requires explicit estimates that control the behavior of the solution throughout the domain by its behavior on a sub-domain. By integrating the shape design approach with a compatible weighted Hardy inequality, we establish new quantitative estimates and unique continuation results for higher-dimensional degenerate elliptic operators, bypassing the stringent regularity requirements of traditional methods.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $d\in\mathbb N$, $p\in(1,\infty)$, $p':=\frac{p}{p-1}$, and $s\in(0,\min\{1+\frac1p,\frac dp\})$. For an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, let $F:=\mathbb{R}^d\setminusΩ$. For any $α\in(0,1]$ and $x\inΩ$, let \begin{align*} d_{α,s,p}(x) :=\inf\left\{r\in(0,\infty): \frac{\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{F\cap B(x,r)})} {\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{B(x,r)})}\geα\right\}, \end{align*} where $\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}$ is the capacity associated with the fractional Sobolev energy $[\,\cdot\,]_{s,p}^p$. In this article, we prove that there exists a positive constant $C$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $p$, such that, for any $α\in(0,1]$ and $u\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(Ω)$, \begin{align*} \int_Ω\frac{|u(x)|^p}{d_{α,s,p}(x)^{sp}}\,dx \le Cα^{-p'}[u]_{s,p}^p. \end{align*} We also show that both the exponent $p'$ in $α^{-p'}$ as $α\to0^+$ over the class of all open sets and the range $s\in(0,1+\frac1p)$ within $sp<d$ are sharp. Our proofs use variational minimization, equilibrium measures on trees, and weighted Hardy inequalities.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters. The proof combines a transverse heteroclinic connection and invariant multicones with spectral points from periodic realizations. A strict geometric window permits integer scale matching, and the required parameter inequalities are verified by exact rational arithmetic.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Observability and Domain Shape Design for a Class of Degenerate Schrödinger Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper investigates boundary observability for a class of two dimensional degenerate Schrodinger equations on the unit square. The diffusion matrix has diagonal entries x1 to the power alpha1 and x2 to the power alpha2, where both parameters lie between zero and one. Since the underlying degenerate elliptic operator lacks global H2 regularity, classical Rellich space time multiplier and hidden regularity arguments cannot be applied directly to weak solutions. We introduce a truncation parameter delta and construct uniformly elliptic problems on nondegenerate subdomains. Weighted Poincare inequalities, Sturm Liouville nodal properties, spectral decomposition, and Hilbert tensor product techniques yield an operator resolvent approximation and strong convergence of the state solutions and their boundary normal derivatives in suitable energy and trace spaces. Passing to the limit in the parameterized multiplier identities gives a boundary observability inequality for the original degenerate system on the nondegenerate active boundaries. When alpha1 is less than or equal to alpha2, the minimal observation time is 4 times the square root of 2 divided by the product of 1 minus alpha1 and 2 minus alpha2. This time tends to infinity as alpha1 tends to one, whereas it tends to 2 times the square root of 2 in the nondegenerate limit.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Potential theory for double phase equations with measure data
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop a potential theory for elliptic equations with double phase growth and signed measure data. We establish existence of solutions obtained by approximation, pointwise bounds for the flux in terms of linear Riesz potentials, and nonlinear potential estimates for the solution in terms of generalized Wolff potentials; a quantitative decay estimate for the flux excess is the main ingredient and also yields a potential criterion for gradient continuity. The results cover both singular and degenerate equations, including the range $p>n$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Convection--diffusion equations with non-integrable initial data
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We characterize the long-time behaviour of solutions to the convection--diffusion equation $u_t-u_{xx}+(|u|^{q-1}u)_x=0$, $q>1$, with initial data behaving like a non-integrable power at infinity, $|x|^γu_0(x)\to k_\pm$ as $x\to\pm\infty$, $0<γ\le1$. The decay rate in time and the asymptotic profile depend on the strength of convection as compared to the size of the solution at infinity, leading either to a convective behaviour or to a diffusive one. When the nonlinear convection dominates, we observe an enhanced dissipation effect: the decay rate in time is faster than for the purely diffusive equation with the same initial datum. For $0<γ<1$ we obtain the limit self-similar profile, which, in the convective regime, has one shock, or two when $k_+k_-<0$ and $|k_+|>\eps(γ,q)|k_-|$, where $\eps(γ,q)\in(0,1)$ is an explicit threshold. For $γ=1$ logarithmic corrections appear, and the limit is a multiple of the heat kernel if $q>2$ and an $N$-wave if $1<q\le2$. The convergence takes place in the spaces to which the datum belongs, and not only on expanding sets. The main new ingredients are an Oleĭnik type estimate of Hölder type valid for $q\geq 2$ and a far-field estimate, uniform in time, showing that beyond the self-similar region the solution is still described by its own datum.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities via Optimal Transport and Study of Equality Cases
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities using the theory of optimal transportation, more precisely an anisotropic version of Caffarelli's contraction theorem. Furthermore, we provide a full picture concerning the issues of finiteness of the Brascamp-Lieb constant and of the existence of Gaussian extremizers, and completely determine all optimizers. The characterization of equality cases requires several new ideas to deal with difficulties, which do not appear for the non-regularized Brascamp-Lieb datum. Finally, we give applications retrieving Brascamp-Lieb-type inequalities with respect to the Gaussian measure and a regularized hypercontractivity inequality.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 64 pages, added a new proof of the fact that dual extremizable Brascamp-Lieb data are Gaussian extremizable, expanded technical details, corrected typos and mistakes, improved the structure of Section 4, added references

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Weak-Type Inequalities for Scalar and Matrix Weights
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $p':=\frac p{p-1}$. In this article, we establish a mixed multiplier weak-type inequality with weight dependence $[w]_{A_p}^{\frac1p}[w]_{A_\infty}^{\max\{\frac1p,\frac1{p'}\}}$ for scalar $A_p$ weights and Calderón--Zygmund operators whose modulus of continuity satisfies the Dini condition. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp exponent $\max\{1,\frac2p\}$ of $[w]_{A_p}$ in the corresponding pure $A_p$ bound. Moreover, in the matrix-weighted setting, we prove the sharpness of the exponent $1+\min\{\frac1p,\frac1{p(p-1)}\}$ of $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}$ in the known multiplier weak-type inequality for the Hilbert transform.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Improved contraction estimates for linear elliptic diffusion-advection-reaction equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper analyzes contraction estimates for the unique strong solution to a linear elliptic diffusion-advection-reaction equation in a bounded open subset of $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d \geq 3$, where the zero-order coefficient lies in $L^{\frac{d}{2}}$ and the drift coefficient belongs to $L^p$ with $p \in (d, \infty)$. Compared with existing results, we obtain contraction estimates with improved constants in a quantitative sense. In particular, for the $L^\infty$-contraction estimate, the constant is shown to have the explicit form $\frac{1}α$, depending only on the constant $α> 0$ in the zero-order term. The key step is to represent the solution as the image of a weighted resolvent associated with a Dirichlet form.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the absence of point defects in biaxial Landau--de Gennes models
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study local minimizers of a sextic-potential Landau--de Gennes energy for nematic liquid crystals in the small-elastic-constant limit. Under the uniform energy and $L^\infty$ bounds, these minimizers converge to a locally energy-minimizing harmonic map $\mathbf{Q}_0$ into a biaxial vacuum manifold. The main result of this paper is that such a limiting map $\mathbf{Q}_0$ has no interior point singularities. The proof relies on a geometric identification of the lifted Frobenius metric on the universal cover $\mathbb{S}^3$ with a rescaled Berger metric. For a hypothetical tangent cone at a point singularity, its link is a nonconstant harmonic two-sphere into the Berger sphere. We construct a smooth variation field adapted to the Hopf direction and show that it induces a quantitative instability estimate, in contradiction with the shifted stability inequality inherited from local minimality. This replaces the usual round-sphere test fields by a target-specific construction and rules out interior point defects in the biaxial setting. The result is sharp in view of the well-known existence of point defects in the uniaxial theory.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 21 pages, comments are welcome! Major revision. Many proofs have been substantially simplified from the first version

Analysis of PDEs.title: Genericity of singularities of solutions to quasilinear systems on compact sets
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the genericity of singularities of types $A_2,A_3,D_4^\pm$ in solutions of the equations of gas dynamics and nonlinear geometrical optics. The sets of solutions satisfying the corresponding transversality conditions are proved to be open and dense in spaces of smooth and real-analytic solutions equipped with the Whitney topology on compact sets.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Determining evolutionary equations from a single passive boundary observation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study inverse boundary problems (IBPs) for evolutionary partial differential equations from a single passive boundary observation generated by an unknown internal source in an unknown medium. The goal is simultaneous recovery of the source and medium coefficients. In stark contrast to active measurements, where designed inputs provide rich, structured data, passive-observation inverse boundary problems have minimal observable information and intrinsically coupled unknowns. Consequently, these problems have been studied far less systematically than their active counterparts.
  In this paper, we develop a unified and novel framework based on fundamental integral identities, integrating tools from harmonic analysis, interface asymptotics, and free-boundary regularity together with delicate low- and high-frequency asymptotics. This framework provides the first systematic resolution for a broad class of such inverse problems for {second-order hyperbolic, parabolic, and Schrödinger equations} within a single coherent approach. The key technical condition we impose is that the {cardinality of the measurement dataset exceeds that of the unknowns by at least one dimension}. This extra dimensional room enables us to decouple the unknowns and effectively handle inherent nonlinearity of the inverse problem. The unique identifiability results we obtain are arguably the best possible from a cardinality point of view. They not only subsume all existing results in the literature as special cases, but also cover significantly more general configurations of practical interest. Our framework complements several classical theories for IBPs and opens up a promising new direction with numerous potential developments.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Keywords: inverse boundary problems, evolutionary equations, single passive observation, multi-parameter decoupling, formally determined, unique identifiability, Fourier analysis, interface asymptotics, free-boundary regularity, frequency asymptotics

Analysis of PDEs.title: Self-similar solutions to the time-fractional Porous-Medium Equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We show the existence of self-similar solutions with constant finite mass to the time-fractional Porous-Medium Equation for all spatial dimensions $d \ge 1$ and all exponents $m>m_c=(d-2)_+/d$. This range is optimal. We find two types of solution depending on the exponent: compactly supported solutions in the slow-diffusion range $m > 1$ and positive solutions with heavy tails in the sub-critical fast-diffusion range $m_c < m < 1$. The self-similar solutions in the linear case $m=1$ were already known explicitly obtained by the Fourier transform, and we discuss their properties in our settings and the limit $m \to 1$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stochastic Representation-Inspired Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Incompressible Fluid Flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The effectiveness of neural networks in solving partial differential equations depends not only on their approximation capability but also on the suitability of their representations for the underlying solutions. Motivated by stochastic integral representations of incompressible fluid flows and the associated Biot--Savart kernel, we propose a Biot--Savart-informed (i.e. physics-informed) neural network (BS-PINN) for the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations. By extracting a rational profile from a regularized Biot--Savart kernel, we construct a smooth activation function with fixed and learnable kernel scales. Both variants retain the conventional velocity--pressure formulation and physics-informed training framework, allowing the influence of the activation function to be examined independently. We evaluate the method on five benchmarks, including Kovasznay flow, cylinder wake, three-dimensional Beltrami flow, Taylor--Green vortex, and double shear layer. Across 21 benchmark--architecture comparisons, both variants consistently reduce the combined velocity error relative to the conventional $\tanh$-based PINN, achieving mean relative error reductions of 31.7\% and 33.2\%, respectively. Improvements are also observed in reported pressure and vorticity errors. Notably, the double-shear-layer experiments demonstrate improved resolution of localized shear structures and, for BS-PINN-F, qualitatively clearer vortex-roll-up patterns in the long-time simulation. These findings highlight the potential of incorporating analytical flow structures into neural-network representations for incompressible flow simulations.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Physics-informed neural networks; Navier--Stokes equations; Stochastic integral representations; Biot--Savart kernel; Numerical simulation

Analysis of PDEs.title: On $U(1)^{2}$-Invariant Cayley $4$-Folds in $\mathbb{R}^{8}$
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study $ \mathrm{U}(1)^{2} $-invariant Cayley submanifolds in $ \mathbb{R}^{8} $, under the action with weights $ (e^{i θ_{1}}, e^{i θ_{2}}, e^{-i(θ_{1} + θ_{2})}, 1) $ on coordinates $ (z_{1}, z_{2}, z_{3}, z_{4}) \in \mathbb{C}^{4} $. Locally, we can prove that $ N $ can be written as a graph of functions $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2}: \mathbb{R}^{2} \rightarrow \mathbb{R} $ (where $ a_{3}= -a_{1}-a_{2} $), where unlike in the special Lagrangian setting, the moment-map parameters are not required to be constant, which gives rise to additional degrees of freedom in the reduced equations. We prove that $ N $ is Cayley if and only if a non-linear, Cauchy-Riemann system of partial differential equations in $ u, v, a_{1}, a_{2} $ holds, with ellipticity away from its degeneracy locus.
  We investigate the special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions of the system, obtaining potential functions in both cases. For general $ \mathrm{U}(1)^{2} $-invariant Cayley $ 4 $-folds, we derive almost-conservation laws (with clear obstruction terms) involving natural $ S_{3} $-invariant and alternating combinations of the moment-map parameters. These identities exhibit additional source terms, distinguishing the general Cayley system from its special Lagrangian and coassociative reductions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Perturbation results for the Choquard equation in the sublinear case
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study perturbations of the positive ground state of the Choquard equation $$ -Δu+u=(I_α*|u|^p)|u|^{p-2}u\qquad\text{in }\mathbb R^N $$ by means of a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction. For $p\ge2$ the energy is $C^2$ on $H^1$ and a standard machinery applies. The case $α=2$, $1+2/N<p<2$ is different: the ground state has an algebraic decay and the energy is not twice differentiable on $H^1$. We introduce a weighted space adapted to the tail and we perform a finite-dimensional reduction on it. The outcome is a positive solution of a localized perturbation problem near every critical point of the first-order interaction functional with nonzero local degree. For the singularly perturbed problem with potential $V$ we obtain, under a small relative oscillation assumption, solutions concentrating near every critical point of $V$ with nonzero local degree, and a Lusternik--Schnirelman lower bound near compact sets of local minima. We also consider the variant in which $V$ multiplies both the linear and nonlocal terms, and we construct solutions that concentrate near isolated critical points of nonzero degree.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Liouville theorem for the Hénon parabolic equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that every nonnegative classical entire solution of $u_t-Δu=|x|^αu^p$ in $\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ is identically zero when $n\ge3$, $α\ge0$, and $1 < p < \frac{n+2+2α}{n-2}$. The same conclusion holds for weighted parabolic Gross--Pitaevskii systems with nonlinearities of degree $p=2r+1$ and constant coupling coefficients $β_{ij}=β_{ji}\ge0$ and $β_{ii}>0$. Both results include the unweighted case and require no boundedness, radial symmetry, spatial decay, finite-energy, or growth assumptions. The range is optimal for both problems: bounded nonzero nonnegative stationary solutions exist for $p\ge\frac{n+2+2α}{n-2}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The topological degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We resolve the long-standing open problem of computing the Leray--Schauder degree of the regular $SU(3)$ Toda system on a closed oriented surface $M$. If $d_{m,k}$ denotes the degree in the block $(4πm,4π(m+1))\times(4πk,4π(k+1))$, then \[
  \sum_{m,k\geq0}d_{m,k}x^my^k
  =(1-x)^{χ(M)-1}(1-y)^{χ(M)-1}(1-xy)^{χ(M)}, \] where $χ(M)$ is the Euler characteristic of $M$. Nonvanishing of $d_{m,k}$ thus gives an existence criterion in terms of the topology of $M$ and the parameter block.
  At each step of the degree computation, we show that the only possible local mass pairs are $(4π,0)$ and $(8π,4π)$. We use generic perturbations and local second-order information on the weights to exclude collisions of shadow centers and splitting at mixed blow-up points. The shadow degrees and the Morse index then give the degree jump at each critical value.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stochastic Homogenization of Schrödinger Equations with Exponentially Mixing Sub-Gaussian Potentials
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study $i\partial_t u_{\varepsilon}=H_{\varepsilon} u_{\varepsilon}$, $H_{\varepsilon} = -Δ+ V\left(\frac{x}{\varepsilon},ω\right)$, where $V$ is a stationary ergodic sub-Gaussian field with exponential mixing. We establish the optimal algebraic error rate $\varepsilon^{\frac{d}2}$ in $L^2(Ω;L^2_x)$ for every $d\ge1$, prove it sharp by a matching lower bound under a non degeneracy condition, and upgrade the mean square convergence of Zhang--Bal [Stoch. Dyn. 14 (2014), 1350013] to almost sure convergence. The results are non perturbative in the amplitude of $V$ and require neither Gaussian marginals nor weak randomness. We further establish a Gaussian fluctuation central limit theorem with explicit covariance. The limiting fluctuation is the solution to the linear stochastic Schrödinger equation with additive spatial white noise \begin{equation*} i\partial_t\mathcal{G} = H_0 \mathcal{G} + \sqrt{\widehat{R}(0)}\,\bar{u}\,ξ, \qquad H_0 = -Δ+ \mathbb{E}[V], \end{equation*} where $ξ$ is a time frozen spatial white noise on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathcal{G}$ takes values in $H^{-\mathfrak{s}}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for every $\mathfrak{s}>\frac{d}{2}$. The proofs combine Duhamel iteration with multiscale cluster expansion for the cumulants of smoothed linear functionals of the potential.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 31 pages. This version replaces the limiting SPDE and its covariance by the correct time frozen one, and replaces the block martingale argument by a weighted spatial average

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global existence and semi-classical limit for the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi--Dirac Fokker--Planck equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the global existence and the semi-classical limit of the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi--Dirac Fokker--Planck equation. We first establish the existence and uniqueness of a global weak solution for initial data with finite mass and second velocity moment satisfying the Pauli bound. When the initial datum also has finite spatial second moment and finite free energy, we prove that the solution satisfies the Fermi--Dirac free energy inequality. Next, as the quantum parameter $\hbar$ goes to zero, we prove that the solution of the Fermi--Dirac Fokker--Planck equation converges strongly to the classical Fokker--Planck solution in $\mathcal C([0,T];L^1_j(\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R^d))$ for all $j\in[0,2)$. We also obtain a quantitative convergence rate in $\hbar$ when both equations share the same bounded initial datum.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Scaling-invariant smallness and global strong solutions to the three-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with a non-vacuum far-field density
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We consider the Cauchy problem for the three-dimensional
  isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with a
  positive far-field density $ρ_\infty$.
  We identify the following scaling-invariant quantity
  associated with the initial data:
  \begin{align*}
  ρ_\infty^{\frac{3-γ}{2}}
  \left(
  \|\nabla u_0\|_{L^2}^2
  +P(ρ_\infty)
  \Big(
  \frac12\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}ρ_0|u_0|^2\,dx
  +\int_{\mathbb{R}^3}G(ρ_0)\,dx
  \Big)
  \right),
  \end{align*}
  where $G$ denotes the relative potential energy density
  with respect to $ρ_\infty$.
  Provided that the scaling-invariant quantity is sufficiently small,
  we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, allowing the initial density to contain interior vacuum and exhibit large oscillations.
  The smallness criterion depends explicitly on the far-field density through the prefactor $ρ_\infty^{(3-γ)/2}$ and the background pressure $P(ρ_\infty)$.
  Our result provides a non-vacuum counterpart to Wen's
  scaling-invariant global existence result for the
  far-field vacuum case
  (\textit{Adv. Math.} \textbf{482} (2025), Paper No. 110628).

Analysis of PDEs.title: Helicity conservation for compressible barotropic Euler flows: regularity criteria and a momentum-based approach
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study helicity conservation for weak solutions to the compressible barotropic Euler equations. Using generalized Constantin-E-Titi-type commutator estimates that fully exploit the kinetic energy, we derive new sufficient conditions for helicity conservation across a broader range of regularity exponents. These conditions reveal the interplay between temporal, spatial integrability and differentiability of the velocity and density, as well as the influence of velocity-density coupling on helicity conservation. A key feature of our approach is that helicity conservation is established directly from the momentum equation, without invoking the vorticity equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Remarks on uniqueness and nonuniqueness for the isotropic $L_p$-Minkowski problem with $p<-n$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study uniqueness and nonuniqueness for the isotropic $L_p$-Minkowski problem with $p<-n$. For $n\geq3$, we prove uniqueness for $p$ just below $-n$ without any symmetry assumptions. Moreover, for $n\geq8$, we obtain nonuniqueness for $p$ just above $-2n-3$, even under full simplex symmetry. The proofs use the Chou-Wang obstruction and Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stability for a multi-frequency inverse source problem in diffusion-based tomography
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is concerned with the inverse source problem for the time-harmonic diffusion equation arising in optical tomography. In inhomogeneous media, we establish a conditional logarithmic stability estimate by using multi-frequency boundary flux measurements. The proof combines a boundary observability inequality for the associated heat equation with quantitative analytic continuation. For constant coefficients, we further derive an increasing stability estimate with explicit dependence on the frequency bandwidth. In this case, the analysis employs complex polynomial interpolation of the Fourier-Laplace transform of the source. We also implement a multi-frequency Landweber iteration with a discrepancy-based stopping rule to reconstruct the sources. Numerical experiments show an overall improvement in reconstruction accuracy and resolution as the frequency bandwidth increases under the tested noise settings.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Wasserstein gradient flow of the Sinkhorn divergence between Gaussian distributions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Wasserstein gradient flow of the Sinkhorn divergence when both the source and the target are Gaussian distributions. We prove the existence of a flow that stays in the class of Gaussian distributions, and is unique in the larger class of measures with strongly-concave and smooth log-densities. We prove that the flow globally converges toward the target measure when the source's covariance matrix is not singular, and provide counter-examples to global convergence when it is, giving a first answer to an open question raised in [Carlier et al. 2024, \S4.2]. When the covariance matrix of the source distribution commutes with that of the target, we derive more quantitative results that showcase exponential convergence toward the target when the source and the target share their support, but dropping to sublinear rates (O(t^{-1})) if the target is concentrated on a strict subspace of the source's support.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Liouville theorems for the stationary Navier-Stokes equations under partial component conditions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove Liouville theorems for smooth stationary incompressible Navier-Stokes flows in $R^3$ with finite Dirichlet integral and velocity vanishing uniformly at infinity. If the partial components of velocity $(u_1,u_2)$ belong to $L^{4,\infty}$, then we show that $u$ must vanish. The second result only requires that one component $u_1$ belongs to $L^{3/2,\infty}$. The proofs are based on the head-pressure sign and a localized energy identity, combined with different pressure estimates for the two cases.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Power loss for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi estimate on smooth hypersurfaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove power-type lower bounds for the local Mizohata--Takeuchi constants for $C^{2,β}$ hypersurfaces with $0<β\leq1$ whose second fundamental form is nonzero at some point. This result, in particular, disproves the so-called local Mizohata--Takeuchi conjectures for the paraboloid and the sphere and, in turn, presents an obstruction to a general weighted approach to the theory of Fourier restriction of those classical surfaces.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Forward Self-similar Solutions of the Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations in Dimensions Five and Higher
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct forward self-similar solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$ ($n\ge 5$) for arbitrary $(-1)$-homogeneous, divergence-free initial data $u_0$ smooth on the unit sphere. For $n\ge 6$, the $O(|y|^{-3})$ bound on the nonlinear residual of the linear heat profile no longer yields $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$-integrability, obstructing a direct global energy perturbation around $e^Δu_0$. To overcome this difficulty, we truncate $u_0$ near the origin via a divergence-free cutoff and take the time-one slice of the resulting Navier--Stokes flow as the background profile, whose residual reduces to a parabolic scaling derivative evolving in $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ from compactly supported data. Choosing a large cutoff radius yields a global $H^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$ remainder and a forward self-similar weak solution converging strongly to $u_0$ in $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ as $t\downarrow 0$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on non-CMC closed manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In the paper, we prove the existence of a positive and essentially bounded solution to a Lichnerowicz equation in the Einstein-scalar field theory on a closed manifold with non-constant mean curvature. In particular, the non-constant mean curvature gives rise to supercritical terms in the equation, on top of singular ones. We employ a recent fixed-point argument, which involves sub- and supersolutions. Additionally, we provide several conditions on the coefficients in the equation that prevent the existence of positive classical solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Determining $W^{1,n}$ conductivities for Calderón's problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish a global uniqueness result at the critical Sobolev regularity for the isotropic Calderón problem in all dimensions $n \ge 4$. More precisely, for every $n \ge 4$ and every bounded Lipschitz domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$, any real-valued, uniformly elliptic scalar conductivity $γ\in W^{1,n}(Ω)$ is uniquely determined by its full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. Together with the known results for $n=2,3,4$ in the literature, this settles a long-standing open problem in the field while providing a unified proof for all dimensions $n \ge 4$. To prove uniqueness at this endpoint, we develop an averaged trace norm method, which combines complex geometrical optics with trace-norm estimates averaged over directions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On an inverse boundary problem in elastodynamics
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the simultaneous identification of the Lamé parameters $λ$ and $μ$ in three-dimensional static isotropic elasticity. For smooth coefficients, we establish uniqueness from the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map when $μ$ is axisymmetric, admits a multiplicative or additive separation on a product domain, or is quasianalytic in one fixed direction. These results require neither smallness of $\nablaμ$ nor real analyticity of the coefficients, and impose no corresponding structural condition on $λ$. In the axisymmetric and separated cases, partial boundary data suffice to determine $μ$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Normalized solutions for logarithmic $p$-Laplacian equations on graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a logarithmic $p$-Laplacian equation with prescribed $L^2$ mass on connected locally finite weighted graphs, with $p > 2$. By minimizing the energy, we obtain a positive solution for every prescribed mass $m > 0$ on finite graphs and, under additional assumptions on the vertex measure and the potential, on infinite graphs. We describe the behavior of positive solutions and their Lagrange multipliers as $m \to 0^+$ or $m \to +\infty$. In particular, as $m \to 0^+$, the minimizers rescaled to unit mass converge along subsequences to functions supported at a single vertex.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global well-posedness and regularization for a nonlinear relativistic Fokker--Planck equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a nonlinear relativistic Fokker--Planck equation on momentum space, whose diffusion coefficient and drift vector field are nonlinear integral functionals of the solution. We prove global existence and uniqueness of weak probability density solutions preserving the relativistic energy-momentum $(E,P)$. A fundamental step in the proof is to establish that the scalar diffusion coefficient remains uniformly positive on every finite time interval. The key mechanism ensuring this property is the strict relativistic inequality $E^2-|P|^2>1$, combined with the uniform integrability of the energy tails on every finite time interval. We further prove that global weak solutions become instantaneously smooth and strictly positive for positive times. Finally, for even initial data, we prove that the diffusion coefficient remains uniformly positive for all time.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gradient estimate for $p$-heat equation on complete Riemannian manifold
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We derive a Hamilton-type gradient estimate for positive solutions to the $p$-heat equation via the Moser iteration method. Our result relaxes the curvature assumption from sectional curvature to Ricci curvature. In addition, we obtain a Liouville-type theorem and a Harnack-type inequality as corollaries.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness and Nondegeneracy of Positive Bounded Solutions for Semilinear Dirichlet Problems in Exterior-Star Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of positive bounded solutions for the Dirichlet problem $$-Δu=f(u)\,\ \ \text{in}\ \ Ω, \ \ u=0\,\ \ \text{on}\ \ \partialΩ,$$ where $f$ is a positive reaction and $Ω\subsetneq\mathbb{R}^d$ is a uniformly $C^{2,γ}$ domain with a star-shaped complement. Our uniqueness result gives a positive answer to Open Question 1 of [H. Berestycki and C. Graham, ARMA, 2026].

Analysis of PDEs.title: Growth of Sobolev Norms for Linear Schrodinger Equations with Denjoy--Carleman Potentials
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We consider the linear Schrödinger equation on a torus of arbitrary dimension with a real time-dependent potential satisfying a mixed space--time Denjoy--Carleman condition. More precisely, for an increasing concave weight \(ω(r)\asymp \log^σ(e+r)\), \(σ> 1\),we assume \[
  \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\partial_t^q\widehat V(k,t)|
  \le Ae^{Bq^{p}}e^{-ρ_{0}ω(|k|)},\qquad
  p=\fracσ{σ-1}. \] The corresponding spatial class is strictly larger than every Gevrey class, while the moment factor gives the quantitative ultradifferentiable control in time needed by the finite normal form. We adapt the method of Delort and Fang--Zhang to this non-power Fourier weight. The essential new point is a quantitative operator calculus whose majorant is built from the moment sequence and an auxiliary factorial that closes the exact Leibniz convolutions. For every $s>0$ we prove \[
  \|u(t)\|_{H^s}\le C_s
  \exp\{C_s[\log(2+|t|)]^{\frac{1}σ}\}
  \|u(0)\|_{H^s}. \] The estimate is valid for every \(t\in\mathbb R\), holds in every space dimension, requires neither smallness, quasi-periodicity, nor a transversality condition.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Remarks on nonlinear dispersive PDEs with rough dispersion management
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we study the Cauchy problem for a class of dispersive PDEs where a rough time coefficient is present in front of the dispersion. Under minimal assumptions on the occupation measure of this coefficient, we show that for the large class of semilinear dispersive PDEs whose well-posedness theory relies on linear estimates of Strichartz or local smoothing type, one has the same well-posedness theory with or without the modulation. We also show a regularization by noise type of phenomenon for rough modulations, namely, large data global well-posedness in the focusing mass-critical case for the modulated equation. Under rougher assumptions on the modulation, we show that one can also transfer the well-posedness theory based on multilinear Fourier analysis from the original dispersive PDE to the modulated one. In the case of the NLS equation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathbb{T}^d$, this covers all the sub-critical and critical regularities, thus completing and extending the various results currently available in the literature. At last, in the case of the periodic Wick-ordered cubic NLS, we show an even stronger form of regularization by noise, namely well-posedness in the critical Fourier-Lebesgue space for rough modulations.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The proof of Theorem 1.4 has been corrected for the local well-posedness, and a globalization argument has been added. Appendix A has also been added to discuss the case where the occupation measure is no longer absolutely continuous with respect to the Lebesgue measure. 54p

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global Well-Posedness of Two-Dimensional Compressible Navier--Stokes Equations with Vacuum under a Scaling-Invariant Smallness Condition
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with vacuum as far-field density. For the initial data that satisfy suitable regularity conditions, we establish the global well-posedness of strong solutions, provided that the scaling-invariant initial quantity \( \barρ \big( \|ρ_0\|_{L^1} +
\barρ^{-2γ} \|ρ_0\|_{L^1}^{-1} +
\barρ^{\frac{α(γ+1)}{2}} \|ρ_0 |x|^α\|_{L^1} \big) (1+\barρ E_0)^{3/2} \big( \|\nabla u_0\|_{L^2}^2 + \|ρ_0^γ\|_{L^2}^2 \big) \) is sufficiently small. Moreover, if the initial data possess additional higher order regularity and satisfy the corresponding compatibility condition, the global strong solution becomes a classical one. %The smallness condition above is invariant under the natural scaling of the two-dimensional isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes system. %A key point of the proof is to use this scaling to normalize the density upper bound \(\barρ\). Meanwhile, a priori large-time decay estimates for both the pressure and the spatial gradient of the velocity field are obtained in \(L^2\) at rate \(t^{-1/2}\), together with the same rate for the density-weighted material derivative of the velocity. The initial density is allowed to contain vacuum, and vacuum at infinity is included. In particular, compactly supported initial density is admissible. The result provides a scaling-invariant smallness framework for the global well-posedness theory of two-dimensional compressible barotropic flows with far-field vacuum.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global strong solutions to isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations under a scaling-invariant smallness condition in $\mathbb{R}^2$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem for the isentropic compressible Navier--Stokes equations with vacuum at far field in two dimensions. Under an explicit scaling-invariant smallness condition on the initial data, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions. The scaling-invariant smallness condition implies some classes of large data. The main difficulty is to obtain a uniform upper bound for the density under such the condition. Some new estimates of the dissipation and time-weighted energy estimates with explicit dependence on the initial data are derived, which control the effective viscous flux and close the a priori upper bound for density. In addition, we also obtain algebraic decay of the pressure and the velocity gradient.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Synchronized Normalized Solutions for a Critical Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg System
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study positive synchronized normalized solutions to the critical
  Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg system:
  \begin{equation*}
  \left\{
  \begin{aligned}
  -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u)
  &=λ_1|x|^{-2a}u+β_1|x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u
  &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(
  μ_1|u|^{p-2}u
  +να|u|^{α-2}u|v|^γ
  \right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N,
  -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla v)
  &=λ_2|x|^{-2a}v+β_2|x|^{-bq}|v|^{q-2}v
  &\quad+|x|^{-bp}\left(
  μ_2|v|^{p-2}v
  +νγ|u|^α|v|^{γ-2}v
  \right),\quad\text{in }\mathbb R^N,
  \end{aligned}
  \right.
  \end{equation*}
  subject to the prescribed weighted masses
  \begin{equation*}
  \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx=ρ_1^2,
  \qquad
  \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}v^2\,dx=ρ_2^2,
  \end{equation*}
  where $N\geq5$, $0\leq a<\frac{N-4}{2}$, $a<b<a+1$,
  $α,γ>1$,
  $α+γ=p=\frac{2N}{N-2(1+a-b)}$, $2<q<p$,
  $β_i,μ_i,ρ_i>0$ for $i=1,2$, and $ν>0$.
  The associated Lagrange multipliers
  $λ_1,λ_2\in\mathbb R$ are unknown.
  Under suitable algebraic compatibility conditions, we establish
  existence and multiplicity results for positive synchronized
  normalized solutions. The construction is based on synchronized
  reduction and critical energy estimates involving a finite-mass
  Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg extremal.
  In the mass-subcritical regime, we find two positive solutions
  with opposite energies when
  $β=β_1ρ_1^{q-2}=β_2ρ_2^{q-2}$
  is sufficiently small. In the mass-critical and mass-supercritical
  regimes, we obtain a synchronized Pohozaev ground state below the
  critical energy threshold for sufficiently small $β$ and for all
  $β>0$, respectively.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Subwavelength resonances and localization in finite resonator chains with a size defect
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study subwavelength resonances of a finite chain of $N\ge2$ close-to-touching spherical resonators in three dimensions with a single radius defect of relative size $τ\in(0,1]$ and gap width $\varepsilon$. Taking the high-contrast limit before the narrow-gap limit, we prove that the positive generalized eigenvalues of the weighted chain coupling matrix with respect to the volume matrix determine the leading relative resonant frequencies. After eliminating the finite tails, we obtain an exact characteristic determinant and identify a unique critical ratio $τ_*\in(0,1)$ at which the largest eigenvalue crosses the upper edge of the homogeneous recurrence band $[0,4]$. For every $0<τ<τ_*$, exactly one eigenvalue lies above this band, and its eigenvector decays geometrically along the tails. As $τ\toτ_*^-$, its recurrence decay length diverges like $(τ_*-τ)^{-1/2}$. As $τ\to0$, exactly one eigenvalue diverges like $τ^{-2}$ and its eigenvector concentrates at the defect; if the defect is interior, one additional positive eigenvalue has order $τ$. For suitably normalized relative resonant modes, the sequential limit of the $\varepsilon$-scaled gradient supremum in each gap equals the absolute difference between adjacent reduced amplitudes. For the largest-eigenvalue mode, this yields defect-adjacent gradient concentration as the defect shrinks.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Pólya-Szegő inequalities for polygons
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Of the simple polygons of given area with at most $n$ sides, $n\ge5$, the regular $n$-gon uniquely maximizes torsional rigidity and minimizes the first Dirichlet eigenvalue, up to congruence. The same polygon minimizes the Dirichlet Sobolev quotient for $1\le q\le2$. For convex polygons the proof uses mixed boundary problems on a partition. When there are fewer than $n$ convex vertices, the exterior angles give a lower bound on the torsion deficit. The torsion and eigenvalue inequalities have quadratic stability in Hausdorff distance at fixed area and at fixed perimeter, with optimal exponent.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniform spatial Schauder estimates for backward stochastic partial differential equations with random coefficients
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove spatial Schauder estimates for super-parabolic backward stochastic partial differential equations. All coefficients can be random and depend on time and space, and the estimates are uniform in probability and time. The key ingredient is a weighted conditional energy norm adapted to the parabolic scale of each frequency block. Together with heat-kernel bounds and coefficient freezing, it controls the gradient-martingale coupling without assuming a bounded martingale integrand. As an application, we establish Schauder solvability for semilinear stochastic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations.

Analysis of PDEs.title: $H_2$-optimal riblet profiles for turbulence suppression in channel flows
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The drag-reducing properties of streamwise-elongated surface corrugations, commonly referred to as riblets, have been extensively studied through experiments, simulations, and reduced-order modeling. Notably, the linearized Navier-Stokes framework introduced by Ran, Zare, and Jovanovic (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 906, 2021) employs volume penalization to model riblet-induced boundary conditions and predict drag reduction. These approaches typically quantify drag reduction as a function of a single geometric parameter, such as spanwise spacing or groove cross-sectional area, evaluated over fixed riblet shapes. As a result, identifying optimal riblet geometries across a broader design space often necessitates exhaustive parametric studies. To address this problem, we propose an optimization framework for the systematic design of optimal riblet shapes. Accordingly, we reformulate the volume penalization term in the linearized dynamics as a structured state-feedback operator. Targeting maximal suppression of turbulence, we pose a composite optimization problem that minimizes the steady-state variance of velocity fluctuations and riblet-induced dynamical augmentations while maintaining a constant bulk-flux. For a fixed spanwise wavelength (riblet spacing), this framework yields optimal wall-normal profiles that achieve maximal turbulence attenuation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The singular set of the superconductivity free boundary problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove the uniqueness and continuous dependence of blow-ups at singular points of the free boundary for the superconductivity problem. As an application, we show that the free boundary is contained in a countable union of $C^1$ submanifolds of dimension at most $n-1$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Some of the main ideas in this paper originate from arXiv:2204.11426 and are combined into the present work, which recovers its results. The preprint arXiv:2204.11426 will no longer be updated and will not be submitted for publication

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density-valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Extremal metrics for the $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalues
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the $G$-invariant Steklov spectrum of compact connected Riemannian manifolds with boundary, endowed with an effective isometric action of a compact Lie group $G$. Under a mild nontransitivity assumption on the boundary action, we establish that this spectrum consists of an infinite sequence of eigenvalues diverging to infinity. We then investigate extremal metrics for the normalised $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue functionals. Assuming that $\dim G \geq 1$, we prove that none of these functionals admits an extremal $G$-invariant metric. Moreover, when $\dim M \geq 3$, the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue is unbounded above even within a fixed $G$-invariant conformal class. The proof relies on a local model near a boundary orbit and spectral convergence under conformal collapse. Finally, in contrast with the upper bounds obtained by Colbois, Dryden and El Soufi for invariant Laplace eigenvalues of embedded spheres of revolution, we construct, for any $n \geq 3$, a sequence of smooth Euclidean domains of revolution in $\mathbb R^n$, all diffeomorphic to the ball, along which the normalised first $G$-invariant Steklov eigenvalue blows up.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the uniqueness of ground states for pseudo-relativistic boson stars
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish the uniqueness of both action and energy ground states for the pseudo-relativistic Hartree equation. The latter, for every prescribed mass below the critical stellar mass, proves the Lieb-Yau conjecture. Our approach establishes radial nondegeneracy and a strict monotonicity property of the mass-frequency relation, providing a unified framework for proving uniqueness in both variational settings.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Heat-wave semigroup estimates and the compressible Navier-Stokes Equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the connection between the heat-wave semigroup and the compressible Navier-Stokes (CNS) equations. On one hand, the parabolic-hyperbolic nature of the CNS motivated the study of space-time estimates for the heat-wave semigroup by using recent harmonic analysis development, in particular, the local smoothing estimates for the wave equations; on the other hand, we apply the new estimates to obtain global well-posedness for CNS in the optimal critical Besov spaces. For the latter purpose, we introduce a new iteration framework for CNS that exploits some intrinsic structures of the equations, so that we can successfully apply these estimates.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stability of Anomalous Dissipation for the Forced Three-Dimensional Navier--Stokes Equations under Geometric Perturbations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The energy dissipation in the inviscid limit is a central problem in turbulence theory. Kolmogorov's 1941 (K41) theory predicts nonvanishing energy dissipation as viscosity tends to zero, a phenomenon known as anomalous dissipation. Bruè and De Lellis constructed solutions exhibiting this phenomenon, but their construction relies on precise geometric conditions. Based on quasi-self-similar mixing, we prove that anomalous dissipation persists under small pure normal perturbations of the central curves satisfying area-preserving and equal-length conditions. The perturbations vanish near the spatial endpoints and at the initial and terminal times, and smallness is measured in a mixed norm with at most two time derivatives and total order at most six. We establish stability of the area-preserving maps and full local fields, including the mixed derivatives needed for Hölder estimates of the forcing, and obtain high-frequency energy concentration. A comparison estimate and a contradiction argument give a positive dissipation lower bound uniform over the admissible perturbations. Using the $(2+\frac12)$-dimensional framework, we construct solutions of the forced three-dimensional (3D) Navier--Stokes equations with anomalous dissipation for a sequence of viscosities tending to zero.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 38 pages. Revised version with corrected and expanded proofs and clarified assumptions

Analysis of PDEs.title: Gradient estimates and monotonicity formulae for the $p$-filtration equation on Riemannian manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We derive Li--Yau type estimates on closed Riemannian manifolds and local Hamilton-type gradient estimates on complete manifolds for the $p$-filtration equation $u_t=Δ_pF(u)$. Under nonnegative Ricci curvature and a structural condition on $F$, we establish a $\mathcal W$-entropy formula, entropy-power concavity and local entropy rigidity. We also prove a parabolic frequency monotonicity formula without curvature assumptions. The results include homogeneous doubly nonlinear diffusion and extend to nonhomogeneous power sums and the arctangent law.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Blow-up rate for the subcritical semilinear heat equation in non-convex domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the semilinear heat equation $u_t=Δu+|u|^{p-1} u$ in possibly non-convex and unbounded domains. Our main result shows the nonexistence of type II blow-up for possibly sign-changing solutions in the energy subcritical range $(n-2)p<n+2$. This resolves a long-standing open question dating back to the 1980s and also deduces the blow-up of the scaling critical norm.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 30 pages; revised following referee comments; main results unchanged

Analysis of PDEs.title: Radial nodal action ground states with two prescribed masses for coupled Schrodinger equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study normalized nodal solutions of a cooperative system of nonlinear Schrödinger equations with two independently prescribed masses. For sufficiently small positive coupling, we obtain a radial nodal action ground state for every mass pair in a fixed compact subset of the positive quadrant. We first minimize the action on a radial nodal Nehari set at fixed frequencies. We then select both frequencies through an interior minimization of the action level. In this way, we adapt the scalar action approach of De Coster--Dovetta--Galant--Serra (\emph{Ann. Inst. H. Poincaré Anal. Non Linéaire}, 2026) to construct solutions whose components both change sign and whose action is minimal among radial nodal solutions at the selected frequencies.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz capacity in one dimension
Analysis of PDEs.summary: The Brunn-Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity is proved on the line for every $p<1$ and all compact sets. For $-1<p<1$, equality holds exactly for a singleton summand or else two intervals, provided at least one capacity is positive. The proof couples equilibrium measures in increasing order.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 9 pages, 1 figure; ancillary file: mathematical audit (4 pages). v2: mathematical results unchanged; updated reference to higher dimensions paper; updated ancillary audit

Analysis of PDEs.title: Smooth stationary water waves with multiple vortex spikes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For any prescribed positive integer $n$, we establish the existence of a family of stationary solutions to the two-dimensional capillary-gravity water wave equations in finite depth, whose stream functions exhibit $n$ well-separated vertically aligned vortex spikes with alternating signs. The construction is based on a nonlinear gluing scheme for a singularly perturbed semilinear elliptic equation coupled to the Bernoulli equation on the free surface. Our results extend the single-spike construction to arbitrary finite multi-spike configurations and reveal a mechanism through which exponentially localized vortex spikes can coexist with an almost flat free surface.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Characterizing nonlocal Sobolev spaces as generalized Bessel potential spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study nonlocal Sobolev spaces $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ with $p \in (1,\infty)$, defined via a general class of nonlocal gradients $D^ρ$ associated with a kernel function $ρ$. As our main contribution, we establish three new equivalent characterizations of these spaces. First, we describe $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ in terms of Fourier multipliers involving the symbol of the nonlocal potential associated with $D^ρ$. Second, we give a thorough functional analytic treatment of the nonlocal $ρ$-Laplacian $Δ^ρ$, which allows us to represent general nonlocal Sobolev spaces through its square root $(-Δ^ρ)^{1/2}$. Third, we show that $H^{ρ,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ coincides with the image $g_ρ* L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for a suitable convolution kernel $g_ρ\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^n)$, which confirms that these spaces are genuine potential spaces.
