These results generalize the well-known fact that, in the special case of the Riesz kernel, the resulting fractional Sobolev spaces coincide with the classical Bessel potential spaces. In this spirit, the present work can also be viewed as introducing a natural notion of generalized Bessel potential spaces.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Singularity removal in nonlocal operator inequalities on domains and applications: A $((Q,1)\implies (\GO,ρ))$ theorem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that certain classes of nonlocal integral inequalities on bounded uniform domains, involving operators, may be reduced to the local analogues on cubes without the singular weight. The theory applies to two-sided inverse doubling and quasi-monotone kernels with some moment conditions, and with a left-hand-side operator with average bi-Lipschitz properties. Direct applications to fractional semi-norm rigidity inequalities in nonlocal continuum mechanics, such as fractional Korn's Inequalities, Geometric Rigidity Estimates, and rigidity of some types of affine deformations, that are common in mechanics, are presented.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 36 pages. Title updated. Theorem 2.4 on norm/semi-norm equivalence is added, 2 new examples added in Section 5

Analysis of PDEs.title: Norm Approximation with Linear Growth of Error for Bosonic Dynamics in the Mean-Field Regime
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the quantum many-body dynamics of a homogeneous confined Bose gas in three dimensions in the mean-field scaling regime. We study the Cauchy problem for a class of initial data describing finitely many excitations over a Bose-Einstein condensate. Using a rigorous version of Bogolyubov's theory, we prove that the many-body evolution can be approximated in Fock space norm by a quasifree evolution of the excitations with an error which grows linearly in time. In distinction from earlier results, the slow growth in time holds even though the effective equation is not dispersive.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the local boundedness of weak solutions to doubly nonlinear equations with variable exponents
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish local boundedness, together with quantitative estimates, for non-negative weak sub-solutions to a class of doubly nonlinear parabolic equations whose prototype is \[ (u^q)_t-\operatorname{div} \Big(|Du|^{p(x,t)-2}Du\Big)=0, \qquad p(x,t)>1,\quad q>0. \] The results are obtained under a logarithmic continuity condition on the variable exponent $p(x,t)$ and suitable relations between $q$ and the local bounds of $p(x,t)$. In certain ranges of the exponents, an additional local integrability assumption is required.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp spectral gap and large time asymptotics for the Poisson-Nernst-Planck system with confinement
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Poisson--Nernst--Planck (Debye--Hückel) system for a single species of charged particles in $\mathbb R^d$, $d=2$ or $3$, with an external confinement potential. The particles repel each other through the Coulomb interaction. For a class of potentials with at least linear growth at infinity, solutions converge to the unique stationary state at an exponential rate in a weighted $\mathrm L^2$ space. The rate is given by the spectral gap of the linearized operator, which is symmetric for a scalar product adapted to the free energy. Our main result is that, for the harmonic potential $φ(x)=\frac\mu2\,|x|^2$, this spectral gap is exactly $μ$, for any mass and in both dimensions. The corresponding eigenspace is spanned by the translation modes. Unlike the attractive (Keller--Segel) case, the repulsive interaction destroys the monotonicity of the spectrum with respect to the angular momentum. We overcome this difficulty with a duality criterion and explicit \emph{chiral fluxes} built from vector spherical harmonics. These reduce the non-local spectral problem to one-dimensional weighted inequalities, which we prove by a ground state transform. The center of mass decays exactly like $e^{-μt}$. After removing this motion, the convergence rate improves to a second spectral gap $Λ_2>μ$, for which we prove an explicit lower bound in terms of the central density of the stationary state. As consequences, we obtain rates of convergence in $\mathrm L^p$ norms, and improved intermediate asymptotics for the unconfined system in $\mathbb R^2$, after recentering at the center of mass.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness of ground state solutions for fractional Schrödinger equations with general nonlinearities
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In 2013, R.L. Frank and E. Lenzmann [R.L. Frank, E. Lenzmann, Uniqueness of non-linear ground states for fractional Laplacians in $\mathbb{R}$, Acta Math. 210 (2) (2013) 261-318] studied the following problem:
  \begin{align*}
  (-Δ)^su + u = u^{p-1} \quad \text{in } \mathbb{R}^N,
  \end{align*} where $s \in (0,1)$, $N = 1$, $p \in (2,2_s^*)$, and $2_s^*$ is the critical fractional Sobolev exponent. They proved that the ground state is unique (up to translations). Then in 2016, they, together with L. Silvestre [R.L. Frank, E. Lenzmann, L. Silvestre, Uniqueness of radial solutions for the fractional Laplacian, Comm. Pure Appl. Math. 69 (9) (2016) 1671-1726], showed similar uniqueness results for high dimensions ($N \geq 2$), in which they proposed a challenging open problem to extend their results about non-degeneracy and uniqueness of ground states to nonlinearities $f(u)$ beyond the pure-power case. In this paper, we aim to give an affirmative answer to this open issue for two classes of more general nonlinearities, including the case of sums of powers with certain conditions on exponents.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: In this version, we have restricted the class of nonlinearities under consideration and proved the uniqueness of ground state solutions up to translations

Functional Analysis.title: Almost minimizing Yang$-$Mills fields: log-epiperimetric inequality, non-concentration, and uniqueness of tangents
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish a direct log-epiperimetric inequality for Yang$-$Mills fields in arbitrary dimension and we leverage it to prove uniqueness of tangent cones with isolated singularity for almost energy minimizing connections and $ω$-ASD connections (where $ω$ is not necessarily closed) satisfying some suitable regularity and non-concentration assumptions. En route to this we establish a Luckhaus type lemma for connections to exclude curvature concentration along blow-up sequences.

Functional Analysis.title: The Bessis Moussa Villani conjecture in finite von Neumann algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove the Bessis--Moussa--Villani conjecture, which is known for matrix algebras, for bounded operators in a finite von Neumann algebra with a faithful normal tracial state. Following the approach of Heinavaara, for a pair of positive operators, we construct a tracial joint spectral measure on the punctured plane whose moments are the traces of symmetrized words. We construct a scalar measure by holomorphic spectral selection and a Lyapunov identity. An integral identity for its moments then gives positivity of two coordinate-weighted distributions. From these we obtain the planar measure and the Laplace representation of the trace exponential.

Functional Analysis.title: Fine properties of nonlinear potentials and a unified perspective on monotonicity formulas
Functional Analysis.summary: We rigorously show that a large family of monotone quantities along the weak inverse mean curvature flow is the limit case of the corresponding ones along the level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials. Such monotone quantities include Willmore and Minkowski-type functionals on Riemannian manifolds with nonnegative Ricci curvature. In $3$-dimensional manifolds with nonnegative scalar curvature, we also recover the monotonicity of the Hawking mass and its nonlinear potential theoretic counterparts. This unified view is built on a refined analysis of $p$-capacitary potentials. We prove that they strongly converge in $W^{1,q}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ as $p\to 1^+$ to the inverse mean curvature flow and their level sets are curvature varifolds. Finally, we also deduce a Gauss-Bonnet-type theorem for level sets of $p$-capacitary potentials.
Functional Analysis.comment: 52 pages. To appear: Arch. Rat. Mech. Anal

Functional Analysis.title: Generalized and Convex Poincaré Inequalities via Transport-Divergence Inequalities
Functional Analysis.summary:
We investigate the relationship between generalized $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and transport-divergence inequalities involving $χ^q$-type divergences. Extending the classical correspondence between the $(2,2)$-Poincaré inequality and quadratic transport-$χ^2$ inequalities, we prove that a $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequality is equivalent to a transport-divergence inequality for conjugates $(p,p')$ and $(q,q')$. We then study the convex counterpart of these inequalities. Using weak barycentric optimal transport and convex order, we establish an equivalence between convex $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities and weak transport-divergence inequalities involving a projected $χ_q$ divergence. We further characterize the minimizers arising in this projection problem through a geometric condition on the relative density. In dimension one, we analyze the geometric consequences of $(q',p')$-Poincaré inequalities by identifying sharp conditions on the behavior of the density both at infinity and near isolated zeros.
  We show that when $q'>p'$, the concentration behavior becomes polynomial rather than exponential at infinity. Finally, we interpret these inequalities through the lens of optimization in Wasserstein space. In particular, the equivalence between transport-divergence and Poincaré inequalities appears as an analogue of the equivalence between quadratic growth and Polyak--Łojasiewicz inequalities in finite-dimensional optimization.

Functional Analysis.title: Hadamard inverse mapping theorem for certain continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings
Functional Analysis.summary: Hadamard inverse mapping theorem concerns global inversion of continuously differentiable mappings between Banach spaces. Here we consider a weaker notion of smoothness and work with continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings. We prove that a continuously Gateaux differentiable mapping with invertible derivatives such that the inverses are uniformly bounded, possesses a continuous right inverse on every compact set. We also provide sufficient conditions for global invertibility of certain continuously Gateaux differentiable mappings between Banach spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Annihilating ideals and Agler--McCarthy spectral varieties in the bidisc
Functional Analysis.summary: The closed unit bidisc $\overline{\mathbb{D}^2}$ is known to be a spectral set for any pair $(T_1,T_2)$ of commuting contractions. When each $T_i$ is pure and has finite defect, the pair admits a much smaller spectral set: the closure of a distinguished variety $V\subset \mathbb{D}^2$. We exhibit conditions on $(T_1,T_2)$ that guarantee that no proper closed subset of $\overline{V}$ can be a spectral set. In addition, we examine the relationship between $V$ and the annihilating ideal $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ in $H^\infty(\mathbb{D}^2)$. While $V$ is typically strictly larger than the zero set of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$, we isolate a natural constrained co-extension $(S_1,S_2)$ of $(T_1,T_2)$ whose Taylor spectrum is contained in $V$ and is closely linked to the so-called support of $Ann(T_1,T_2)$. We also find simple conditions on $Ann(T_1)$ detecting whether $Ann(T_1,T_2)$ is the ideal of functions vanishing on the joint point spectrum of $(S_1^*,S_2^*)$.
Functional Analysis.comment: Version 3: A missing assumption has been added to Theorem 2.6. The statement of Theorem 2.11 has been reworded. An issue in Theorem 3.12 has been fixed. 26 pages

Functional Analysis.title: $(α,β)$-lineability and spaceability of functions with a unique maximum
Functional Analysis.summary: Motivated by the classical work of Gurariy and Quarta on linear spaces of continuous functions with a unique point of maximum, we determine the largest possible dimension of such spaces in several settings. For a connected $n$-manifold $M$ without boundary, with $n\ge2$, the largest dimension of a subspace of $\mathcal{C}_0(M)$ whose nonzero elements attain their maximum at exactly one point is $n+1$ if $M$ is homeomorphic to $S^n$, and $n$ otherwise. We also establish the sharp bound $n+1$ in $\mathcal{C}(\mathbb R^n)$ and obtain results on extensions of prescribed finite-dimensional subspaces.

Functional Analysis.title: The random Riesz's lemma in random normed modules
Functional Analysis.summary: Riesz's lemma states that a normed space is finite-dimensional if and only if its closed unit ball is sequentially compact. The purpose of this paper is to establish a random counterpart of this lemma in a random normed module. Precisely speaking, based on the two recent developments in random functional analysis: one is the dimensional decomposition of a regular $σ$-stable $L^0$-module, and the other is the theory of random sequential compactness in a random normed module, we can finally establish the random Riesz's lemma, which states that a $σ$-stable random normed module is proper if and only if its random closed unit ball is random sequentially compact.

Functional Analysis.title: Commutants of diagonal operators
Functional Analysis.summary: The aim of this paper is devoted to the profound and comprehensive characterization when diagonal operators having the minimal or double commutant property on a separable Hilbert space, in terms of the topological and geometric properties of their spectra.

Functional Analysis.title: Boundary Feller-Dynkin processes associated with Laguerre processes and Pickrell diffusions
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we construct a Feller-Dynkin boundary process by applying the method of intertwiners to the coherent family, introduced in our previous work, of Laguerre processes with a fixed parameter. The corresponding boundary process is computed explicitly, and it turns out to be a deterministic dynamical system. Since the Pickrell diffusions that leave the Pickrell measure invariant are coherent with respect to the same projective system, we also obtain the stochastic boundary process associated with the coherent family of Pickrell diffusions.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for multiple sets. These are of the type: $$\prod_{i=1}^I γ_{Σ_i}(K_i)^{\tilde λ_i} \le C_{\text{sharp}}γ_Γ\Big(\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i K_i\Big),$$ with convex sets $K_i \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, whose barycenter $b_{K_i,Σ_i}$ with respect to the Gaussian measure $γ_{Σ_i}$ is zero, where $λ_i, \tilde λ_i \in (0;1)$ such that $\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i=\sum_{i=1}^I \tilde λ_i=1.$ In addition, we provide natural conditions on the matrices $Γ, Σ_1,\cdots,Σ_I \in \mathrm{Sym}_{>0}(n)$, which are given through a pointwise inequality involving the Karcher mean. Furthermore, we study equality cases of the corresponding functional forms in such situations. We also investigate the role of centering in the (B)-property by giving a counterexample for convex bodies with zero Lebesgue barycenters in dimensions at least three and thereby answering negatively a question of Faifman-Polterovich in \cite{Faifman_Polt}. Finally, a new slicing approach is introduced, which allows us to pass from centered convex sets to sets with arbitrary barycenters such that their weighted sum is convex. Based on this idea, we show a new Gaussian Brunn-Minkowski inequality $$e^{|\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} γ_n \Big(\sum_{i=1}^I λ_i K_i \Big)^{1/n} \ge \sum_{i=1}^I λ_i e^{|b_{K_i,I_n}|^2/2n} γ_n(K_i)^{1/n},$$ and consider a further application in the direction of the Gaussian correlation inequality, together with the rigidity for both inequalities.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Fractional Capacitary-Distance Hardy Inequalities
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $d\in\mathbb N$, $p\in(1,\infty)$, $p':=\frac{p}{p-1}$, and $s\in(0,\min\{1+\frac1p,\frac dp\})$. For an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, let $F:=\mathbb{R}^d\setminusΩ$. For any $α\in(0,1]$ and $x\inΩ$, let \begin{align*} d_{α,s,p}(x) :=\inf\left\{r\in(0,\infty): \frac{\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{F\cap B(x,r)})} {\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}(\overline{B(x,r)})}\geα\right\}, \end{align*} where $\operatorname{cap}_{s,p}$ is the capacity associated with the fractional Sobolev energy $[\,\cdot\,]_{s,p}^p$. In this article, we prove that there exists a positive constant $C$, depending only on $d$, $s$, and $p$, such that, for any $α\in(0,1]$ and $u\in C_{\rm c}^\infty(Ω)$, \begin{align*} \int_Ω\frac{|u(x)|^p}{d_{α,s,p}(x)^{sp}}\,dx \le Cα^{-p'}[u]_{s,p}^p. \end{align*} We also show that both the exponent $p'$ in $α^{-p'}$ as $α\to0^+$ over the class of all open sets and the range $s\in(0,1+\frac1p)$ within $sp<d$ are sharp. Our proofs use variational minimization, equilibrium measures on trees, and weighted Hardy inequalities.

Functional Analysis.title: Regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities via Optimal Transport and Study of Equality Cases
Functional Analysis.summary: We consider regularized Brascamp-Lieb inequalities using the theory of optimal transportation, more precisely an anisotropic version of Caffarelli's contraction theorem. Furthermore, we provide a full picture concerning the issues of finiteness of the Brascamp-Lieb constant and of the existence of Gaussian extremizers, and completely determine all optimizers. The characterization of equality cases requires several new ideas to deal with difficulties, which do not appear for the non-regularized Brascamp-Lieb datum. Finally, we give applications retrieving Brascamp-Lieb-type inequalities with respect to the Gaussian measure and a regularized hypercontractivity inequality.
Functional Analysis.comment: 64 pages, added a new proof of the fact that dual extremizable Brascamp-Lieb data are Gaussian extremizable, expanded technical details, corrected typos and mistakes, improved the structure of Section 4, added references

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp Weak-Type Inequalities for Scalar and Matrix Weights
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $p\in(1,\infty)$ and $p':=\frac p{p-1}$. In this article, we establish a mixed multiplier weak-type inequality with weight dependence $[w]_{A_p}^{\frac1p}[w]_{A_\infty}^{\max\{\frac1p,\frac1{p'}\}}$ for scalar $A_p$ weights and Calderón--Zygmund operators whose modulus of continuity satisfies the Dini condition. As a consequence, we obtain the sharp exponent $\max\{1,\frac2p\}$ of $[w]_{A_p}$ in the corresponding pure $A_p$ bound. Moreover, in the matrix-weighted setting, we prove the sharpness of the exponent $1+\min\{\frac1p,\frac1{p(p-1)}\}$ of $[W]_{\mathcal A_p}$ in the known multiplier weak-type inequality for the Hilbert transform.

Functional Analysis.title: Auxiliary Gradient-Flow Solvers for Generalized Newtonian Models
Functional Analysis.summary:
We introduce an auxiliary gradient-flow framework for variational problems with generalized Newtonian structure governed by an N-function. The key idea is to replace the nonlinear constitutive dependence on the gradient, or symmetric gradient, by an auxiliary scalar variable representing its squared magnitude. This shifts the nonlinearity from the state equation to the auxiliary variable, yielding a sequence of uniformly elliptic weighted linear problems.
  At the continuous level, we construct an auxiliary energy on a metric space adapted to the growth of the underlying N-function. In this topology, we prove lower semicontinuity, geodesic $λ$-convexity, and exponential convergence of the associated minimizing-movement scheme. At the finite element level, we derive a metric gradient flow through an explicit Riesz map, prove global well-posedness of the resulting semi-discrete ODE, and establish convergence to the finite element solution of the Euler--Lagrange equations of the generalized Newtonian energy. For the $p$-Laplacian and $p$-Stokes models, this gives a rigorous convergence result for $4/3\le p\le 4$, $p\ne2$, with asymptotic rate estimates beyond this range.
  We also propose practical time discretizations, including an operator-splitting scheme that gives the \kac iteration as a special case, and an adaptive pseudo-transient method that can be implemented using scalable linear solvers. Numerical experiments for power-law, Carreau--Yasuda, regularized Bingham, and optimal-design models demonstrate robustness, mesh-independent iteration counts in the tested regimes, and performance that matches or outperforms Newton's method.

Functional Analysis.title: Bourin's Crossed-Heinz Inequality in the Frobenius Norm
Functional Analysis.summary: For positive semidefinite matrices $A,B \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and $0<t<1$, we establish the sharp quantitative Frobenius-norm inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t}+B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2+4t(1-t)\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2 \le \|A+B\|_{\mathrm{F}}^2$ for every dimension $n\ge1$. In particular, Bourin's crossed-Heinz inequality $\|A^t B^{1-t}+B^t A^{1-t}\|_{\mathrm{F}} \le \|A+B\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ holds with equality if and only if $A=B$.

Functional Analysis.title: Approximation numbers of Hankel Operators on Weighted Fock Spaces and the Berger--Coburn Phenomenon
Functional Analysis.summary:
Let $\varphi\in C^2(\mathbb{C}^n)$ be a real-valued weight whose real Hessian is uniformly positive definite and bounded. For $0<p<\infty$, $1\le q<\infty$, and possibly unbounded symbols $f$, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for prescribed decay of the approximation numbers of Hankel operators $H_f$ from weighted Fock spaces $F^p(\varphi)$ to weighted Lebesgue spaces $L^q(\varphi)$ in terms of the non-increasing rearrangement of the IDA function of $f$. We also characterize membership in the approximation ideals $\mathfrak A_s(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ and their weak counterparts $\mathfrak A_{s,\infty}(F^p(\varphi),L^q(\varphi))$ for $0<s<\infty$. The symbol criteria involve Lorentz, Lorentz--Zygmund, and Copson--Lorentz spaces. Our approach also yields the converse to the sufficient condition in [15], thereby completing the characterization of prescribed singular value decay for Hankel operators on a broad class of weighted Bergman spaces.
  For the pair $H_f$ and $H_{\bar f}$ on weighted Fock spaces, we characterize simultaneous decay of their approximation numbers and simultaneous membership in these ideals in terms of the mean oscillation function of $f$. For bounded symbols, we establish the Berger--Coburn phenomenon for both ideals in sharp exponent ranges. A new feature in the case $p<2<q$ is that the Berger--Coburn equivalence holds for $s_0(p,q)<s\le1$, where the sharp threshold $s_0(p,q)$ is strictly less than $1$.

Functional Analysis.title: A Bourgain-Gromov problem on non-compact Sobolev-Lorentz embeddings
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the non-compact Sobolev embeddings into the optimal scale of Lorentz spaces, $W_0^mL^{p,q}(Ω) \to L^{\frac{dp}{d - mp},r}(Ω)$, where $Ω\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$, $1 \leq m < d$, $0<q<r\le\infty$ with $1<p<\frac dm$ or $p=q=1$. We show that these embeddings are finitely strictly singular with certain upper bounds on the decay rate of the Bernstein numbers. We reduce the Sobolev embeddings to embeddings of Besov spaces and sequence spaces, which simplifies the previous methods by Bourgain-Gromov and Lang-Mihula.
Functional Analysis.comment: Final version, 6 pages. Published in Constructive Approximation

Functional Analysis.title: A Classification Theorem on Non-compact Embeddings between Besov Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We analyze the embedding properties between Besov spaces, defined on the total space $\mathbb R^n$ and on bounded domains. We give a complete classification on whether or not these embedding maps satisfy certain weaker forms of compactness characterized by the so-called strictly and finitely strictly singular conditions. The result extends the recent findings on Sobolev embeddings by offering a refined description of the quality of non-compactness in the setting of Besov spaces.
Functional Analysis.comment: Final version, 16 pages. Published in Mathematische Annalen

Functional Analysis.title: On the Fourier Mean Bodies of a Convex Body
Functional Analysis.summary:
In 1998, R. Gardner and G. Zhang introduced the radial $p$th mean bodies $R_pK$ of a convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$, $p>-1$, which have since become important objects in geometric tomography. In this paper, we study the Fourier transforms of the radial functions of $R_pK$. This leads to a new family of star-shaped sets $F_pK$, which we call the Fourier $p$th mean bodies of $K$. We prove Fourier inversion formulas connecting $R_pK$ and $F_pK$, realizing them as $p$-intersection bodies in the sense of A. Koldobsky. We develop the basic affine geometry of $F_pK$; this includes affine covariance and monotonicity properties.
  We give sufficient conditions for the compactness of $F_pK$ in terms of the decay of $|\widehat{χ_K}|^2$. We show that $F_pK$ is an origin-symmetric convex body for every $0<p\le1$. This range is sharp in general: already for the cube, $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not convex for $1<p<2$ and $n\geq 2,$ while $F_p[-1,1]^n$ is not compact for $p\geq 2$. We further investigate the features Fourier mean bodies share with intersection bodies: we prove Hensley-type estimates for $F_pK$ when $K$ is isotropic and investigate an affine isoperimetric inequality.
Functional Analysis.comment: eight pictures; v3: Improved Hensley-type theorem, rewrote introduction and abstract and simplified proofs

Functional Analysis.title: Continuous improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for Gaussian random vectors
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish continuous versions of the improved Hölder and reverse Hölder inequalities for correlated Gaussian random vectors, where a finite covariance matrix is replaced by a covariance operator acting on a Hilbert space of parameter fields. Under operator comparisons between the covariance and the exponent multiplier, we prove both inequalities and characterize equality in terms of a compatible probability density on the underlying Gaussian space. We further describe this density as a product of independent factors on common eigenspaces and a Gaussian factor whose mean and covariance satisfy explicit algebraic conditions. In the reverse setting, positive and negative exponents may coexist. The continuous product is defined by ordered truncation, allowing zeros in the positive-exponent factors. The equality proof combines an exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck semigroup comparison, a spectral gap away from the kernel of the governing operator difference, and characteristic-function deconvolution. We also treat exponential quadratic functions without requiring a uniform positive-definiteness margin on the precision matrices.

Functional Analysis.title: Boundedness of a Schur multiplier on the Schatten p-class, $1 < p \neq 2 < \infty$, does not imply complete boundedness
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove the existence of a bounded Schur multiplier on the Schatten class $S_p(\ell_2)$ which is not completely bounded when $1<p\ne 2<\infty$, which confirms Pisier's conjecture (1998).

Functional Analysis.title: A counterexample to the one-supremum conjecture and sharp logarithmic weighted bounds for Calderón--Zygmund operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We give a negative answer to the one-supremum conjecture of Hytönen and Lacey~\cite[Remark~1.3]{HL}, in the strong-type form stated by Lerner and Moen~\cite[Conjecture~1.3, formula~(9)]{LM}. The conjecture asks whether the mixed $A_p$--$A_\infty$ characteristics $K_p(w)$ and $K_{p'}(σ)$, with both factors evaluated on the same cube, control Calderón--Zygmund operators without a logarithmic loss. For every $1<p<\infty$, we construct explicit weights for which $K_p(w)+K_{p'}(σ)\eqsim_p m$, but one fixed Hilbert transform has weighted norm at least $m(1+\log m)^{γ_p}$, where $γ_p=\max\{1/p,1/p'\}$. Thus the proposed bound fails even for a fixed singular integral. The counterexample also extends to a fixed Riesz transform in each dimension $n\ge2$. We further establish a logarithmically corrected bound for Calderón--Zygmund operators, with powers $1/p'$ and $1/p$ on the respective one-supremum terms. Together, the lower and upper bounds identify $γ_p$ as the optimal common logarithmic exponent and give the sharp worst-case growth $(1+\log A)^{γ_p}$ under the constraint $[w]_{A_p}\le A$. The results show why information from any one cube cannot fully capture the accumulation of a singular integral across many scales.

Functional Analysis.title: A proof of the constant-width numerical range conjecture
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that the numerical range of a complex matrix has constant width \(d\) if and only if it is a closed disk of radius \(d/2\). The width in each direction is the gap between the extreme eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix. When that gap is constant, the midpoint of the projected interval is a rational function of the direction parameter. An operator norm bound and reversal of direction then show that the midpoints are projections of a single point, the disk's center.

Functional Analysis.title: The Operator Systems of Hankel Matrices and Complex Polynomials
Functional Analysis.summary: Using polynomial matrix spectral factorization, we establish a complete order duality between $(n+1)\times(n+1)$ Hankel matrices and complex polynomials of degree at most $2n$ on the real line. The projection construction and trace pairing identify $e_n(t)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}t^{2j}$ as the polynomial order unit corresponding to the restriction of the matrix trace. The Cayley transform relates these matrix orders to Toeplitz matrices and truncated trigonometric polynomials, but for $n\geq 2$ the polynomial systems with units $e_n$ and $(1+t^2)^n$ are not unital order isomorphic. We establish polynomial minimality and Hankel maximality, and characterize positivity of $C^*$-algebra-valued block Hankel matrices through completely positive maps on the polynomial operator system. An augmented Vandermonde decomposition describes polynomial states as trace-one positive Hankel matrices, with extreme states given by normalized evaluations and the leading-coefficient functional at infinity.

Functional Analysis.title: Weighted orbits of hypercyclic vectors on F-spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We study $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclicity of weighted orbits $λ_nT^nx$ for continuous linear operators $T$ on complex F-spaces, where $\mathcal{F}$ is a Furstenberg family with the cut--shift--and--paste (CuSP) property. We characterize the scalar sequences for which weighted hypercyclicity always implies ordinary hypercyclicity: their nonzero values must be bounded and bounded away from zero. This condition also guarantees weight removal for every Furstenberg family with the CuSP property. For the converse inclusion, we prove that, for any Furstenberg family $\mathcal{F}$ with the CuSP property, a bounded scalar sequence preserves all $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclic vectors if its backward-shift $ω$-limit system is distal and does not contain the zero sequence. For chaotic operators, minimality of this system suffices. In particular, every complex nilsequence which is not identically zero preserves $\mathcal{F}$-hypercyclicity, and equality holds when its nonzero values are bounded away from zero. We also obtain simultaneous weighted return results and stability under unimodular weights with asymptotically trivial multiplicative differences.

Functional Analysis.title: On Talagrand Type
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that for every $1<s<2$ and every $0<δ<1$, Rademacher type $s$ coincides with Talagrand type $(s,ψ_{s,δ})$. Together with the result of Cordero-Erausquin and Eskenazis for $s=2$, this yields the equivalence for every $1<s\le2$ and every $0<δ<1$.
Functional Analysis.comment: Main result strengthened to cover all $0<δ<1$ for $1<s<2$; exposition revised and a figure added

Functional Analysis.title: On rough ideal convergence
Functional Analysis.summary:
We continue the study of ideal convergence for sequences $(x_n)$ with values in a topological space $X$ with respect to a family $\{F_η:η\in X\}$ of subsets of $X$ with $η\in F_η$, where each $F_η$ measures the allowed ``roughness'' of convergence toward $η$.
  More precisely, after introducing the corresponding notions of cluster and limit points, we prove several inclusion and invariance properties, discuss their structural properties, and give examples showing that the rough notions are genuinely different from the classical ideal ones.

Functional Analysis.title: Singularity removal in nonlocal operator inequalities on domains and applications: A $((Q,1)\implies (\GO,ρ))$ theorem
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that certain classes of nonlocal integral inequalities on bounded uniform domains, involving operators, may be reduced to the local analogues on cubes without the singular weight. The theory applies to two-sided inverse doubling and quasi-monotone kernels with some moment conditions, and with a left-hand-side operator with average bi-Lipschitz properties. Direct applications to fractional semi-norm rigidity inequalities in nonlocal continuum mechanics, such as fractional Korn's Inequalities, Geometric Rigidity Estimates, and rigidity of some types of affine deformations, that are common in mechanics, are presented.
Functional Analysis.comment: 36 pages. Title updated. Theorem 2.4 on norm/semi-norm equivalence is added, 2 new examples added in Section 5

Functional Analysis.title: Quantum Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport in spacetime through spatiotemporal Kirkwood-Dirac distributions and spatiotemporal states
Functional Analysis.summary: Monge-Kantorovich optimal transport is a mathematical framework that determines the most efficient way to transform one probability distribution into another while minimizing a given cost function. Its central constructions include the Wasserstein distances, which quantify the space of probability distributions, and dual formulations that link to convex analysis. Its standard quantum generalization replaces probability distributions with density operators and cost function with positive semidefinite cost operator, which should be regarded as spatial quantum optimal transport. In this work, we propose the quantum optimal transport problem in spacetime through the spatiotemporal phase-space Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distribution and spatiotemporal states and through spatiotemporal state. We show that the two formalisms are equivalent and related via spatiotemporal operator frames. In the Kirkwood-Dirac phase-space formalism, the spatiotemporal distribution and the cost function are complex-valued, and the spatiotemporal couplings are Kirkwood-Dirac quasiprobability distributions that yield the correct marginals for the local states. In the spatiotemporal state formalism, the cost operators are generally non-Hermitian, and the spatiotemporal couplings are generally non-Hermitian and yield the correct reduced local states. The Margenau-Hill phase-space distribution gives rise to a real-valued optimal transport in spatiotemporal phase space; in the spatiotemporal state formalism, this corresponds to a Hermitian spatiotemporal coupling state. We give a rigorous definitions and a careful discussion of its duality. We also introduce a spatiotemporal quantum Wasserstein metric based on a metric in spatiotemporal phase spaces and show that it satisfies the metric axioms.

Functional Analysis.title: Separability and Submetrizability in Locally Convex Spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce the property of countable separation for a locally convex Hausdorff space $X$ and relate it to the existence of a metrizable coarser topology. Building on this, we demonstrate how the separability of $X$ is equivalent to the existence of a locally convex topology on the dual $X'$ that is metrizable and coarser than the weak topology $σ(X', X)$. This result generalizes known conditions for separability and provides a precise duality between separability and metrizability. We also show how to derive new and known conditions for the separability of $X$ from this characterization.
Functional Analysis.comment: This version of the article has been accepted for publication, after peer review but is not the Version of Record and does not reflect post-acceptance improvements, or any corrections. The Version of Record is available online

Functional Analysis.title: Incremental Roseland: Batch-wise Landmark Diffusion via Kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève Update
Functional Analysis.summary: Landmark diffusion (Roseland) computes a diffusion-map-style spectral embedding from the singular value decomposition of a degree-normalized data-to-landmark kernel matrix, at a cost far below that of full diffusion maps. It assumes, however, that all data are available at once. We introduce incremental Roseland (iRoseland), which casts the landmark affinity as a row-growing matrix whose SVD can be updated with a kernelized Sequential Karhunen--Loève (SKL) scheme. Degre correction is handled by a first order expansion about a reference mean kernel row and so that the landmark-side eigenbasis may be recovered from a single landmark-by-landmark eigendecomposition at each step. The presented method requires only a single pass over the data and runs in bounded-memory with state independent of the number of points processed. A forgetting factor lets the method track drifting distributions, and a sample-size-invariant embedding keeps outputs comparable across time. Experiments show agreement with Roseland to round-off on stationary data, and accuracy that exceeds equal-memory Roseland by an order of magnitude on long streams. On drifting data, we observe large gains from forgetting with a window matched to the drift.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlinear wave superpositions and quasi-rectifiable Lie modules
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper presents a study of nonlinear superpositions of Riemann wave solutions admitted by quasilinear hyperbolic first-order systems of partial differential equations. In particular, we focus on the Euler system and non-elastic wave superpositions that cannot be decomposed into pairwise independent interactions of waves. A crucial tool for this analysis is the property of quasi-rectifiability of the families of vector fields determined by this system. It imposes certain conditions to be satisfied by the commutators of these vector fields. They enable us to find a parametrization of the region of superpositions of Riemann waves which leads to a simplification of the initial system of equations. In order to identify non-elastic superpositions we prove that a class of Lie modules associated with them can be uniquely transformed into a real Lie algebra through an angle-preserving transformation. We are then able to select a particular basis of vector fields associated with a given module which ensures the property of quasi-rectifiability. That, in turn, allows us to construct the reduced form of the Euler system for which a non-elastic superposition of two Riemann waves is then derived analytically. A study of the geometry of the manifold of non-elastic wave superpositions in terms of deformations of submanifolds corresponding to the Lie algebras is performed. Finally, we adapt the described approach to the general form of a hydrodynamic-type system i.e., to arbitrary Lie modules of vector fields associated with such a system, providing the criteria for their quasi-rectifiability. A geometric interpretation of non-elastic wave superpositions in this system is given.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Infinite cascades for the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square torus
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For each $1<s<2$ we construct a solution of the defocusing cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the square two-torus with initial data in $H^s$ whose $H^s$ norm tends to infinity as $t\to+\infty$. The growth can be arbitrarily slow. More precisely, the squared norm agrees, up to a bounded error at all positive times, with the number of selected axial frequencies $K_j$ for which $K_j^s\le t$. The central construction couples a finite tree of orthogonal frequency pairs to a periodic one-dimensional solution of the same equation. Each transfer leaves a nonvanishing Fourier coefficient on the horizontal axis. Control on an entire half-line allows successive transfers to retain the coefficients produced earlier.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This version extends the results presented in https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.35044186

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Geometric Calderón Problem for Differential Forms
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish boundary determination and global partial-data uniqueness for Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential $p$-forms. We derive an explicit recursion for its full symbol and determine the full boundary jet of the metric, modulo conformal gauge in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$. For $p\geq1$, partial data determine metrics that are analytic in the interior and near the measured boundary subset, up to isometry or conformal equivalence. The global uniqueness relies on a new projection-kernel embedding that detects the unobserved boundary through rank loss and small eigenvalues. We also establish global partial-data uniqueness for smooth metrics with harmonic curvature, using elliptic-transport unique continuation and, in the critical dimension, conformal-geodesic coordinates. A Weyl nondegeneracy condition further upgrades conformal equivalence to isometry.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An alternative proof of the Keel--Tao endpoint Strichartz estimates
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we give an alternative proof of the abstract endpoint Strichartz estimates proved by Keel and Tao. Our method is based on the near-far decomposition technique, which was developed in a recent work by Toyoshima and the author.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness of coexistence states in diffusive predator-prey models, at the occasion of the 100th anniversary of the first publication of V. Volterra on the predator-prey system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper analyzes the existence and uniqueness of coexistence states for a generalized class of diffusive Lotka--Volterra predator-prey models involving spatial heterogeneities and mixed boundary conditions of non-classical type. Its main findings are the following: (a) after characterizing the existence of coexistence states, the uniqueness of the coexistence state is established, in a multidimensional context, near the curves of change of stability of the semi-trivial positive solutions of the model, (b) the one-dimensional uniqueness theorem of López-Gómez and Pardo [65,67] is sharpened up to cover the case of mixed boundary conditions of nonclassical type, (c) the multidimensional uniqueness theorem of [66] is substantially generalized up to deal with variable coefficients, and it is complemented with the global attractivity of the unique coexistence state, which excludes any Hopf bifurcation, (d) assuming Neumann boundary conditions and constant coefficients, we can sharpen, very substantially, the pioneering results of Leung [46] establishing the the constant coexistence state is the unique coexistence state of the model. In this setting, we can also prove that the constant coexistence state is a global attractor with respect to the positive solutions of the associated parabolic problem, and that it is non-degenerate, even for general differential operators, not necessarily self-adjoint. \par As this paper is a personal homage to Volterra [92] at the centenary of the publication of his foundational paper on the predator-prey model, based on the field data of D'Ancona [4], this paper begins with a review of the first scientific works in population dynamics of Vito Volterra and Umberto D'Ancona.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Higher-order estimates for $p$-harmonic functions in the plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Closing a longstanding gap in the theory, we establish uniform interior $C^{k,β}$ estimates for planar $p$-harmonic functions with $1<p<2$. These estimates hold for every integer $k\ge2$ and every $0<β<1$ such that $k+β<s(p)$, where $s(p)$ is the optimal regularity order identified by Iwaniec and Manfredi. As consequences, we obtain decay estimates at critical points, a Liouville theorem with optimal growth exponent, and uniform higher-order estimates for the flux of planar $q$-harmonic functions with $q>2$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The Lean code and a description of the formalization process are available at https://github.com/na0b/phigherorder-lean

Analysis of PDEs.title: On least energy solutions for a critical nonlinear Schrödinger system with $K$-wise interaction: the competitive case
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study least energy fully non-trivial solutions of a nonlinear Schrödinger system with Sobolev critical nonlinearities and repulsive interaction involving all the components at the same time. Under the scalar Brezis-Nirenberg assumptions on the linear coefficients, we prove existence of least energy fully non-trivial solutions on smooth bounded domains for every negative coupling in dimensions \(N=5,6\). For \(N=3,4\), due to the lack of $L^2$-integrability of the Aubin-Talenti bubbles, the same conclusion holds under additional sufficient assumptions, and in particular we provide an explicit condition on the domain and coefficients. We also investigate the strong competition limit, and characterize fully non-trivial limiting profiles as minimizers of a partially segregated variational problem. A preliminary study of independent interest concerns the whole-space problem. For general admissible \(K\), we determine the component-wise Nehari infimum and prove that it is not attained, even in the radial class. Finally, when the linear coefficients coincide, we establish a sharp criterion for the existence of positive synchronized solutions in terms of the strength of the competition.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,α}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we prove that for $3\leq k\leq n-1$, continuous $k$-convex solutions of the $σ_{k}$ equation on bounded strictly $(k-1)$-convex $C^{3}$ domains $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^{n}$ with $C^{3}$ boundary values and positive continuous density on $\overlineΩ$ belong to $W^{2,p}(Ω)$ for every $1<p<\infty$. If, in addition, the density is $C^α$ on $\overlineΩ$, $0<α<1$, the solutions belong to $C^{2,α}(\overlineΩ)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Partial Regularity of Weakly Pseudoholomorphic Maps Into Projective Algebraic Varieties
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every $m\geq2$, we prove that a weakly pseudoholomorphic $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}$ map from a real-analytic almost complex $2m$-manifold into a projective algebraic variety has a countably $(2m-4)$-rectifiable singular set. When $m=2$, the singular set is shown to be locally finite. We first establish both conclusions on smooth almost complex domains under the additional assumption that the pullback of the Fubini--Study form is distributionally closed. We then show that this conservation law follows from the Cauchy--Riemann equation alone on real-analytic domains.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the $L^p$-Neumann problem for divergence form elliptic equations in the upper half-space
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
A central question has been whether the $L^p$-Neumann problem is solvable for some $p\in(1,\infty)$ in the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_+:=\mathbb{R}^n\times(0,\infty)$, $n\geq2$, for second-order uniformly elliptic equations in divergence form whose coefficients are either independent of the transverse variable or satisfy the Dahlberg--Kenig--Pipher (DKP) condition. We answer this question in the negative for both classes, even for matrices whose symmetric part is the identity. The two examples have the same nonzero Neumann datum $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ of mean zero. Although $g$ is bounded and belongs to the real Hardy space $H^1(\mathbb R^n)$, neither equation admits a weak solution with this datum whose gradient has a non-tangential maximal function in $L^p(\mathbb R^n)$ for any $1\leq p<\infty$. For the variational solution $u$ associated with either matrix $A$, the non-tangential maximal functions of $\nabla_x u$, $\partial_tu$ and $(A\nabla u)_{n+1}$ each have infinite $L^p$ norm for every $1\leq p\leq\infty$.
  In the example with coefficients independent of the transverse variable, the equation in the interior is the Laplace equation. The matrix in the DKP example has finite $L^2$-type Carleson discrepancy from the identity. This shows that solvability of the $L^p$-Neumann problem is not stable under arbitrary Carleson perturbations of the identity. For a suitable choice of the coefficients in the lower half-space, the $L^2$ non-tangential maximal and uniform slice estimates fail for both the tangential gradient and the transverse derivative of the associated single layer potential. The $L^2$ estimate for the tangential gradient of its boundary trace also fails. We explain the role of the coefficients below the boundary and prove the $L^2$ layer potential estimates for the reflected extension when the DKP norm is sufficiently small.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Fourier--Galerkin Methods for Subwavelength Resonances in two-dimensional Acoustic Metamaterials
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We present a Fourier--Galerkin asymptotic framework for the analysis and computation of subwavelength resonances in two-dimensional scattering problems in finite domains. Starting from the boundary integral formulation, we apply a Fourier--Galerkin discretization to derive an explicit finite-dimensional effective matrix whose kernel characterizes the resonant frequencies. In the subwavelength regime, we obtain asymptotic expansions of this matrix in terms of $ω$ and the material contrast, identifying the leading-order operators and their kernel structure.
  This reduction transforms the resonance problem into a low-dimensional nonlinear eigenvalue problem, avoiding large-scale discretizations and global root-search procedures. The entries of the effective matrix are explicitly computable and admit fast evaluation using FFT-based quadrature. The resulting approach provides an efficient and robust computational framework for resonances in general smooth geometries.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharpness of the Osgood threshold for anomalous dissipation and non-uniqueness in passive scalar transport
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that for any concave, non-Osgood modulus of continuity $ω$, there exists a divergence-free velocity field $u\in L^\infty([0,1];C^ω(\mathbb T^2))$ and an initial data $f_0\in C^\infty(\mathbb T^2)$ such that the solutions of the associated advection-diffusion equation exhibit anomalous dissipation. This establishes the sharpness of the Osgood threshold for anomalous dissipation. It follows as a corollary of our main result that the Osgood condition is also sharp for the uniqueness of bounded solutions to the transport equation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Quadratic splitting for a weighted Monge--Ampère equation on $(0,\infty)^l\times\R^m$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study a Monge--Ampère equation arising from the existence problem for complete Kähler--Einstein metrics with zero Ricci curvature on divisor complements. We prove a splitting theorem for nonnegative smooth strictly convex solutions on a product of positive half lines and a Euclidean space. The potential and its first derivatives extend continuously to the boundary. The directional derivative in the equation is positive in the interior and vanishes on the boundary. After an affine change of variables, the solution is the sum of a function on the product of half lines and a positive definite quadratic form in the Euclidean variables. No growth condition or homogeneity is assumed.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Exponential boundary stabilization of the KdV--KdV system with time-varying delay: the nonlinear case
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider a Boussinesq system of KdV--KdV type on a bounded interval, with a boundary feedback that includes a damping term with a time-varying delayed term. Although the exponential stability of the linearized system was established in [1] by a Lyapunov approach, global existence and stabilization for the nonlinear problem remained open. Here, we prove that, for sufficiently small initial data and under a suitable restriction on the interval length, the nonlinear system admits a unique global solution whose energy decays exponentially. In particular, we provide an explicit decay rate and a quantitative smallness condition on the initial energy. Our approach combines a Lyapunov argument with well-posedness estimates that are uniform under time translations of the delay, allowing the solutions to be continued globally.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Formal contact-line regimes in the vanishing-slip limit of the thin-film equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We analyze the evolution of thin liquid droplets in the lubrication approximation with different slip conditions at the liquid-solid interface. Motivated by the classical no-slip paradox which states that the Navier-Stokes equations with a no-slip boundary condition require unphysical infinite dissipation during droplet spreading, we focus on the limit of vanishing slip. We show that in the no-slip limit three fundamentally different classes of limiting solutions are approached, each of them corresponding to a different scaling of the microscopic contact angle as the regularization parameter vanishes. These findings suggest that the thin-film equation with no slip supports a rich family of physically admissible solutions, provided one interprets the no-slip thin film equation as the asymptotic limit of models which regularized slip conditions. Even though the large apparent contact angles in some of these solutions seem incompatible with the lubrication approximation, a refined analysis shows that the underlying physical variables remain consistent with the assumptions for the lubrication approximation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Foliations by constant spacetime mean curvature surfaces for asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data sets
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct an exhaustive family of constant spacetime mean curvature (STCMC) surfaces for initial data sets close to the anti-de Sitter-Schwarzschild hyperboloid. In particular, we obtain such a foliation as the long time limit of the volume preserving spacetime mean curvature flow starting from the constant mean curvature foliation constructed by Neves-Tian (Geom. Funct. Anal., 2009). As an application, inspired by the definition of STCMC center of mass for initial data sets proposed in the asymptotically Euclidean setting by Cederbaum-Sakovich (Calc. Var. PDE, 2021), we study the center of mass of an asymptotically hyperboloidal initial data set.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Comments are welcome! Decay hypothesis improved with respect to the author's talk at the KTH conference "Geometric Analysis: Parabolic and Elliptic Methods", June 2026

Analysis of PDEs.title: Flexibility for the Monge-Ampere system implies flexibility for isometric immersions into Riemannian manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that any flexibility result for the Monge-Ampère system implies the corresponding flexibility result for the isometric immersion system, with the same Hölder regularity. We treat the general isometric immersion system, in which both the source and the ambient metrics are arbitrary Hölder regular, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. Combining this implication with existing results for the Monge-Ampère system, we obtain new ${C}^{1,α}$ flexibility statement for isometric immersions with arbitrary source and ambient metrics. To our knowledge, these are the first such results for non-Euclidean ambient metrics.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Polar director structure of SmAP$_\text{F}$ phase of bent-core liquid crystals in thin planar cells with bias electric field
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the polar director structure in thin planar cells filled with bent-core liquid crystals in the ferroelectric smectic-A phase (SmAP$_\text{F}$). We analyze a continuum phenomenological model proposed in the physics literature and present proofs establishing the existence of weak solutions and conditional uniqueness of nonconstant solutions. We further investigate the qualitative properties of nontrivial solutions and examine the effects of a bias electric field, surface anchoring, and cell thickness on the polar director configuration. Our results are consistent with previous experimental and numerical simulations reported in the physics literature. In addition, our analysis reveals new parameter-dependent behaviors supported by our numerical simulations and extends results reported from previous literature.

Analysis of PDEs.title: All Serrin bands are unduloidal
Analysis of PDEs.summary: A Serrin domain is a smooth domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^n$ where Serrin's overdetermined problem for $Δu+2=0$ admits a positive solution $u$. In the plane, Fall-Minlend-Weth and Dávila-del Pino-Musso-Wheeler constructed periodic Serrin bands close to a flat strip and a singular chain of tangent disks, respectively. More recently, Cerezo-Fernández-Mira constructed a real-analytic $1$-parameter family of unduloidal Serrin bands interpolating between these two limiting geometries. In this work, we prove that every Serrin band in $\mathbb{R}^2$ belongs to this canonical unduloidal family.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 37 pages. We explained in more detail several arguments, simplified some of them, fixed some typos and expanded the introduction. The results remain unchanged with respect to the first version

Analysis of PDEs.title: A variational approach to an anisotropic nonlocal porous medium equation with drift
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study nonlocal porous-medium equations driven by anisotropic Riesz-type repulsive interactions and an external confining potential. The pressure is determined by convolution with an interaction potential of the form $$ W(x)=|x|^{-s}Ω\left(\frac{x}{|x|}\right), \qquad d-2<s<d, $$ where $Ω$ is a smooth, even, and strictly positive angular profile. For quadratic confinement and $s\in(d-2,d)\cap(0,5]$, under suitable positivity assumptions on the anisotropic kernels, we prove that the unique energy minimizer is the only steady state among bounded continuous probability densities. We then establish the long-time convergence of global weak solutions to this equilibrium, both locally and globally in Hölder norms. To obtain these results, we derive uniform $L^p$, $L^\infty$, and Hölder estimates, adapting the regularity theory for fractional porous-medium equations to the anisotropic setting. We also construct global weak solutions through a minimizing-movement scheme in Wasserstein space, establish the corresponding energy-dissipation inequality, and prove a Talagrand-type transport inequality.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Multiplicity of positive solutions for degenerate nonlocal $p$-Laplacian problems without monotonicity of the normalized reaction
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study degenerate nonlocal Dirichlet problems driven by the $p$-Laplacian, with diffusion depending on weighted sums of integral powers of the solution. Under explicit sign, spectral and size conditions, we obtain two positive solutions for each bounded positivity interval of the diffusion coefficient with zero endpoint values. Neither monotonicity of the normalized reaction $f(x,t)/t^{p-1}$ nor uniqueness of the frozen problem is required. The proof combines Schauder's theorem on a product space of a scalar parameter and a function with subsolution bounds and an energy estimate. The multiplicity result also persists under uniformly small continuous perturbations of the nonlocal functional, including perturbations that do not preserve order.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp potential and Brenier map $W_2$-stability for log-concave sources
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study quantitative stability of Brenier potentials and maps under changes of the target measure. Let $κ>0$, for a $κ$-strongly log-concave source $ρ$, possibly with a non-smooth potential, the normalized transport potentials satisfy \[ \left\Vert u_μ-u_ν\right\Vert _{L^{2}(ρ)}\leqslant\left( 1/κ\right) ^{1/2}W_{2}\left( μ,ν\right) \] for arbitrary targets with finite second moments. This readily yields a Poincaré inequality for $κ$-strongly log-concave sources. The coefficient $(1/κ)^{1/2}$ is shown to be optimal. The proof relies on a probabilistic interpretation of cell energies and the subsequent variance decomposition. Interpolation from potential to map then yields the map stability for targets in a common compact set, \[ \left\Vert T_μ-T_ν\right\Vert _{L^{2}(ρ)}\leqslant \operatorname{Const} \cdot W_{2}\left( μ,ν\right) ^{1/3}. \] Sharpness of the order for both the potential and map stability are established. This clarifies a long- standing limitation in topological embedding: representing distributions by their Brenier maps preserves convergence, but it need not preserve local distances.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<θ<π/2$, we consider \[
  σ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)
  =
  f(ξ)h^{p-1}\frac{ρ^{k+1}}{\varphi(ρ)},
  \qquad
  ρ=(h^2+|\nabla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $\nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A unified Sobolev framework for long-wave limits of the Gross-Pitaevskii equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We present a unified justification of the KdV, Airy, inviscid Burgers, and Whitham approximations for the one-dimensional Gross-Pitaevskii equation in Sobolev spaces. Using energy estimates for its Madelung formulation, we establish quantitative error bounds on the natural time scales of the respective approximations. The analysis covers different long-wave scaling regimes within a single framework.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Failure of the $L^p$ Neumann problem in bi-Lipschitz images of a ball
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For every $n\geq 2$ we construct a bounded domain $Ω\subset\mathbb R^{n+1}$, which is the image of the unit ball under a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism of $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, and a bounded Neumann datum $g$ with zero mean such that the variational solution $u$ of the Neumann problem with datum $g$ satisfies $\mathcal N(\nabla u)\notin L^1(\partialΩ)$. In particular, the $L^p$ Neumann problem is not solvable in $Ω$ for any $1<p<\infty$, although $Ω$ is a two-sided chord-arc domain whose boundary supports a weak $(1,1)$-Poincaré inequality, and although in this class of domains the Dirichlet and the regularity problems are solvable for some exponents. This answers in the negative a question of C. Kenig, and it also shows that, unlike the solvability of the Dirichlet problem, the solvability of the $L^p$ Neumann problem for some $p\in (1,\infty)$ is not invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms of $\mathbb R^{n+1}$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: About the occurrence of Akhmediev breathers in dispersive systems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Akhmediev breathers are spatially periodic solutions of the NLS equation which are localized in time. We prove a new NLS approximation result for dispersive wave systems, showing that there are solutions to these systems where Akhmediev breathers in the lowest order approximately modulate the underlying wave packet. Since the solutions of the original wave system are quasi-periodic in space, the main challenge is to find an appropriate function space to estimate the approximation error.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper gives a readable and accessible version of the profile-construction part of OpenAI's manuscript "Finite Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes". We regard OpenAI's work as a major advance on the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem. We construct an axisymmetric leading flow that is regular at the axis and sum its lower-order corrections to obtain an approximately self-similar background field. Its Navier-Stokes residual consists of a divergence-form term and a remainder vanishing to infinite order in $1-t$ on fixed similarity sectors. The associated stress and radial shear satisfy the admissible cone condition. The stress need not be small. We introduce a new linear model that provides a clearer explanation of the inner core construction. The cancellation of the divergence-form residual by oscillatory pulses is treated in the companion paper "Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part II: Residual Correction via Oscillatory Pulses" (arXiv:2611.06869). We claim no original mathematical contribution.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: We have reduced the length of the paper from 245 to 182 pages. We claim no original mathematical contribution

Analysis of PDEs.title: On a Fuzzy Landau Equation: I. A Variational Approach
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we introduce a fuzzy Landau equation, where particles interact through delocalised collisions. We establish a variational characterisation that recasts the fuzzy Landau equation within the framework of GENERIC systems (General Equations for Non-Equilibrium Reversible-Irreversible Coupling), obtaining an equivalent characterisation of H-solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global well-posedness and decay estimates of strong solutions to a non-conservative compressible two-fluid model in $L^p$ critical framework
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the global existence and long-time behavior of solutions to a general multidimensional non-conservative compressible two-fluid model satisfying the algebraic capillary pressure relation \(P^{+}(ρ^+)-P^{-}(ρ^-)=f(α^{-}ρ^{-})\) in the $L^p$ critical framework. Our main contributions are twofold. First, under the sharp stability condition \(-\frac{s_{-}^{2}(1,1)}{α^{-}(1,1)}<f^{\prime}(1)<0,\) we establish the global existence and uniqueness of solutions for small perturbations around a linearly stable constant equilibrium. In particular, our result removes the additional negativity assumption required in Evje--Wang--Wen [Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 221:1285--1316, 2016]. Second, assuming in addition that the low-frequency of the initial perturbation is small in a lower-regularity Besov space, we derive optimal decay rates for the solution.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Optimal Stability for Bivariate Weighted Fourth-Order Inequalities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we prove sharp stability estimates for a two-component radial weighted fourth-order Caffarelli--Kohn--Nirenberg inequality in the two radial regimes for which the scalar optimizers are explicitly known and the corresponding spectral non-degeneracy holds. These regimes are \(4-N<α<2,\ \ell=-α\), and \(2<α<N,\ \ell=4(α-2)(N-2)/(N-α)-α\). Let $N\ge 3$, $p=2(N+\ell)/(N-4+α)>2$, \(μ_1,μ_2\geq0\), \(κ>0\), and $r,s>1$ satisfy $r+s=p$. For radial pairs $(u,v)\in X_{\mathrm{rad}}\times X_{\mathrm{rad}}$, we determine the sharp constant $S_{r,s,μ_1,μ_2,κ}$ in the coupled inequality \[ S_{r,s,μ_1,μ_2,κ} \left(\int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^\ell\big(μ_1|u|^p+μ_2|v|^p+pκ|u|^r|v|^s\big)dx\right)^{2/p} \le \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^α\big(|Δu|^2+|Δv|^2\big)dx . \] The sharp constant is expressed through the scalar sharp constant and the minimum of an explicit one-dimensional ratio function. We also characterize all extremals and prove sharp quantitative stability estimates. The stability exponent is determined by the degeneracy of the ratio minimizers: it is quadratic in the non-degenerate case and becomes square-root type in the degenerate case.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Logarithmic Stability for an Inverse Source Problem in a Coupled Nonlinear Helmholtz System
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider an inverse source problem for a coupled nonlinear Helmholtz system motivated by second-harmonic generation. For a known susceptibility bounded away from zero, we prove that small real-valued sources are uniquely determined by the full first Fréchet derivative of the nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann map at a fixed small real boundary value. Under an a priori Sobolev bound, we derive a conditional logarithmic stability estimate. The proof uses linearization, complex geometric optics solutions for a matrix Schrödinger equation, and interpolation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp Sobolev thresholds and rapid rotation for Navier--Stokes equations with fractional horizontal dissipation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the three-dimensional incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb R^3$ with fractional horizontal dissipation $νΛ_h^{2α}$, $0<α\le1$, and a Coriolis force. There is no vertical dissipation. The scaling-critical Sobolev index is $s_c=5/2-2α$. For $0<α<1$, we prove local Hadamard well-posedness in $H^s$ for $s\ge s_c$; for $α=1$, the range is $s>1/2$. At every prescribed finite rotation rate, norm inflation holds in all remaining positive-order Sobolev spaces for classical solutions with smooth compactly supported divergence-free initial data, starting from arbitrarily small $H^s$ data in arbitrarily short time. Thus $H^{s_c}$ is a well-posedness space for $0<α<1$, whereas $H^{1/2}$ exhibits norm inflation for $α=1$. These results give sharp Sobolev thresholds for each finite rotation rate. Throughout the well-posedness range, small data yield global solutions with a rotation-independent smallness threshold, and every fixed datum yields a global solution for sufficiently rapid rotation. The nonlinear solution converges to the linear Stokes--Coriolis evolution uniformly on $[0,\infty)$ and in the global dissipation norm as $|Ω|\to\infty$. For spectrally localized data separated from the vertical frequency axis, the convergence rate is $O(|Ω|^{-γ})$ for every $0<γ<1/2$. For $0<α<1$, the energy estimates close at $s=s_c$ without loss of derivatives in isotropic Sobolev spaces, using Littlewood--Paley decomposition, Sobolev trace inequalities, and localized horizontal product estimates. Below $s_c$, norm inflation follows from an approximation by a fixed smooth Euler solution after rescaling. At $(α,s)=(1,1/2)$, viscosity remains fixed under critical rescaling; the construction instead uses a localized scalar shear and conormal analytic stability estimates uniform in the vertical concentration parameters.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the Critical Exponent for a Time--Space Fractional Reaction--Diffusion Equation with a Slowly Varying Time-Dependent Source
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Fujita critical exponent for the Cauchy problem $\partial_t^αu+(-Δ)^{θ/2}u=h(t)u^p$ in $(0,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^N$, $u(0)=u_0\ge0$, where $α\in(0,1]$, $θ\in(0,2]$, $p>1$, $\partial_t^α$ is the Caputo derivative, and $h(t)\sim t^γ\ell(t)$ for large $t$, with $γ\in\mathbb{R}$ and $\ell$ slowly varying at infinity in the sense of Karamata. For $α=1$ and every $θ\in(0,2]$ we obtain a complete classification. If $γ\le-1$, small data give global solutions for every $p>1$, so there is no Fujita threshold. If $γ>-1$, the critical exponent is $p_c(γ)=1+θ(γ+1)/N$: every nontrivial solution blows up for $1<p<p_c(γ)$, while small global solutions exist for $p>p_c(γ)$. At $p=p_c(γ)$ the slowly varying factor decides: blow-up occurs if $\int_1^\infty t^{-1}\ell(t)dt=\infty$, and small global solutions exist if this integral converges. Hence global existence may occur at the critical exponent, unlike the autonomous case. For $α\in(0,1)$, the memory of the Caputo derivative replaces $γ+1$ by $γ+α$. We prove small-data global existence for every $p>1$ when $γ\le-α$. When $γ>-α$, all nontrivial solutions blow up for $1<p<p_c(γ,α):=1+θ(γ+α)/(Nα)$. If $N<θ$, we also obtain global existence for $p>p_c(γ,α)$, so the classification is complete, and at $p=p_c(γ,α)$ the dichotomy is governed by the boundedness of $\ell$. If $N\geθ$, we obtain global existence for $p>1+(γ+α)/α$, which coincides with $p_c(γ,α)$ when $N=θ$. Finally, a second, purely local blow-up mechanism shows that for $N>θ$ and $γ>αθ/(N-θ)$, $p_c(γ,α)$ is not the Fujita exponent. Our results extend the theorems of Meier (1990) to the nonlocal setting.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global existence for the 1D compressible Euler equations with time-decaying damping and spatial perturbations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional compressible Euler equations with damping coefficient $b(t)+a(x)$, where $b(t)=λ(1+t)^{-μ}$ with $0<μ<1$, $λ>0$, or $μ=1$, $λ>2$, and $a\in C_b^1(\mathbb R)\cap L^1(\mathbb R)$ is nonnegative. We prove global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions for sufficiently small $C_b^1$ perturbations of a constant state, without assuming spatial decay or convergence of the initial data at infinity. No smallness condition is imposed on the spatially dependent damping coefficient, even though its contribution persists for all time. We also obtain decay estimates of order $\varepsilon(1+t)^{-μ}$ for the derivatives $u_t$, $v_t$, and $v_x$, together with a pointwise estimate for $u_x$ involving the spatial coefficient $a(x)$. The main ingredient is a time-uniform $L^\infty$ estimate for an inhomogeneous coupled transport system with a non-small spatial coefficient. Combined with suitable transformations of the Riemann-invariant derivatives, this estimate allows us to control the nonlinear terms and establish global $C^1$ bounds.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Batched Discrepancy Principle for Stochastic Landweber-Kaczmarz Iteration and its Application to EIT
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider an inverse problem given as ill-posed system of possibly nonlinear operator equations between Hilbert spaces. To solve the problem we use a stochastic mini-batch Landweber-Kaczmarz method, drawing uniformly a subset of equations in each step. As an a posteriori stopping rule, we introduce a batched version of the discrepancy principle, in which only the residual of the selected batches is monitored. Under the tangential cone condition, we establish the convergence of the iterates for exact data, the convergence of the regularized iterates for noisy data under an a priori choice of the stopping index, and the convergence of the method when it is terminated by the proposed batched discrepancy principle. Numerical experiments for the electrical impedance tomography problem illustrate the theoretical results and demonstrate the performance of the method for different batch sizes.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global stability and nonlinear asymptotics for the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the three-dimensional compressible Navier--Stokes--Fourier system with horizontal shear viscosity, a positive coefficient $λ+μ>0$ in the divergence term, and full heat conduction. Horizontal viscosity does not dissipate vertical shear derivatives, while thermal diffusion is coupled to the compressible variables. For small $H^2$ perturbations of a constant equilibrium, we construct global strong solutions. Additional spatial localization yields anisotropic decay through second order, convergence of the full $H^2$ norm, and horizontal Gaussian profiles determined by an effective velocity datum. The third-order behavior contains nonlinear contributions: horizontal viscous heating generates a differentiated Newton potential in temperature, while compressible transport slows the decay of the potential velocity. We prove the corresponding bounds with exponents $17/8$ and $2$; for each exponent, we construct a fixed datum in the corresponding class for which every larger exponent fails. For each fixed initial datum, however, the corresponding time-weighted norms tend to zero as $t\to\infty$. Smallness of the first vertical derivative of the initial velocity in the horizontal mixed norm improves the vertical decay estimates and restores the linear third-order temperature rate. Both the existence and decay results require only $H^2$ Sobolev regularity of the initial data.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Free Boundary Propagation of a Thin-Film Equation with Nonlinear Diffusion: Scale-Consistent Methods for Optimal Results
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the free boundary propagation of a non-linear degenerate parabolic problem with both fourth and second order non-linearities, which may be used to model viscous thin-film flow in the regime of weak slippage with an additional contributions from a singular disjoining pressure brought forth by inter-molecular forces. By carefully treating the individual scaling behaviors of the non-linearities, we obtain asymptotically optimal upper and lower bounds on the rate of forward support propagation. These rates show that the fourth-order operator dominates the propagation rate on short time scales, but the long-term rate of propagation is controlled by the second-order operator. We estimate further the time at which this trade-off in propagation rate occurs. Lastly, we examine sufficient conditions to ensure that the free boundary does not immediately advance in a given direction, leading to a detailed picture of how the competition between the second/fourth-order operators influence the free boundary dynamics of solutions.
