Analysis of PDEs.title: Quadratic Convexity for Closed and Free Boundary High Codimension Mean Curvature Flow
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We introduce quadratic convexity for mean curvature flow in high codimension. It combines quantitative convexity in the mean curvature direction with control of the full second fundamental form. Strict Andrews-Baker quadratic pinching implies quadratic convexity, while the new inequality also admits curvature tensors beyond the critical quadratic ratio.
  For compact connected closed submanifolds of dimension $n\geq5$, we prove preservation of quadratic convexity and convergence in finite time to a round point. For compact connected submanifolds of dimension $n\geq4$ with spherical free boundary, we prove preservation and convergence to a round hemisphere in a uniquely determined $(n+1)$-plane. To our knowledge, this is the first such convergence theorem for spherical free boundary MCF in arbitrary codimension. The closed theorem requires additional quadratic pinching for $5\leq n\leq7$, and the free boundary theorem for $4\leq n\leq7$. For $n\geq8$, the necessary quadratic bound follows from quadratic convexity.
  We also establish preservation of ordinary quadratic pinching $|A|^2\leq c|H|^2$ under spherical free boundary flow for $n\ge2$ and $\frac{9}{8n}\leq c\leq\frac{4}{3n}$, including both endpoints.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Fujita equation with time-integrable forcing: effective mass, mass annihilation and sharp lifespan
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the Cauchy problem $\partial_t u-Δu=|u|^p+ζ(t)w(x)$ in $\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty)$, $p>1$, with sign-changing data and a forcing whose temporal profile $ζ$ is integrable on $(0,\infty)$, the model case being $ζ(t)=t^σe^{-t}$, $σ>-1$. For power-type profiles $ζ(t)=t^σ$ the forcing is known to raise the critical exponent above the Fujita exponent $p_F=1+2/N$ or to destroy global existence. We show that an integrable forcing leaves $p_F$ unchanged and acts only through the effective mass $M_{\rm eff}=\int u_0+(\int_0^\inftyζ)(\int w)$. Our central result is an exact mass-annihilation identity: if $1<p\le p_F$, every global weak solution lies in $L^p(\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty))$ and satisfies $\iint|u|^p=-M_{\rm eff}$. Hence, for $p\le p_F$, no global solution exists when $M_{\rm eff}\ge0$ and the data are nontrivial, and every global mild solution vanishes in $L^1$ as $t\to\infty$; examples show that $M_{\rm eff}<0$ neither excludes nor implies global existence. For $p>p_F$, every solution is dominated by a multiple of the linear forced flow under a single integral condition; this gives small-data global existence without sign restrictions and, if $ζ$ decays mildly, convergence to $m_\infty G_t$ with asymptotic mass $m_\infty=M_{\rm eff}+\iint|u|^p$. We also give a localized necessary condition valid for all $p>1$, showing that large or slowly decaying data blow up regardless of the forcing and that non-integrable forcings shift the threshold, and sharp lifespan estimates for small data with positive effective mass: $T_\varepsilon\simeq\varepsilon^{-2(p-1)/(2-N(p-1))}$ for $p<p_F$ and $\log T_\varepsilon\simeq\varepsilon^{-(p-1)}$ for $p=p_F$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Logarithmically Coupled p-Laplacian Systems: From Discrete Ground States to Rigidity and Critical Continuous Limits
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We introduce a new class of logarithmically coupled p-Laplacian systems on locally finite graphs and on \(\mathbb{R}^N\) for the critical case \(p = N > 4\). The coupling poses two challenges: the energy functional is ill-defined on the natural Sobolev space, and loss of the \(L^\infty\)-embedding prevents standard control of logarithmic terms. To resolve this non-separable logarithmic singularity, we develop an \textbf{exponent calibration technique} that converts logarithmic terms into strictly lower-order power estimates. The technique plays an essential role in two critical steps: the existence proof for the regularised problem and the uniform boundedness of regularised ground states that restores compactness. Thus, we prove solvability of the original ill-posed continuous critical equation. In the discrete setting, we identify five new intrinsic structures, including an exact constrained Hessian factorisation and a scalar rigidity index. We complete a discrete--continuous double loop, providing a unified variational framework for logarithmically coupled systems.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Two-Scale Calculus for Riesz Fractional Gradients: Compactness, Realization, and Periodic Homogenization
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We develop a two-scale calculus for the Riesz fractional gradient $\grads$, $0<s<1$, acting on functions that vanish outside a bounded open set $Ω\subset\R^N$. For bounded families in $H_0^s(Ω)$ we characterize the interior two-scale limits of the fractional gradients and prove, by a Fourier-multiplier estimate, that every limit of this form is generated by such a family; a periodic fractional Helmholtz decomposition identifies the microscopic potentials, and $\eps^s$ is the natural amplitude of the oscillations. For periodic fractional divergence-form equations with bounded measurable, uniformly elliptic, not necessarily symmetric coefficients, we identify the two-scale limit of the fractional gradients and the homogenized problem, whose coefficient is the classical homogenized matrix in $Ω$ and the cell average outside $Ω$, and we construct correctors in $H_0^s(Ω)$ that give strong convergence in $H^s(\R^N)$. The identification extends to parabolic problems with dual-space forcing.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Absence of uniform bounds for the boundary nodal count of Steklov eigenfunctions on Euclidean domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that for any $K,N\in\mathbb N$ there exist smooth bounded domains in $\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq 3$, homeomorphic to a ball, for which the first $N$ positive Steklov eigenvalues are simple and the boundary traces of the corresponding eigenfunctions have at least $K$ nodal domains. This provides a negative answer to the question of whether the number of nodal domains of Dirichlet-to-Neumann eigenfunctions satisfies a Courant-type bound in the Euclidean setting and complements the results of [6].

Analysis of PDEs.title: Rough vector fields with vanishing Lie brackets
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider two vector fields $X, Y \in W^{1,p}_{loc}(\mathbb R^d) \cap \mathbf L^\infty$ with bounded divergence. If $p \geq 2$, this paper shows that $DX \,Y - DY \, X = 0$ almost everywhere if and only if their Regular Lagrangian Flows commute. If instead $1 \leq p < 2$, we present an example of two divergence free locally Sobolev vector fields in $\mathbb R^2$ with vanishing Lie brackets whose flows do not commute. In the regime $2 \leq p < \infty$ this paper also yields a quantitative commutation result not depending on the Lipschitz constant for vector fields with $[X, Y] \neq 0$, which is new even in the smooth setting.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Singular Contour Dynamics and Paradifferential Reduction
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We develop a direct paradifferential approach to nonlinear graph integral operators arising in contour dynamics. The main methodological result is an abstract structure-preserving paralinearization theorem, valid in arbitrary dimension, for a class of homogeneous kernels whose nonlinear dependence on the graph is expressed through normalized finite differences. The theorem covers both critical principal-value kernels and subcritical locally integrable kernels, gives explicit formulas for the principal symbols, and separates the finite-order symbolic contribution generated by the homogeneous singularity from order-zero far-field terms and arbitrarily smoothing remainders. A structural feature of the reduction is the cancellation of the intermediate symbolic order; at the critical endpoint the construction also preserves the exact skew-adjoint structure of the original singular integral.
  As a main application, we consider the three-dimensional two-phase free-boundary Euler equations with constant interfacial background vorticity. We first derive an autonomous contour-dynamics equation in canonical surface variables and then apply the abstract theorem directly to the singular integral operators generated by the Birkhoff--Rott formulation. This yields the complete paradifferential structure of the system without taking the Dirichlet--Neumann reduction as a starting point. After introducing an Alinhac good unknown and diagonalizing the resulting system, we obtain local well-posedness for small Sobolev perturbations in the stable Kelvin--Rayleigh--Taylor regime, uniformly on compact subsets of the stable parameter set.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sharp boundary regularity for planar minimal graphs with analytic Dirichlet data
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We study the boundary behavior of generalized (BV) solutions of the Dirichlet problem for the minimal surface equation over a bounded set \(Ω\). Such a generalized solution is always the graph of a smooth function \(v\) inside \(Ω\), but might carry a vertical part over \(\partialΩ\), which records the gap between the prescribed Dirichlet datum \(g\) and the boundary trace \(h\) attained by \(v\). When \(Ω\) is a bounded real-analytic planar domain and \(g\) is real analytic we prove that \(h\) is Lipschitz, right and left differentiable at every point, of class \(C^1\) on \(\partialΩ\setminusΣ\), and real analytic on \(\{h\neq g\}\setminusΣ\), where \(Σ=\{κ=0\}\) is the zero set of the curvature of \(\partialΩ\). Also, at each point \(p\inΣ\cap\{h\neq g\}\), the two one-sided branches extend real analytically across \(p\).
  The proof recasts the vertical part near a contact point as a scalar obstacle problem with a possibly degenerate right-hand side, whose model case is \(Δv=H\,\id_{\{v>0\}}\) with \(H\ge0\) a polynomial. These results are optimal: for merely smooth data the trace may be discontinuous, while in the real-analytic case there are examples where corners do occur.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Estimates for viscosity solutions of fully nonlinear equations near smooth boundaries
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We reduce the problem of proving decay estimates for viscosity solutions of fully nonlinear PDEs to proving analogous estimates for solutions of one-dimensional ordinary differential inequalities. Our machinery allow the ellipticity to vanish near the boundary and permits general, possibly unbounded, lower-order terms. A key consequence is the derivation of boundary Harnack inequalities for a broad class of fully nonlinear, nonhomogeneous equations near $C^{1,1}$-boundaries.
  In combination with $C^{1,α}$-estimates, we also obtain that quotients of positive vanishing solutions are Hölder continuous near $C^{1,1}$-boundaries.This result applies to a wide family of fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic PDEs; and for $p(x)$-harmonic functions and planar $\infty$-harmonic functions near locally flat boundaries. We end by deriving some Phragmén-Lindelöf-type corollaries in unbounded domains.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Periodic KPP equations in hyperbolic space
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study Fisher-KPP equations in hyperbolic space with reactions periodic in a Busemann coordinate, in the distance from a point, or in the distance from a complete geodesic. For the Busemann and radial reactions, solutions with nonzero compactly supported initial data become uniformly extinct precisely when the principal eigenvalue of the periodic linearisation with the curvature correction is nonpositive. When this eigenvalue is positive, we determine the logarithmic delay of spreading up to a bounded error. For compactly supported data we bound the Busemann superlevel sets between horoballs in fixed transverse windows and between balls in sectors away from the endpoint of the defining ray. For data between a positive multiple of one horoball indicator and the indicator of a containing horoball, the horoball inclusions hold throughout hyperbolic space. For reactions periodic in the distance from a geodesic, extinction is governed by the top of the transverse spectrum. In the hyperbolic plane we construct a smooth periodic reaction for which compactly supported populations die out in the Busemann and radial cases but persist near the geodesic in the geodesic-distance case. For the geodesic-distance reaction in this example, the smallest positive stationary solution tends to zero with distance from the geodesic, and a variational formula gives the spreading speed along it. For every fixed level below the value of this solution on the geodesic, we determine the logarithmic delay up to a bounded error in both directions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Mixed local and nonlocal laplacian without standard critical exponent for Lane-Emden equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we investigate a mixed elliptic equation
  involving both local and nonlocal Laplacian operators,
  with a power-type nonlinearity. Specifically, we consider a
  Lane--Emden type equation of the form
  \[
  -Δu + (-Δ)^s u
  = u^p\quad\text{ in }\R^n,
  \]
  where the operator combines the classical Laplacian and
  the fractional Laplacian, \(s\in(0,1)\). We first observe, by a
  variational argument that works for any finite sum of fractional
  Laplacians of different orders, that positive radial solutions exist
  in the whole range \(\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}<p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}\), while in
  star-shaped bounded domains the threshold for existence is the local
  Sobolev exponent \(\frac{n+2}{n-2}\). Hence, for a sum of two diffusion
  operators without zero-order term, the classical duality between the
  critical exponent in \(\R^n\) and the one in star-shaped domains fails.
  Our main results describe the solutions near both thresholds. For
  \(n\ge6\) (or \(n=5\) and \(s>\frac14\)) and \(p<\frac{n+2}{n-2}\) close to
  \(\frac{n+2}{n-2}\), we construct by a Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction radial
  solutions which concentrate at the origin with the profile of the
  Aubin--Talenti bubble, at the explicit rate
  \(δ_\varepsilon^{2(1-s)}\sim\varepsilon=\frac{n+2}{n-2}-p\) dictated by the
  competition between the two diffusions. Dually, in every dimension \(n\ge3\)
  and for \(p>\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\) close to \(\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\), we construct
  radial solutions which bifurcate from the bubble of \((-Δ)^s\) and vanish
  by spreading out at the rate \(μ_η^{-2(1-s)}\simη=p-\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}\).
  These results show that this mixed Lane--Emden equation does not admit a
  critical exponent in the traditional sense.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Long lived QNM for multiple black holes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We provide a rigorous definition of quasinormal modes (QNM) for the Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetimes with multiple extremal black holes. For certain configurations, the trapped set of the null geodesic flow contains stable (elliptic) orbits. We analyze this phenomenon in the case of two black holes of equal mass and show that it produces QNM converging exponentially fast to the real axis. QNM for black holes have been extensively studied for $\textit{single}$ black holes and this appears to be the first $\textit{mathematical}$ result for the case of multiple black holes.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Fujita exponents on quantum Euclidean spaces
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the well-posedness of a non-linear heat equation with power nonlinearity with positive initial data on quantum Euclidean spaces. We prove a noncommutative analogue of the classical Fujita theorem by identifying the critical exponent separating finite-time blow-up from global existence for small initial data. Moreover, we establish a fundamental inequality in general semifinite von Neumann algebras that is of independent interest and plays a crucial role in the study of global existence and local well-posedness of solutions of nonlinear equations in noncommutative setting.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the self-adjointness of two-dimensional relativistic shell interactions
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We discuss the self-adjointness of the two-dimensional Dirac operator with a transmission condition along a closed Lipschitz curve. The main new ingredients are an explicit use of the Cauchy transform on non-smooth curves and a direct link with the Fredholmness of a singular boundary integral operator. The new self-adjointness condition includes and extends all previous results for this class of problems. The study is particularly precise for the case of curvilinear polygons, as the angles can be taken into account in an explicit way.
