While semigroup regularity and decay estimates are well understood for the no-slip case, such results have been limited to bounded domains in the slip setting. By exploiting the geometric regularity of the sphere, we establish strong $L^q$-regularity, bounded analyticity, and sharp $ L^q-L^r$ estimates for the corresponding fluid-structure operator. These results would provide a foundation for constructing strong $W^{2,1}_q$ solutions and Kato-type solutions to the corresponding nonlinear system.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the two critical exponents for a dispersive equation with weak dissipation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study a nonlinear Cauchy problem written in normal form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_{tt} + A u+ Bu_t =D|u|^α, & t\geq 0, x \in \mathbb{R}^n\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\,u_t(0,x)=u_1(x). \end{cases} \end{equation*} Here~ $Af=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(a(ξ)^2\mathscr{F}f)$, with $a(ξ)$ homogeneous of order $k > 0$ under the assumption that the Hessian matrix of $a(ξ)$ is nonsingular, the operator $Bf=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(b(ξ)\mathscr{F}f)$ represents a weak dissipation, in the sense that $b(ξ) \sim 1$ as $|ξ| \to \infty$ and %, in several models, $D=B$ but we also consider the case $Df=ν\ast (-Δ)^δ(I-Δ)^{-δ}$, with $ν$ a bounded measure and $δ\geq k/2$. We derive $L^p-L^q$ estimates of the linear solution operator to the considered model and we prove the transition from a Fujita-type exponent to a Strauss-type exponent for the global-in-time existence of small data solution for the corresponding nonlinear problems.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: This is the final version of the paper, accepted for publication in Annali dell'Università di Ferrara

Analysis of PDEs.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of a Class of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove local smoothing estimates for a class of Schrödinger operators on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global-in-time maximal regularity for the Dunkl heat equation in BMO
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish global-in-time maximal regularity for the Cauchy problem of the Dunkl heat equation in BMO, without assuming reflection invariance of the external force. For a Hilbert-valued BMO function $F$, we integrate the spatial mean-square oscillation of the Dunkl gradient of its heat extension over all $t>0$ on each fixed Euclidean ball. The supremum of these integrals is comparable to the squared BMO seminorm of $F$. In particular, the upper estimates imply time-weighted energy estimates for the zero-initial-value solution and maximal regularity for nonzero initial values whose weak Dunkl derivatives belong to BMO.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A non-zero gap for the planar Mumford-Shah convex lifting and the nonexistence of crack-tip calibrations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that the convex lifting of the Mumford-Shah functional constructed through the notion of calibration introduced in [2] is not sharp in dimension two. For Dirichlet boundary data prescribed by the crack-tip function, we construct a lifted competitor whose energy is strictly lower than that of the crack-tip subgraph. Since the crack-tip minimizes the original Mumford-Shah functional, this establishes a strict gap between the infima of the original and lifted problems. As a consequence we establish that the crack-tip admits no calibration.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Equi-integrable approximation of Sobolev mappings between manifolds
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We show that limits of sequences of smooth maps between compact Riemannian manifolds with equi-integrable $W^{1, p}$-Sobolev energy can always be strongly approximated by smooth maps, giving a counterpart of Hang's density result in $W^{1, 1}$ for the Sobolev space $W^{1, p}$ with integer $p \ge 2$. Our result extends to higher-order Sobolev spaces and is straightforward in fractional Sobolev spaces. We also provide a proof based on the weak continuity of Jacobians in the cases where the cohomological criterion of Bethuel, Demengel, Colon and Hélein applies.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global-in-time L p -- L q estimates for solutions of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this work, we prove an optimal global-in-time $L^p \to L^q$ estimate for solutions to the Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation with short range potential in dimension three. Our result shows that the decay rate as t $\rightarrow$ +$\infty$ is the same as the heat equation in x-variables and the divergence rate as t $\rightarrow$ 0 + is related to the sub-ellipticity with loss of 1/3 derivatives of the Kramers-Fokker-Planck operator.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Sheetwise stationarity for stationary unions of $C^{1,α}$ graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We prove that stationarity of a finite union of $C^{1,α}$ graphs implies stationarity of each individual graph, in arbitrary dimension and codimension. The proof closely follows the approach of Minter and Stanbury \cite{MinterStanbury}, who also raised this question in their Remark~1.6. As in their paper, we give a proof that uses the planar frequency results of Krummel, Minter and Wickramasekera \cite{KMW26} (but avoids the centre manifold construction of that paper). We also rely on the Schauder estimates for $Q$-valued functions established in \cite{Luc26}.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Refined Strichartz Estimates for sub-Laplacians in Heisenberg and $H$-type groups
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the sub-Riemannian Schrödinger equation on $H$-type Carnot groups using Fourier restriction techniques. In particular, we extend the previously known Strichartz estimates previously obtained for the Heisenberg group also to non radial initial data. The same arguments permits to obtain refined Strichartz estimates for the wave equation on $H$-type groups. Our proof is based on estimates for the spectral projectors for sub-Laplacians and reinterprets Strichartz estimates as Fourier restriction theorems for nilpotent groups in the context of trace-class operator valued measures.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Perturbation Algorithm and Iterative Realization of a Four-Layer Semi-Discrete Scheme for an Evolutionary Problem with a Variable Operator
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In a Hilbert space, we consider the Cauchy problem for an evolutionary equation with the operator $A+B(t)$, where $A$ is a self-adjoint positive definite operator and $B(t)$ is a bounded operator depending on time. By means of the perturbation algorithm, the purely implicit four-layer semi-discrete scheme of the third order of approximation (the three-step backward differentiation formula) is reduced to three two-layer schemes, whose solutions are used to construct an approximate solution of the original problem. In each two-layer scheme, the term containing $B(t)$ is moved to the right-hand side, and the resulting equation is solved by an iterative method, so that only the time-independent operator $I+τA$ has to be inverted; the convergence of the iterations at the rate of a geometric progression with a ratio of order $τ$ is proved. A priori estimates for the two-layer and four-layer schemes are obtained by means of a discrete analogue of Gronwall's lemma. An estimate of order $τ^3$ for the error of the approximate solution is proved under an assumption on the difference quotients of the computed grid functions on the first layers. The results are illustrated by numerical experiments.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 17 pages in total, including the cover page; 3 figures and 4 tables

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large time decay of the fluid-structure semigroup subject to the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Consider the motion of a rigid body moving into a viscous incompressible fluid that fills the whole space in 3D. The fluid motion obeys the Navier-Stokes system, while the motion of the body is governed by the Newton law. Both motions are affected by each other at the fluid-solid interface through the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition, which is known as a substitution for the no-slip one to resolve the no-collision paradox. We adopt a monolithic approach and carry out the spectral analysis to deduce the large time behavior of the fluid-structure semigroup, where the shape of the body is allowed to be arbitrary. What is remarkable is that the decay structure is somewhat different under the full slip condition when the body is axially symmetric. If, in particular, the body is a ball, we then apply the linear theory developed above to the nonlinear initial value problem to show the stability of the rest state. It is, furthermore, asymptotically stable except for the full slip case.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(Ω) \le \frac{π^{s-\frac{1}{2}}Γ\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)Γ\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partialΩ)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $Γ$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The first version of this article was submitted to arXiv on July 21, 2026, and then it was on hold by arXiv till September 17, 2026. During the period when it was on hold, on August 13 we submitted a revised version to arXiv by adding an acknowledgement to AI

Analysis of PDEs.title: A variational theory for von Kármán vortex streets
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct von Kármán vortex streets as global kinetic energy maximizers for the 2D Euler flow in an infinite periodic channel: our variational framework imposes no a prior symmetry, support constraints, or sign conditions on the admissible class. More specifically, under $O(\varepsilon^{-2})$ constraint of the absolute vorticity maximum with other natural constraints, we show that the maximizers are traveling pairs of simply connected vortex patches of support radius $O(\varepsilon)$, converging to the von Kármán point-vortex configuration satisfying glide reflection symmetry as $\varepsilon \to 0$. We prove nonlinear stability of the von Kármán streets under a bound on the vertical support, using a compactness result valid for more general assumptions. Furthermore, we construct slightly tilted asymmetric von Kármán vortex streets as energy maximizers under a tilted moment constraint.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Critical nonlocal GJMS operator on odd dimensional spheres and mean field equation
Analysis of PDEs.summary: For a smooth axially symmetric function on $\mathbb{S}^n$ with $n\geq 1$, in odd dimensions we prove a neat formula for the critical nonlocal GJMS operator $P_n$ similar to the one in even dimensions. With this formula, we give a simple proof of the Liouville theorem by Gui-Hu-Xie (J. Funct. Anal. 2022): Every smooth axially symmetric solution to $$\frac{1}{n+1} P_n u = (n-1)!(e^{nu}-1) \quad \mathrm{on} \quad \mathbb{S}^n,n\geq 2$$ is identically zero, without using any delicate property of Gegenbauer polynomials.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A family of homogeneous convex non-scattering domains with analytic non-circular boundaries
Analysis of PDEs.summary: A homogeneous planar non-scattering domain is a bounded medium with a constant material coefficient that produces no scattered field for some nonzero entire solution of the Helmholtz equation at a particular wave number. It is known that the boundary of such a domain must be real analytic at all points where the incident field does not vanish. Previously, disks were the only known examples. We construct a family of homogeneous strictly convex non-scattering domains that are neither disks nor ellipses. The family bifurcates from a particular non-scattering disk, with the boundary, wave number, and constant coefficient varying along the branch. The construction uses a conformal change of variables and analytic bifurcation theory applied to the resulting nonlinear problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A note on a nonlocal antisymmetric barrier
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this note, we present a barrier function for an equation involving the fractional Laplacian in the antisymmetric setting, providing an explicit inequality in the full positivity set of the function. This leads to an improvement of the quantitative maximum principle given in [DPTV26], where the bound was obtained in a strict subset of its positivity set and required additional assumptions on lower order coefficients.
  As a consequence of this, we give an optimal lower bound on the growth of antisymmetric solutions from the symmetry hyperplane.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A One-Sided Liouville Theorem and a Critical Sparse-Support Inverse Theorem for Discrete Harmonic Functions
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We answer the one-sided Liouville question of Buhovsky, Logunov, Malinnikova, and Sodin (Duke Math. J. 171 (2022), Remark 1.4). There is an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that a real harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is constant if it is nonnegative on at least a $1-\varepsilon$ proportion of every sufficiently large centered square. More generally, for every nonconstant real harmonic function and every $a\le b$, the sets $\{u<a\}$ and $\{u>b\}$ each occupy a fixed positive proportion of the same arbitrarily large centered squares.
  Turning from sign conditions to sparse supports, we prove in three dimensions a local inverse theorem at the critical quadratic support scale. Write $Q_R=[-R,R]^3\cap\mathbb{Z}^3$. If a complex-valued function is harmonic in $Q_{30R}$ and has at most $AR^2$ nonzero values there, its support in $Q_R$ lies in at most $K_A$ characteristic planes $x_i\pm x_j=c$. The minimum number $m_3(N)$ of nonzero values in $Q_N$ among whole-lattice harmonic functions nonzero at the origin satisfies $m_3(N)=(1+o(1))(2N+1)^2$. More generally, if a fixed nonzero harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ has $O(N^2)$ nonzero values in $Q_N$ along a sequence $N\to\infty$, then its support has a unique irredundant cover by finitely many characteristic planes. If there are $k$ such planes, the support count in $Q_N$ is $k(2N+1)^2+O_u(N)$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Determination of the unbounded potential of the Robin Laplacian from fixed-time boundary measurements of time-fractional diffusion-wave equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the time-fractional diffusion-wave equation $\partial_t^ρu - Δu + q u = 0$ in a bounded domain $Ω\subset \RR^n$, $n \geq 3$, where $\partial_t^ρ$ is the Caputo derivative of arbitrary order $ρ\in (0,2)$. This framework covers in a unified way the sub-diffusive case $ρ\in (0,1)$, the classical heat equation $ρ= 1$, and the super-diffusive case $ρ\in (1,2)$. The real-valued potential $q$ is only assumed to lie in $L^{n/2}(Ω)$, and the equation is endowed with zero initial conditions and a non-homogeneous Robin boundary condition, whose coefficient is allowed to be unbounded as well. The boundary excitations are supported in an arbitrary open subset $Γ_0$ of the boundary, and the trace of the solution is measured, at one fixed time, on another open subset $Γ_1$. We prove that the corresponding Robin-to-Dirichlet map uniquely determines the boundary spectral data of the underlying Robin Laplacian on $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$, provided that $Γ_0$ and $Γ_1$ overlap. When $Γ_0 \cup Γ_1$ is the whole boundary, we deduce that $q$ is uniquely determined by this map in every dimension $n \geq 3$, the critical case $q \in L^{3/2}(Ω)$ in dimension three being included. The proof combines analytic continuation in the time variable, the Laplace transform and an identification of the poles and residues of meromorphic functions. The potential is then recovered from the boundary spectral data through an elliptic Robin-to-Dirichlet map, an integral identity, and complex geometric optics solutions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Shrinking Limit for the Stationary Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation on Cross-Shaped Infinite Domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the stationary nonlinear Schrödinger equation on a planar, cross-shaped infinite domain and in the shrinking limit. For any fixed thickness, we establish the existence of solutions through a variational approach. To overcome the loss of compactness inherent to the unbounded geometry and bypass the regularity obstructions caused by the re-entrant corners, we constrain the minimization problem to a cone of symmetric and monotonic functions. We then establish the resolvent-preservation property, ensuring the constrained minimizers are stationary solutions. As the transverse width vanishes, we establish a transverse collapse phenomenon, that is, the two-dimensional solutions flatten across the central junction and become purely one-dimensional along the infinite branches. In this way, we prove that cross solutions converge strongly to a stationary solution on the limiting graph in a suitable sense. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this dimensional reduction recovers both vertex continuity and the Kirchhoff conditions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: An inverse problem for semilinear elliptic equations with generalized Kerr-type nonlinearities
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the inverse problem of reconstructing the convex hull of unknown inclusions in semilinear elliptic equations with nonanalytic nonlinearities, by extending Ikehata's enclosure method to accommodate such nonlinear effects. To overcome the lack of the higher-order differentiability required for the Taylor-based construction, we construct an approximate solution based on the linearized equation through a first-iteration approximation. Under suitable structural conditions on the nonlinearity, we establish a reconstruction result for the convex hull of the inclusion. The method applies to a broad class of generalized Kerr-type nonlinearities that need not be analytic, without requiring an explicit formula for the nonlinear term. We also address the numerical challenges arising from the exponential decay of the CGO test data and show how they limit the accuracy of an implementation in double-precision arithmetic.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The abstract has been updated, a numerical simulation has been added, and a MATLAB implementation is available in our GitHub repository. The revised manuscript is now 25 pages long

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global renormalized finite-energy weak solutions to the three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system on tori for $γ>4/3$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Building on the foundational theory of finite-energy weak solutions initiated by P.-L. Lions and further developed by E. Feireisl and collaborators, we establish the global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, with constant viscosity coefficients and pressure law \(P(ρ)=ρ^γ\), for every \(γ>4/3\) and arbitrary finite-energy initial data. This extends the classical three-dimensional Lions--Feireisl existence theory beyond the threshold \(γ>3/2\), and in particular, covers the important case $ γ=7/5 $ for air (cf. \cite{Anderson}). Compared to the classical theory, we develop a novel approach to establish the improved pressure-integrability estimate compatible with the viscous and inertial terms, via constructing a periodic test field through barycentric optimal transport. This improved pressure-integrability estimate, combined with an effective viscous flux identity and an entropy comparison, provides the compactness needed to identify the nonlinear limits and recover the energy inequality.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Entropic metastability for drifted reflected Brownian motion: quasi-stationary distributions, regularity, and the exit position distribution
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Motivated by entropic metastability and the narrow escape problem, we investigate quasi-stationary distributions for reflected, drifted elliptic diffusions under mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions on a bounded domain. We address two problems, which are solved completely independently of each other. First, using purely probabilistic tools, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a quasi-stationary distribution under minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients (the case of an unbounded domain is also analyzed). Second, using spectral theory and the theory of strongly continuous semigroups on L p spaces, we study the analytical properties of the quasistationary distribution. We relate it to the principal eigenfunction of the adjoint of the associated (non-symmetric) infinitesimal generator with mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions, and we establish its regularity up to the interface between the two boundary parts. We also fully characterize the law of the exit point when the process is initially distributed according to its quasistationary distribution. In particular, we work on domains in which the absorbing (Dirichlet) and reflecting (Neumann) parts of the boundary meet tangentially, without forming any non-trivial angle, a configuration that raises genuine regularity difficulties for the solutions of the associated mixed boundary value problem.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Asymptotic behavior of solutions to the one-dimensional $p$-system with time-dependent non-smooth damping
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper is concerned with the asymptotic behavior of solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional $p$-system with time-dependent damping. When the damping coefficient $b(t)$ behaves like $(1+t)^{-λ}$ with $0\leλ<1$, the solutions are expected to converge to a diffusion wave. For $b(t)=(1+t)^{-λ}$, previous studies have established convergence to a diffusion wave together with convergence rates using the energy method, provided that the initial perturbation and the wave strength are sufficiently small. In this paper, we introduce two auxiliary functions and reformulate our problem into two perturbation problems adapted to the structure of the system. This enables us to prove a result analogous to those obtained in previous studies, without assuming the differentiability of $b(t)$. The auxiliary functions are given by the differential equations $1+g'(t)=b(t)g(t)$ and $1-h'(t)=b(t)h(t)$, respectively. Our result shows that it suffices to assume $b\in C([0,\infty))$, $b(t)\asymp(1+t)^{-λ}$, and $|g'(t)|\lesssim(1+t)^{-(1-λ)}$ to obtain convergence to a diffusion wave.

Analysis of PDEs.title: The compressible-incompressible CAO problem introduced by Lions, Temam and Wang
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the (CAO) system of Lions-Temam-Wang, describing a compressible atmosphere coupled to an incompressible ocean through a fully nonlinear boundary condition representing wind stress at the interface. In their foundational work, the system is reformulated in pressure coordinates under the assumption that the pressure is constant at the interface, leading to a purely incompressible system. In this article, we prove for the first time the strong well-posedness of the coupled compressible-incompressible system both locally and globally for small initial data.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: Accepted. To appear in Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées

Analysis of PDEs.title: Low regularity potentials in heterogeneous Cahn--Hilliard functionals
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this paper, we study the prototypical model of liquid-liquid phase separation, the Cahn-Hilliard functional, in a highly irregular setting. Specifically, we analyze potentials with low regularity vanishing on space-dependent wells. Under remarkably weak hypotheses, we establish a robust compactness result. Strengthening the regularity of the wells and of the growth of the potential close to the wells only slightly, we completely characterize the asymptotic behavior of the associated family of functionals through a $Γ$-convergence analysis. As a notable technical result, we prove the existence of geodesics for a degenerate metric and establish a uniform bound on their Euclidean length.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global-in-Time Nonrelativistic Limit and KAM Tori for the Complex Klein-Gordon Equation on the Circle
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper establishes a global-in-time nonrelativistic limit for families of small-amplitude quasi-periodic solutions of the cubic complex Klein-Gordon equation on the circle. Firstly, we construct by a KAM block scheme, small-amplitude two-frequency invariant tori and show that their linear stability depends on whether the two excited Fourier indices coincide or are distinct: coincident indices yield linearly stable tori, whereas distinct indices yield partially hyperbolic tori. Moreover, controlling the dependence of the KAM scheme on the speed of light, we construct quasi-periodic solutions whose frequencies, after a gauge transformation, coincide exactly with those of quasi-periodic solutions of the limiting coupled NLS system, obtaining an approximation uniform for all times in the nonrelativistic regime. By this result, we further show that there exists a positive-measure set of frequencies such that, for each frequency, we can fix a quasi-periodic solution of the coupled NLS system and a suitable subsequence of Klein-Gordon solutions converging globally in time to the fixed NLS solution.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Global well-posedness for the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system
Analysis of PDEs.summary: This paper establishes the global well-posedness and nonlinear stability of the 2D full compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic system $\mathbb T^2$, for smooth initial data close to the equilibrium with constant density and temperature, zero velocity and background magnetic field $\mathbf e_2=(0,1)$. Neither the density nor the magnetic field is damped or diffused in this system. Here, we impose no Diophantine condition on the background magnetic field, no symmetry on the data and no special geometry on the domain. Our proof rests on two intrinsic stabilizing mechanisms hidden in the structure of the system. First, the background magnetic field generates damped wave structures which provide dissipation for the $x_2$-derivatives of the density and of the magnetic field. Second, we introduce a new good unknown $Φ$, an effective total pressure gradient that combines the density, the temperature with the magnetic pressure. Although none of its constituents is dissipative by itself, we show that the coupling of $Φ$ with the divergence of the velocity and with the temperature produces dissipation for $Φ$ in all directions, together with an extra regularization of the divergence of the velocity. Combining these two mechanisms with new anisotropic commutator estimates and a hierarchy of time-weighted energy estimates, we prove that the system admits a unique global solution in $H^N(\mathbb T^2)$ for every $N\geq5$, and obtain a uniform-in-time bound on the highest-order energy as well as explicit algebraic decay rates. Even in comparison with the known result for the simpler isentropic counterpart, where the highest-order energy was only shown to grow at most algebraically in time for data in $H^{N}$ with $N\geq10$, our result removes the possible growth and lowers the regularity requirement to $N\geq5$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Sharp Nodal Measure Bound for the Mixed Clamped--Navier Biharmonic Eigenvalue Problem in Dimensions $n\ge 2$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We estimate the interior nodal set of real eigenfunctions of $Δ^2u=λu$ on a bounded connected Euclidean domain. Each boundary component is either of class $C^\infty$ with clamped conditions or of class $C^{2,α}$ and subject to Navier conditions. We obtain $\mathcal H^{n-1}(\{u=0\}\capΩ)\le C_Ωλ^{1/4}$ for $n\ge2$. A spectral inequality on auxiliary clamped collars supplies fixed-scale interior mass. On clamped patches we localize the Carleman estimates of Liu, Tian and Yang. On Navier patches a single harmonic function with trace $u$ controls the two boundary data required for subdivision at every spatial scale. Summing an index linear in local doubling and frequency gives the stated bound. An annulus with one component of each type realizes its order of growth.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Higher-order estimates for $p$-harmonic functions in the plane
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Closing a longstanding gap in the theory, we establish uniform interior $C^{k,β}$ estimates for planar $p$-harmonic functions with $1<p<2$. These estimates hold for every integer $k\ge2$ and every $0<β<1$ such that $k+β<s(p)$, where $s(p)$ is the optimal regularity order identified by Iwaniec and Manfredi. As consequences, we obtain decay estimates at critical points, a Liouville theorem with optimal growth exponent, and uniform higher-order estimates for the flux of planar $q$-harmonic functions with $q>2$.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: The Lean code and a description of the formalization process are available at https://github.com/na0b/phigherorder-lean

Analysis of PDEs.title: Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequalities on the lattice graph \(\mathbb Z^N\)
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we study the following Hardy--Sobolev--Maz'ya inequality on the lattice graph \(\mathbb Z^N\): \[
  \sum_{j=1}^N\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^N}|u(z)-u(z-e_j)|^2
  -C_H(n,m)\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ}
  \frac{|u(z)|^2}{d_Σ(z)^2}
  \geq\overlineκ_{m,n}\|u\|_{\ell^{2^*}(\mathbb Z^N)}^2,
  \quad u\in C_c(\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ), \] where \(n,m\geq1\), \(N=n+m\geq3\), \(Σ=\mathbb Z^n\times\{0\}\), \(2^*=2N/(N-2)\), \(e_j\) is the \(j\)-th coordinate vector, \(d_Σ(z):=\inf_{ζ\inΣ}|z-ζ|\), and \(C_H(n,m)\) is the best constant for the Hardy inequality on \(\mathbb Z^N\setminusΣ\).
  Using the supersolution method and multilinear interpolation, we first prove that the best constant \(\overlineκ_{m,n}\) is positive if and only if either \(1\leq m\leq8\) and \(n\geq1\), or \(m=9\) and \(n\geq14\). Then, we show that \[
  \overlineκ_{m,n}=\overline S_N
  \quad\text{if }m=2\text{ or }(m,n)=(1,2), \] where \(\overline S_N\) is the best constant in the critical Sobolev inequality on \(D^{1,2}(\mathbb Z^N)\). Moreover, for \(m\neq2\) and \(N\geq4\), we prove \(0\leq\overlineκ_{m,n}<\overline S_N\). Finally, using the equality \(\overlineκ_{2,n}=\overline S_{n+2}\), we prove that \(\overlineκ_{2,n}\) is not attained, while for \((m,n)=(1,2)\), we establish nonattainment of \(\overlineκ_{1,2}\) by developing a duality argument based on a comparison of Green functions.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 65 pages. Comments and suggestions are most welcome

Analysis of PDEs.title: Propagation of chaos with singular potentials: A weighted duality approach
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We establish the propagation of chaos and derive the Vlasov equation from a many-body $N$-particle system in the mean-field regime with singular interaction forces bounded by $|x|^{-α-1}$ for $0\le α<(d-1)/2$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which in particular include the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in three dimensions as well as the Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. Our proof is based on an energy-based framework for deriving weighted uniform bounds on cumulants that builds upon the recent duality method developed by Bresch--Duerinckx--Jabin in combination with a new Morawetz-type estimate, allowing us to remove the restriction to locally square-integrable interaction force kernels and handle more singular regimes.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. This is a higher integrability, or Calderón--Zygmund type, estimate for optimal transport, and it settles, on the torus and up to logarithmic factors, a recent conjecture of D'Achille, Mattesini and the third author. As a consequence, we obtain concentration of the matching cost around its mean for every $p\ge2$. The proof combines a deterministic large-scale regularity theory for optimal transport with $p$-costs, based on a harmonic approximation by a non-linear elliptic equation of $p$-Laplacian type, with tail bounds on local matching costs.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional Navier--Stokes equations with singular viscosity
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional isentropic Navier--Stokes system with fast diffusion and singular viscosity. The waves connect a positive left state to zero specific volume at the right far field, where the density becomes unbounded and the viscous coefficient is singular. Under a vanishing--stress condition, we first establish the existence and uniqueness, up to a shift, of a monotone profile with an algebraic right tail. We then prove global existence and convergence to the profile for sufficiently small perturbations in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main difficulties stem from the singular nonlinear viscous term. We note that the existing approach for treating scalar conservation law with singular viscosity can not be applied to Navier--Stokes equations. We propose some new technique: after introducing an effective velocity and using an anti--derivative method, we establish unusual interactive--energy--estimates and thereby the expected energy estimates for velocity by coupling the two perturbation equations; furthermore, we introduce an auxiliary functional to eliminate uncontrollable terms. The artful weighted--energy estimates play a crucial role for treating singularity.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Uniqueness and non-uniqueness of smooth solutions to the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in critical Besov spaces $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}$
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We study the incompressible Navier--Stokes equations on $\mathbb T^d$ with $d\ge2$. For every $2<q\le\infty$ and every smooth mean-zero background solution $U$, we construct two distinct mild solutions with the same initial datum arbitrarily close to $U(0)$ in $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$, both belonging to $C([0,T];\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)) \cap C^\infty((0,T]\times\mathbb T^d)$. The time $T>0$ depends on the background solution but is independent of the prescribed tolerance for the initial data. This gives non-uniqueness for arbitrarily small initial data and density of non-unique initial data in the mean-zero divergence-free subspace of $\dot B^{-1}_{\infty,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $2<q<\infty$. We also prove uniqueness in the same solution class for $1\le q\le2$, establishing the sharp threshold $q=2$ in this Besov scale. The uniqueness result extends to $\dot B^{-1+d/p}_{p,q}(\mathbb T^d)$ for $1\le p<\infty$ and $1\le q\le\infty$, under the same continuity and smoothness assumptions.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Infinitely Many Plasma Echo Cascades and Sobolev Norm Divergence at the Gevrey-3 Threshold
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We construct a global solution to the confined Vlasov--Poisson system near a fixed homogeneous Penrose-stable equilibrium that exhibits infinite-time growth driven by nonlinear plasma echoes. For every sufficiently small \(ε>0\), the initial perturbation has size \(O(ε)\) in a Gevrey-3 norm with radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\). The corresponding solution is real and neutral, and the full distribution remains nonnegative. Its kinetic profile scatters in a lower Sobolev topology, while the spatial density and electric field decay. Nevertheless, the kinetic profile satisfies
  \[ \lim_{t\to\infty}\|f(t)\|_{H^{1000}_{z,v}}=\infty. \]
  The construction combines infinitely many well-separated echo cascades within a single global nonlinear solution. Each cascade generates a high-frequency output that persists under the subsequent evolution, and the accumulated outputs produce divergence in a fixed Sobolev norm. Thus, unlike finite-time echo amplification, the instability persists to arbitrarily large times despite scattering and macroscopic Landau damping. The construction identifies an instability mechanism at the critical amplitude-dependent Gevrey-3 radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\), where cumulative echo amplification balances the initial Fourier decay.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Abstract Formulation of Mean-Field Models and Propagation of Chaos
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We formulate a unified abstract framework for mean-field particle systems and their macroscopic limits from the perspective of differential equations and functional analysis. Combining semigroup theory with optimal transport, we study measure-valued evolutions directly through their generators, allowing different classes of mean-field models to be treated within a common structure. Specifically, the framework involves (1) formulating mean-field models abstractly using semigroups and generators; (2) establishing well-posedness of the corresponding nonlinear mean-field evolution equations in a class of solutions stable under approximation; and (3) proving quantitative propagation of chaos for the associated $N$-particle systems. The central tool is the transport derivative, which measures the infinitesimal variation of transport costs between Markov evolutions. We establish transport-stability criteria expressed through local generator inequalities and show how these criteria underpin both nonlinear well-posedness and particle approximation. When the generator's dependence on the law is controlled by averaged Hilbert-valued features, we obtain an $O(N^{-1})$ sampling contribution to the quadratic Wasserstein estimate through a variance argument. As an application, we obtain quantitative propagation of chaos for Lévy-type mean-field systems with state- and law-dependent drift, diffusion, and jump kernels under intrinsic transport conditions. The admissible jump kernels extend beyond those generated by multiplicative Lévy noise, demonstrating the scope of the abstract framework.

Analysis of PDEs.title: When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Adding constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the loss has been reported to improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in several applications, but mathematical understanding of these benefits remains limited. For several partial differential equations (PDEs), we derive stability estimates for losses with and without integral constraints. The comparison reveals that in certain parameter regimes, the standard loss has very weak control over specific error components, and that the integral constraints restore uniform control of these components. This explains when and why the constraints improve accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments support this interpretation. In parameter regimes where the standard loss is predicted to have weak control over those components, the two losses indeed show clear differences in accuracy. Conversely, in regimes where the standard loss retains sufficient control, both losses yield similar accuracy.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Separated solutions for a critical competitive system with sublinear coupling in domains with shrinking holes
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We construct nonnegative, fully nontrivial separated solutions for the critical competitive system of two coupled elliptic equations with a sublinear competitive coupling, in a bounded domain with two shrinking holes, for $N\ge5$ and every fixed $β<0$; each component concentrates at one of the holes and vanishes near the other. The coupling is not $C^1$ at the origin, so a direct Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction is unavailable, and the reduction has to be closed in a Lebesgue space although the matching requires $L^\infty$ control. We therefore solve a nonlinear outer problem by minimization, derive the dead-core property, solve the two scalar inner problems by a nonlinear contraction, match the inner and outer solutions, and close the scale and position equations by a Brouwer degree argument. This gives a Coron-type construction in the high-dimensional sublinear-coupling regime.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A new approach to interior estimates for fully nonlinear elliptic equations
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We give new proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the quadratic Hessian and Monge-Ampère equations with Dini continuous right-hand sides. Our approach uses a three-point maximum principle and requires no differentiation of the equations. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$. For the Monge-Ampère equation, the proof is localised on sublevel sets of a strictly convex solution.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Complete Classification of the One-Dimensional Nonlocal Eigenvalue Problem
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We give a complete classification of the spectral stability of the following one-dimensional nonlocal eigenvalue problem (NLEP) $$ \partial_x^2φ-φ+pw^{p-1}φ-γ(p-1)\frac{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^{r-1}φdx}{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^r dx}w^p=λφ, $$ where $w$ is the unique positive even solution of $w''-w+w^p=0$ decaying at infinity, $p,r>1$, and $γ\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\Reγ\ge0$. This type of NLEP appears frequently in pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems. We show that on the even subspace, strict spectral stability holds exactly for $\Reγ>1$ when $r=(p+3)/2$. In the $γ$-plane, when $r>(p+3)/2$, two conjugate boundary arcs open to the left from $γ=1$, and the strictly stable region lies to their right. When $r<(p+3)/2$, the arcs open to the right, and the strictly stable region lies between them. Their common endpoint is $γ=1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ=γ_H>1$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$. In each case, the two arcs approach a common vertical asymptote. As an application, for real $γ\ge0$, the condition for strict spectral stability is $γ>1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ>γ_H$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$, where $γ_H>1$ is the value at which a conjugate pair of eigenvalues crosses the imaginary axis. The key ingredient in determining how the number of eigenvalues in the open right half-plane changes at imaginary-axis crossings is a cumulative estimate for the mixed-sign spectral weights that arise for certain $p$ and $r$ with $1<p<3$ and $1<r<2$.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Geometric bounds for Steklov and weighted Neumann eigenvalues on Euclidean domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
We obtain sharp upper bounds for the first two nonzero Steklov eigenvalues among bounded domains in Euclidean spaces of dimension $d \geq 7$ under a natural normalization involving volume and boundary measure. These bounds are derived from a characterization of optimal domains and weights for the first two nonzero weighted Neumann eigenvalues. In dimensions $3 \leq d \leq 6$, we obtain upper bounds that are not sharp.
  We further establish strict upper bounds with sharp constants for all higher Steklov eigenvalues on simply connected planar domains with continuous boundary and finite boundary length. Beyond the second nonzero eigenvalue, these bounds were previously known only for smooth planar domains.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 16 pages; minor typo corrections; to appear in Int. Math. Res. Not

Analysis of PDEs.title: Blow-up suppression for the Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system by Taylor--Couette flow outside a disk
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Taylor--Couette devices have been investigated for enzymatic reactions and cell culture, where cylinder rotation provides a means of controlling mixing and mass transfer (Schrimpf et al., AIChE J., 2021). Motivated by these applications, this paper studies blow-up suppression in the two-dimensional Patlak--Keller--Segel--Navier--Stokes system outside the unit disk. We prove that sufficiently strong Taylor--Couette flow yields a unique global strong solution whose density and concentration are uniformly bounded in time, without smallness assumptions on the initial cell mass or the fixed initial velocity perturbation. The main difficulty is that the angular shear tends to zero at infinity, so decay estimates on bounded regions do not directly control the full solution. To overcome this difficulty, radially weighted energy estimates exploit the radial velocity to control the density and vorticity at large radii. Combining these bounds with linear decay estimates and an energy comparison with the radial chemotaxis solution yields convergence of the density in $L^2$ to the radial solution with angularly averaged initial density, uniformly on fixed finite time intervals away from $t=0$ as the rotation amplitude tends to infinity. The decay of the radial solution then makes the full density small in $L^2$ at a finite time. An energy estimate preserves this smallness and gives global continuation.

Analysis of PDEs.title: A Uniform Positive Lower Bound for the Analyticity Radius of KdV on the Real Line
Analysis of PDEs.summary: We show that, for the Korteweg--de Vries equation on the real line with real-valued initial data in an $L^2$-based analytic class, the radius of spatial analyticity of the solution has a fixed positive lower bound for all time. This improves the previous quantitative lower bounds, which tend to zero as $|t|\to\infty$. The proof uses a positive measure representation of the Hamiltonian multipliers to sum the KdV Hamiltonians into an exactly conserved energy that controls the analytic norm.

Analysis of PDEs.title: Stability analysis and critical thresholds in a nonlocal advection diffusion model of wound healing on bounded domains
Analysis of PDEs.summary: Nonlocal advection diffusion models describe how wound healing depends on the strength of cell-cell adhesion and the cell sensing radius. Depending on these parameters, the wound may close completely or remain in a persistent state with a spatially nonuniform cell density. The model combines random cell movement, cell proliferation, and cell-cell adhesion within a finite sensing radius. We first derive the dispersion relation on the whole line and use it to compute the critical sensing radius and the corresponding wavelength. This relation shows that diffusion and cell proliferation stabilize the healed state, while cell-cell adhesion can make it unstable. On a bounded interval, the cell density is fixed at the healthy value on an exterior collar. In this setting, we establish conditions that keep the cell density within a positive bounded range, derive a sufficient condition for nonlinear exponential stability that depends on domain size, and formulate and numerically solve the associated linear spectral problem. The analysis shows how reducing the domain size can stabilize the healed state at parameter values for which the whole line model is linearly unstable. Finally, we compute critical sensing radii and domain sizes numerically and compare the sufficient stability bounds with the transitions observed in wound simulations involving perturbations of finite amplitude.

Analysis of PDEs.title: On the regularity of stationary solutions to free boundary problems
Analysis of PDEs.summary: In this note, we improve the regularity of Hölder continuous stationary solutions with respect to inner variations which are harmonic outside their zero set. We obtain a $\sqrt{\log}$-Lipschitz estimate for a class of solutions allowing a generalized phase variable and including the two-phase problem. In the case of the one-phase problem, we can improve to Lipschitz regularity. In particular, we show that the initial Lipschitz assumption in the class of variational solutions considered by Kriventsov and Weiss can be replaced by any positive Hölder exponent

Analysis of PDEs.title: Infinitely many positive normalized solutions for Schrödinger equations with nonlinear point defects on noncompact metric graphs
Analysis of PDEs.summary:
In this paper, we study the multiplicity of positive normalized solutions for the following Schrödinger equation with nonlinear point defects on a general metric graph $\G=(\V,\E)$, possibly with infinitely many edges \begin{equation*}
  \begin{cases} u'' = λu & \text{on every } \e \in \E, \\ \int_\G \abs{u}^2\, dx = μ& \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = -\abs{u(\vv)}^{p-2}u(\vv) & \text{at every } \vv \in \V_0, \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = 0 & \text{at every } \vv \in \V \setminus \V_0, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p>2$, $\G$ is connected, $\V_0 \subset \V$ is nonempty, $μ>0$ is a given constant, $λ$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplie. For $p\neq4$, every fixed nonempty finite set $W\subset\V_0$ gives at least $2^{\#W}-1$ distinct positive normalized solutions, for every sufficiently small mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$ and for every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $2<p<4$. When $\V_0$ is finite and $\G$ is noncompact with the bottom of the Kirchhoff Laplacian spectrum equal to zero, we prove that there are exactly $2^{\#\V_0}-1$ positive solutions at every sufficiently small mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$, and at every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $2<p<4$ and $|\overline B_r(o)|=O(r^{4/p})$ as $r\to+\infty$ for a fixed $o\in\G$. If infinitely many defect vertices $\vv \in \V_0$ have uniformly bounded degree, we also obtain infinitely many positive solutions that are pairwise inequivalent under the automorphisms of $\G$ preserving $\V_0$, for every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $2<p<4$ and for every prescribed mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$. In the $L^2$-critical ($p=4$) case, under local conditions near the selected defect vertices, analogous results hold for masses slightly below $kq^2/2$, where $k$ is the number of these vertices and $q$ is their common degree.
Analysis of PDEs.comment: 82 pages. Comments and suggestions are most welcome

Functional Analysis.title: Conditionally Euclidean distance matrices
Functional Analysis.summary: We introduce a new class of matrices called conditional Euclidean distance matrices in this paper. These matrices are a generalisation of Euclidean distance matrices. We develop the theory of conditional Euclidean distance matrices and show that these matrices represent the squared Lorentzian distance between points of a Minkowski space. We also highlight the connection of conditional Euclidean distance matrices with the representation of hierarchical data in machine learning and the theory of general relativity in physics.

Functional Analysis.title: A constructive inverse for the Jordan-von Neuman operator on abelian groups
Functional Analysis.summary: For an abelian group $G$ and a real Banach space $X$, we study the inhomogeneous Jordan--von Neumann equation $\mathsf{Q}[f] = g$, where $\mathsf{Q}$ is the quadratic difference operator of the parallelogram law. We characterize the functions $g$ in the image of $\mathsf{Q}$ and, under a summability hypothesis, recover a solution explicitly by an iteration on the diagonal followed by a propagation argument; neither regularity of $g$ nor divisibility of $G$ is required. As a consequence we obtain a sharp stability estimate of Forti--Găvruţa type for the quadratic functional equation.

Functional Analysis.title: Perturbed, suprametric, and interpolative contractions are metric contractions
Functional Analysis.summary: We show that the fixed point theory of perturbed metric spaces, b-suprametric spaces, and interpolative metric spaces reduces to the metric case. A mapping is a perturbed contraction with constant $λ$ if and only if it is a Banach contraction with constant $λ$ for a metric that dominates the exact metric. Thus the theorem of Jleli and Samet is the Banach contraction principle in a finer metric, and we show that this metric cannot be chosen equivalent to the exact one. We also show that the fixed point theorem claimed for perturbed Kannan mappings is false. A b-suprametric is a logarithmic transform of a b-metric with the same constant, and an interpolative metric is a power of a metric with an explicit exponent, which is optimal for $α= 1/2$. Consequently, contractive conditions of maximum type in these spaces are equivalent to the same conditions in b-metric and metric spaces.

Functional Analysis.title: Spectral isometries and invertibility preservers on Banach algebras
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between complex unital semisimple Banach algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the spectrum-preserving form of Kaplansky's conjecture. We also characterize surjective complex-linear maps between arbitrary unital Banach algebras that preserve invertibility in either direction, satisfy either spectral inclusion, or preserve the spectral radius. In particular, for a complex-linear bijection between semisimple Banach algebras, preservation of invertibility in either direction implies preservation in both directions, and either spectral inclusion implies equality of spectra, even without assuming unitality. As an application, we study preservers of the Fredholm essential spectrum and essential spectral radius.

Functional Analysis.title: Freeness conditions for intermediate $C^*$-algebras of crossed products
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $B$ be a separable $C^*$-algebra, let $Γ$ be a discrete countable group, let $α: Γ\to \text{Aut}(B)$ be an action, and let $A$ be an invariant subalgebra. We find certain freeness conditions which guarantee that any intermediate $C^*$-algebra $A \rtimes_{α,r} Γ\subseteq C \subseteq B \rtimes_{α,r} Γ$ is a crossed product of an intermediate invariant subalgebra $A \subseteq C_0 \subseteq B$ by $Γ$. Those are used to generalize related results by Suzuki.
Functional Analysis.comment: Final version. All the comments of the referees have been implemented. To appear in Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society. The title has been changed to reflect the paper

Functional Analysis.title: Polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces and the polyanalytic $q$-Bargmann transform
Functional Analysis.summary: We study polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces from an operator-theoretic point of view. We compute the formal adjoint $A^*$ of the Jackson derivative $A=\overline{R}_{q}$ on the polynomials in $z,\overline{z}$ inside $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ and we show that, up to unimodular factors, a twist by the grading operator is the only modification of $A$ diagonal in the grading for which a deformed canonical relation $aa^*-λa^*a=I$ holds. The resulting second-order $q$-difference operator $a^*a$ is essentially self-adjoint on the polynomials and $q$-complex Hermite polynomials span its eigenspaces. These eigenspaces give the orthogonal decomposition of $L^{2}(\mathbb{C},μ_{q})$ into true polyanalytic $q$-Fock spaces. We determine the disk on which each of them is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space and we factor the corresponding unitary $q$-Bargmann transforms through powers of $a^*$.

Functional Analysis.title: Regularity of the Semigroup of Regular Probability Measures on Locally Compact Hausdorff Topological Groups in which every element is of finite order
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group in which every element is of finite order, and let $P(\mathcal{G})$ denote the class of all regular probability measures on $\mathcal{G}$. In this note, it is observed that a characterization of algebraically regular elements in certain subsemigroups of $P(\mathcal{G})$ (Theorem~4.1 \cite{MNN}) for compact $\mathcal{G}$ remains true for locally compact $\mathcal{G}$. The results presented rely very much on Wendel's support theorem and the theory of doubly stochastic matrices (\cite{PLC} \cite{WEN}). A more general situation in which the assumption that every element is of finite order is not satisfied is also considered and illustrated with an example. This short article is a followup of \cite{MNN}.In addition,the random walk on an infinite discrete group associated with the generalised inverse of a probability measure is also studied.The last section is devoted to Fourier transform techniques to study the same problem using Bochner-type theorem in harmonic analysis.
Functional Analysis.comment: This article contains 13 pages, which is a revised version of the earlier one where the Fourier transform techniques was not included. The present one contains Fourier transform technique also and deals with more general groups as indicated in the abstract. This helps to deal with examples such as Johnson-type groups

Functional Analysis.title: Matrix-point interpolation for positive real odd functions in one and several variables
Functional Analysis.summary: We study the single matrix point interpolation problem for positive real matrix valued functions on the right half-plane, both in the single variable setting and in the noncommutative multivariable setting. In the single variable case, a careful analysis is done for when the solution may or must have a pole at infinity. In the multivariable setting, as the pole structure at infinity can be more complicated, we focus on the case when there is no pole at infinity. The results also yield numerical algorithms for finding a solution.

Functional Analysis.title: The rigidity phenomenon for weighted composition operators on the Fock spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We establish the rigidity of canonical sums of any finite number of weighted composition operators acting from a Fock space $\mathcal{F}^p$ into another $\mathcal{F}^q$ for all possible combinations of \(p,q\in (0, \infty]\). Specifically, we show that such a sum is bounded (compact, resp.) if and only if its summands are individually bounded (compact, resp.). In the case \(p\le q\), we present two independent approaches -- one analytic and one largely algebraic -- based on some common preliminary rigidity results. As a natural byproduct of our approach, we also obtain the Reproducing Kernel Thesis.

Functional Analysis.title: A Coarse-Geometric Interpretation of Holt's One-End Theorem
Functional Analysis.summary: Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element. Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, almost invariant color classes are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then show, via a separate argument for all slowly oscillating functions, that for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---Protasov's stronger conclusion holds: the full corona is a singleton.

Functional Analysis.title: Convex combinations of strict triangular norms
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that a pointwise convex combination of two strict triangular norms with positive weights is associative if and only if the two norms coincide. Together with the known ordinal-sum reduction and nilpotent case, the theorem yields the same conclusion for all continuous triangular norms and, in particular, for associative bivariate copulas. It also gives a corresponding result for representable uninorms with a common neutral element.

Functional Analysis.title: Composition operators on weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc
Functional Analysis.summary: We study composition operators between weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc induced by smooth symbols. We prove a general result of continuity which only involves the behaviour of the symbol on the polytorus. We deduce from this several consequences about the automatic continuity of the induced operator. We study in depth the case of the tridisc and exhibit several examples showing that a characterization of continuity using only derivatives seems impossible.

Functional Analysis.title: Power topologies and uniformities on bistochastic operators
Functional Analysis.summary: We prove that the set of invertible Koopman operators attached to the usual interval probability space is dense (and hence dense $G_δ$) in the space of bistochastic operators in the polynomial weak topology. This extends the non-polynomial analogue (due to Brown/Vershik/Ryzhikov/Eisner). We also show that the plain and polynomial weak topologies are distinct on bistochastic operators, confirming the distinction between the two results.

Functional Analysis.title: A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
Functional Analysis.summary: In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(Ω) \le \frac{π^{s-\frac{1}{2}}Γ\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)Γ\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partialΩ)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $Γ$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.
Functional Analysis.comment: The first version of this article was submitted to arXiv on July 21, 2026, and then it was on hold by arXiv till September 17, 2026. During the period when it was on hold, on August 13 we submitted a revised version to arXiv by adding an acknowledgement to AI

Functional Analysis.title: Twisted Verlinde formulas for cyclic orbifolds and the order-two simple current of a vertex operator superalgebra
Functional Analysis.summary:
Let $V=\Vev\oplus J$ be a simple vertex operator superalgebra with $\Vev$ simple, rational and $C_2$-cofinite, and let $G$ be a finite cyclic group acting faithfully on $\Vev$. For arbitrary twisted $V$-modules we prove: (1) for $G$ of arbitrary order, a twisted Verlinde formula for $\Vev$; (2) unitarity of the orbifold $S$-matrix block in generating sectors; (3) as a consequence, a formula for $N^{X_3}_{X_1,X_2}\pm N^{J\boxtimes X_3}_{X_1,X_2}$ as sums over $J$-orbits of $G$-stable untwisted modules, in which $J$-fixed points enter with weight two and in the minus sign, with a parity selection rule (read in $\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$) and a dimension sum rule; (4) simplicity of $V^G$. These results concern the $G$-graded fusion category of $\Vev$ together with the order two invertible object $J$ with $θ_J=-\dim_qJ$.
  The statements are tested numerically on six
  examples (odd and even orders up to $15$, both signs of $\dim_qJ$, $J$-fixed modules).

Functional Analysis.title: Optimal domains of Volterra-type operators on Bergman spaces
Functional Analysis.summary: We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_β$ to $A^p_α$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_β$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_β$. Moreover, $A^q_β \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_β$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_α]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_γ] \subset [T_{g},A^p_α]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

Functional Analysis.title: Optimal Beurling-Hörmander-type uncertainty principles and nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces
Functional Analysis.summary:
We study how rapidly a nonzero function $f \in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and its Fourier transform $\widehat{f}$ can simultaneously decay. For each suitable weight function $ω$, we construct a convex weight function $\varpi$ and establish the existence of a threshold $Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)} \in (0, \infty)$, where $\varpi^*$ denotes the convex conjugate of $\varpi$. For $a,b > 0$, the conditions \[
  \int_{-\infty}^\infty |f(x)| e^{ω(a|x|)} \, \mathrm{d}x < \infty
  \qquad \text{and} \qquad
  \int_{-\infty}^\infty |\widehat{f}(ξ)| e^{\varpi^*(b|ξ|)} \, \mathrm{d}ξ
  < \infty \] force $f = 0$ when $ab > Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$, whereas the functions satisfying both conditions form a dense subspace of $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ when $ab < Φ_{(ω,\varpi^*)}$. Similar results are also established in higher dimensions. We characterize the weights $ω$ for which $\varpi$ is equivalent to $ω$ and use this to determine when the Beurling-Hörmander uncertainty principle is optimal. A discrete form of the same construction yields a characterization of the nontriviality of Gelfand-Shilov spaces $\mathcal{S}^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and $Σ^{M}_{A}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ in terms of their defining weight sequences $M$ and $A$, under suitable regularity assumptions.

Functional Analysis.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
Functional Analysis.summary: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. A novelty of our method is building a connection between the $s$-principal submatrix problem and low-rank singular value perturbations. We also provide an algorithm to determine a positive definite matrix that realizes the given global and local symplectic spectra. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.
Functional Analysis.comment: A new section has been added. It provides an algorithm to construct the realizing matrix. The introduction has been revised to enhance the readability of the paper

Functional Analysis.title: A note on a recent result by Lorist, Meyries, and Veraar, or the counterexample which I missed
Functional Analysis.summary: Recently Lorist, Meyries, and Veraar showed, among others, that the inverse of an infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup on a Hilbert space need not to be an infinitesimal generator of a bounded semigroup. In this note we show that with the ingredients of that paper, the example can be constructed more directly. Furthermore, the author reflects on the reason why he did not construct this a decade ago.

Functional Analysis.title: Sharp box-dimension bounds for fractional integrals under unequal Hölder and anti-Hölder exponents
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $0<h\le H<1$ and $0<σ<1$. Graph box dimensions are studied for fractional integrals of functions satisfying an $h$-Holder upper bound on increments and an $H$-anti-H lder lower bound on oscillation on a nondegenerate subinterval. For the Riemann--Liouville integral, the following inequalities hold: \[ \begin{aligned} \max\{1,2-H-σH/h\} &\le\lbdim\G(I_{0+}^σf,[0,1])\\ &\le\ubdim\G(I_{0+}^σf,[0,1]) \le\max\{1,2-h-σ\}. \end{aligned} \] The lower bound is obtained by balancing the truncation error of a Marchaud inverse against the oscillation of the input. For each $(h,H)$, a single sparse tent construction attains it for all $σ\in(0,1)$. The same bounds and their optimality are established for Hadamard integrals on compact intervals bounded away from zero and for left- and right-sided Liouville--Weyl integrals under explicit weighted tail conditions. Zero-mean periodic Weyl integrals with conditionally convergent tails are treated separately. For Hadamard integrals the bounds are transferred by a bi-Lipschitz logarithmic change of variables. For Weyl integrals the transfer relies on invariance of graph box dimensions under continuous perturbations of bounded variation. Local hypotheses and point-dependent anti-Hölder constants are also treated. The exact linear dimension law is recovered for equal exponents, whereas unequal exponents allow a strictly greater loss of graph dimension.

Functional Analysis.title: Herz-type Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces with general weights
Functional Analysis.summary: In this paper, we introduce a new family of function spaces of generalized smoothness that encompasses the classical Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces, their weighted counterparts, as well as Herz-type Besov and Triebel-Lizorkin spaces. We provide a characterization of these spaces via the $\varphi$-transform in the sense of Frazier and Jawerth, and establish the corresponding Sobolev embeddings. Furthermore, we obtain smooth atomic and molecular decompositions for these spaces. Our approach relies on several new maximal inequalities.

Functional Analysis.title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
Functional Analysis.summary: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property. We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

Functional Analysis.title: Collineations of the diamond lattice in a Hilbert space
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ be non-trivial closed subspaces of a separable Hilbert space $\mathscr{H}$ such that $\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}=\{0\}$ and $\mathscr{M}+\mathscr{N}$ is dense in $\mathscr{H}$. We characterize when there exists an invertible operator on $\mathscr{H}$ which maps $\mathscr{M}$ onto $\mathscr{N}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ onto $\mathscr{M}$. We prove that such an operator exists if and only if $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ have a common algebraic complement. This happens if and only if either neither of the operators $(I-P)Q$ and $(I-Q)P$ is compact, or $P-Q$ is compact and $\dim(\mathscr{M}\cap\mathscr{N}^\perp)=\dim(\mathscr{M}^\perp\cap\mathscr{N})$, where $P$ and $Q$ are the orthogonal projections onto $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$. Moreover, the operator can be chosen to be an involution. Consequently, the group of collineations of the diamond lattice $\{\{0\},\mathscr{M},\mathscr{N},\mathscr{H}\}$ which fix $\mathscr{M}$ and $\mathscr{N}$ is always complemented in the group of all its collineations.

Functional Analysis.title: Operator generated topologies and the Krein property
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $X$ be a Banach space and $Z\subseteq X^*$ a subspace separating the points of $X$. We say that $Z$ has the Krein property if the $σ(X,Z)$-closed convex hull of every norm-bounded $σ(X,Z)$-compact set is $σ(X,Z)$-compact. We show that this property passes from $Z$ to every subspace between $Z$ and its sequential weak$^*$ closure in $X^*$, and that the closed convex hulls do not change. In particular, it passes to the smallest $V^*$-invariant space $Z[V]\supseteq Z$ whenever the operator $V$ is a pointwise $σ(X,Z)$-limit of a sequence of $σ(X,Z)$-continuous operators; for nets this fails in general and holds under a double limit condition. As a source of spaces with the Krein property we show that the Mackey topologies $μ(X,Z)$ and $μ(Z,X)$ are complete if the identity of $X$ is suitably approximated by a sequence of operators whose adjoints map $X^*$ into $Z$; in particular, $μ(E^\odot,E)$ and $μ(E,E^\odot)$ are complete for every $C_0$-semigroup on a Banach space $E$ with sun dual $E^\odot$. The results are applied to the history space $\mathrm{BUC}(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ of delay equations with infinite delay, where every space of bounded measures containing $L^1(\mathbb{R}_{-})$ has the Krein property.

Functional Analysis.title: Unbounded Gaps Between Matrix Monotonicity and Frobenius Radial Convexity
Functional Analysis.summary: We show that the gap between matrix monotonicity and Frobenius radial convexity can be arbitrarily large. For every integer $m\ge 2$, we construct rational functions that are matrix monotone of order $m$ but not of order $m+1$, and Frobenius radially convex of order $2m-1$ but not of order $2m$. Thus, the difference between their exact matrix-monotonicity and radial-convexity orders is $m-1$, which can be arbitrarily large. As a consequence, for every $n\ge 3$, Frobenius radial convexity of order $n$ does not imply matrix monotonicity of the same order, either increasing or decreasing.

Functional Analysis.title: The Order of the Non-universal Tree of a Hilbert Space with Respect to the Haar Basis
Functional Analysis.summary: In his 1994 doctoral thesis, Bossard introduced the notion of the non-universal tree $T_{NU}(X)$ associated with each separable Banach space $X$ which does not contain an isomorphic copy of $C(2^\mathbb{N})$. Together with the order operation defined on well-founded trees, we obtain a method of classifying the complexity of separable Banach spaces by the degree of isomorphism of finite-dimensional subspaces of $C(2^\mathbb{N})$. Despite further refinement of this concept in later years, we are unaware of any specific instances of direct exhibitions of the order of the non-universal tree for a concrete space and basis. We show that if $H$ is any separable Hilbert space, then $o(T_{NU}(H)) = ω + 1$ when taken with respect to the Haar basis for $C(2^\mathbb{N})$, demonstrating that the class of Hilbert spaces is the least complex class with respect to this measurement when considering this basis.

Functional Analysis.title: Characterizations and Algebraic, Perturbation, and Topological Properties of $θ(H)$
Functional Analysis.summary: Let $H$ be a separable complex Hilbert space, and let $θ(H)$ be the class of bounded operators whose restrictions to every nonzero closed reducing subspace attain their numerical radii. We characterize this property by eigenvalues of suitable self-adjoint parts. For normal operators, membership in $θ(H)$ is equivalent to pure point spectrum and reverse well-ordering of the moduli of eigenvalues. Without normality assumptions, we prove stability under finite orthogonal direct sums using graph subspaces of closed, possibly unbounded, intertwining operators. We give a compact-perturbation criterion in terms of the essential numerical radius and show that an operator remains in $θ(H)$ under every compact perturbation if and only if it is compact. Finally, $θ(H)$ is norm-dense in $\mathcal B(H)$ and is norm closed if and only if $H$ is finite-dimensional.

Functional Analysis.title: Complemented Copies of $c_{0}$ in Positive Tensor Products of Banach Lattices
Functional Analysis.summary: A result of Cembranos states that a non-trivial injective tensor product of a $C$-space contains a complemented copy of $c_{0}$, and in particular fails the Grothendieck property. We establish a positive analogue of the Cembranos theorem for tensor products of Banach lattices. If $E$ and $F$ are infinite dimensional Banach lattices, one of which contains a copy of $c_{0}$, then the Wittstock tensor product $E\widetilde{\otimes}_{\vert{\varepsilon}\vert}F$ contains a complemented copy of $c_{0}$. If $F$ is in addition reflexive, then $E\widetilde{\otimes}_{\vert{\varepsilon}\vert}F$ fails the positive Grothendieck property.

Functional Analysis.title: Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, II. Operator-Theoretic Tools
Functional Analysis.summary: This is the second part of a two-part work on semiclassical Weyl laws and Connes' integration formulas for spectral triples. It establishes three operator-theoretic results, which are used in Part I but are of independent interest. The first is a factorization formula for the fractional commutators $[|D|^{-α},a]$, which is obtained by means of double operator integrals. The second is an enhancement, for arbitrary unital spectral triples, of a lemma of Connes-Sukochev-Zanin on the differences $(a^{1/2}|D|^{-α}a^{1/2})^s-|D|^{-αs}a^s$, together with a holomorphic version of it. The third is a Tauberian theorem showing that zeta function and heat trace conditions of the type sought by Connes imply Weyl laws for the operators $aD^2a$, where $a$ ranges over positive invertible elements of the algebra. Along the way, we obtain a version for spectral triples of the Tauberian theorem of McDonald-Sukochev-Zanin without any extra regularity assumption or restriction on the degree of summability. This paper can be read largely independently of Part I.
